full_text:
News Corp has reported a slight slide in digital subscriptions at its Australian mastheads, erasing recent gains, among otherwise robust financials at the Rupert Murdoch-backed global conglomerate.
Digital subscribers at News Corp Australia – a division that includes the Australian, the Daily Telegraph and the Herald Sun, among others – fell from 1,166,000 to 1,162,000 during the financial year, according to the company’s internal data published in its full year results on Thursday morning.
The figures represent a reversal in momentum. The Australian division has grown digital subscriptions in recent years, as it transitions away from its traditional newspaper base.
News Corp’s broader news media unit, which includes the Sun and the Times in London and the New York Post, recorded mixed results, with advertising revenue still under pressure, falling 2% during the year to 30 June.
The news media division also recorded costs linked to the launch of News Corp’s latest newspaper, the California Post, which is the Los Angeles outpost of the New York Post and edited by Australian News Corp veteran Nick Papps.
The News Corp chief executive, Robert Thomson, used the release of the company’s financial results to hit out at AI models that “pilfer and profit from our work”, as media companies around the world seek compensation for the use of their content.
“Without our journalists, our authors, our data, our brands and our professional expertise, users would be drowning in a slimy sea of AI slop,” Thomson said.
“We will pursue those pilferers and companies that are clients of these crass kleptomaniacs should know they are patently in possession of stolen goods.”
News Corp has commercial agreements in place with OpenAI and Meta.
The comments come amid contested plans by the Albanese government to expand its news bargaining incentive, which would require tech giants to compensate media outlets for the news on their platforms, either through making commercial deals or paying a higher levy.

title: Nato to ‘urgently’ get air defences for Ukraine, as Zelenskyy warns of surge in Russian missile production
summary:
After Ukraine failed to shoot down a single ballistic missile fired by Russia on Wednesday, the president urged allies to increase supplies of Patriot interceptors

Nato is working to get Ukraine the air defences it “urgently needs”, its secretary general has said, after Kyiv failed to shoot down a single Russian missile in an attack on Wednesday, and as Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was seeking to significantly boost missile ⁠production ahead of winter.

Speaking at a National Security and Defense Council meeting on winter resilience, the Ukrainian president did not rule out the idea that stalling missile supplies from western allies were “aimed at making Ukraine, so to speak, more willing to compromise” in peace talks with Russia.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Nato is working to get Ukraine the air defences it “urgently needs”, its secretary general has said, after Kyiv failed to shoot down a single Russian missile in an attack on Wednesday, and as Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was seeking to significantly boost missile production ahead of winter.
Speaking at a National Security and Defense Council meeting on winter resilience, the Ukrainian president did not rule out the idea that stalling missile supplies from western allies were “aimed at making Ukraine, so to speak, more willing to compromise” in peace talks with Russia.
After meeting Nato’s Mark Rutte, Zelenskyy said: “It is important to cut through all red tape and make the necessary political decisions. Literally every day, people’s lives here in Ukraine depend on the resolve of our partners in Europe and the United States.”
Russia launched 24 ballistic missiles in an overnight attack on Wednesday, killing at least 17 people. Preliminary data from the Ukrainian air force showed its defences shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, but none of the ballistic missiles.
On Wednesday, Zelenskyy said that in the first half of 2026, supplies of air defence missiles from Ukraine’s allies had fallen to a third of their 2025 level.
The president also warned that Moscow was looking to significantly increase ballistic missile production as winter neared, when it is expected to renew its campaign against Ukraine’s energy sector.
Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukraine’s president on the development of defence technology, estimated that Russia was capable of launching 100 ballistic missiles every month to attack logistic hubs, industrial facilities, food stores and warehouses. “The war of attrition has entered its next phase,” he said on the Telegram app.
Ukraine has been short on US-made Patriot interceptors capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles since the start of the war. But in recent weeks, an acute shortage has come into focus, with Moscow pummelling Kyiv, on average, every three days in July alone. Zelenskyy said the shortage of interceptor missiles was mainly caused by the war in the Middle East.
Patriot missile systems are the only system in Ukrainian service able to intercept the Russian Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles, according to the Ukrainian air force.
Russia often combines ballistic missiles with cruise missiles, drones and decoys, forcing defenders to track many threats and ration scarce interceptors, but Ukraine says it has too few batteries and interceptors to properly protect itself.
The interceptor shortage has become more acute as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has consumed large numbers of Patriot and other interceptors. An analysis by the Associated Press estimated that the US Patriot inventory had fallen by at least 65% since before the war. The Pentagon claims it retains a deep arsenal of supplies.
Production cannot immediately close the gap. Lockheed Martin delivered more than 600 of the newest model of interceptors in 2025 and is working toward annual capacity of 2,000 by the end of 2030. But according to some estimates, Gulf states collectively fired more than 1,100 interceptors in the first three months of the Iran war.
Nato says Europe’s first Patriot missile production facility is expected to open in September in Germany.
Political signals from Washington have also shifted. At a Nato summit last month, Donald Trump said the US would give Ukraine a licence to produce Patriots. About three weeks later, he said he had not made a final decision. Even with a licence, officials and experts estimate that starting production in Ukraine would take years.
Despite Trump casting doubt on the deal last month, the US is pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot interceptors, according to reports from Reuters.
The discussions include an option for Ukraine to build some components for final assembly elsewhere in Europe, according to the report.

title: Elon Musk’s attempt at an AI Wikipedia hasn’t been updated in months
summary: xAI's Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia with AI-generated articles that Elon Musk once promised would be a "massive improvement" over Wikipedia, apparently hasn't been updated since April 24th, according to a report from Lawfare. "As far as we can tell, no entry has changed in more than three months," Lawfare said. Grokipedia launched in v0.1 in […]
full_text:
xAI’s Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia with AI-generated articles that Elon Musk once promised would be a “massive improvement” over Wikipedia, apparently hasn’t been updated since April 24th, according to a report from Lawfare. “As far as we can tell, no entry has changed in more than three months,” Lawfare said.
Elon Musk’s attempt at an AI Wikipedia hasn’t been updated in months
Suggested Grokipedia edits haven’t been addressed since April, according to a report.
Grokipedia launched in v0.1 in October 2025 with an initial batch of 885,000 articles, and is now on v0.2 (released in November 2025) and has more than 6,000,000 total articles, according to grokipedia.com/live. But that live page also has a section titled “Recent changes to…” with a message under it that reads “No live edits available right now.”
You can still suggest articles for Grokipedia to cover and edits to individual pages. But Lawfare looked at both popular and unpopular pages on Grokipedia and found that they weren’t updating. “In our subsequent analysis of 34,519 pages with at least one suggested edit in our sample, containing a total of 225,496 recommended edits, we found no accepted or rejected corrections dated within the past three months,” Lawfare said.
xAI didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. Users on Reddit and X have wondered if Grokipedia is “dead.” Lawfare also noted that Musk’s last X post mentioning Grokipedia was from February.

title: Bitcoin steadies above $64,000 as traders watch $100 billion SpaceX unlock
full_text:
Bitcoin steadies above $64,000 as traders watch $100 billion SpaceX unlock
Korea's Kospi fell 4.4% as the AI trade wobbled, and $101 billion of SpaceX stock becomes tradable Thursday.
- Bitcoin held above $64,600 after buyers defended a dip earlier in the week, with optimism focused more on the token than on the broader crypto market.
- Major cryptocurrencies were mixed, with ether slightly higher, XRP and BNB weaker, and Hyperliquid’s HYPE posting the strongest weekly gain among large tokens.
- Global risk sentiment softened as a key world equity index slipped and chipmakers fell, even as gold climbed on reduced rate-hike expectations and traders awaited SoftBank results as a barometer of private AI investment.
Bitcoin held above $64,600 on Thursday, up marginally on the day and 0.5% on the week, while the rest of the majors offered little in the way of direction.
Attention is also on Elon Musk-owned SpaceX, where roughly $101 billion of stock becomes tradable Thursday as the first lockup expires. The company holds 18,712 BTC, worth about $1.1 billion at the end of June.
Ether rose over 1% to $1,904 but remains down 0.7% over seven days. XRP was the weakest of the group, falling almost 3% to $1.04 and 3% on the week. BNB slipped over 1% to $595 though it still leads the majors over seven days at 3.5%.
Solana fell almost 1% to nearly $74 and dogecoin the same to 7 cents. Tron was flat at 33 cents. Hyperliquid's HYPE was little changed at $56 and is up over 4% on the week, the best weekly performance among the majors.
Alex Kuptsikevich of FxPro said in an email that bitcoin has gained momentum since Monday, when buyers stepped in during the dip toward $62,500 and pushed price back above the 50-day moving average. Optimism is centred more on bitcoin than on the wider market, he said, which is typical of the early stages of a long-term shift.
The equity backdrop turned less helpful. The MSCI All Country World Index snapped a five-day run to fall 0.2% as chipmakers retreated on both sides of the Pacific. Korea's Kospi, a bellwether for the AI trade, dropped 4.4% with SK Hynix and Samsung leading losses.
S&P 500 and European futures edged higher.
Meanwhile, Gold rose 0.4% to its strongest since June as traders trimmed rate-hike expectations, with Brent under $80 a barrel after Iran said it had reached an agreement with Oman on a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
SoftBank reports later Thursday. It has put $34.6 billion into OpenAI through Vision Fund 2 since September 2024 and owns chip designer Arm, so its numbers are read as a gauge of whether the private side of the AI trade is holding up.

title: XRP whales keep buying the dip, but ether shows deeper capitulation
full_text:
XRP whales keep buying the dip, but ether shows deeper capitulation
CryptoQuant said large XRP spot orders point to "quiet accumulation" rather than a breakout, while ether’s price below realized value leaves holders underwater and gives it the strongest valuation case among BTC, ETH and XRP.
- Large XRP holders have continued accumulating the token throughout its slide from about $2.40 in January to roughly $1.00 to $1.20, a pattern CryptoQuant describes as quiet absorption rather than capitulation or a breakout.
- Ether is the only major token trading below its realized price, with the market around $1,900 versus an aggregate holder cost basis near $2,450, suggesting investors are underwater on paper even as Bitcoin and XRP trade above their realized prices.
- Onchain data show Ether and Bitcoin whales have been adding to holdings during the downturn, but CryptoQuant warns the market may still face one more leg lower before a durable floor is established, with Ether’s below-cost trading seen as the key metric to watch.
Large XRP holders have kept buying through the token's slide from about $2.40 in January to the current $1.00 to $1.20 range, but they are doing it without lifting the market.
Data from onchain analysis firm CryptoQuant shows average spot order sizes have stayed in what the firm classifies as “big-whale” territory throughout 2026. At the same time, 90-day taker cumulative volume delta, which measures whether buyers or sellers are the aggressors in a trade, has drifted to neutral after a taker-buy-dominant start to the year.
Whales are a colloquial term for large holders of a token, whose buying and selling is watched closely because it tends to lead the wider market rather than follow it.
The firm calls this a quiet absorption and a basing range rather than capitulation or a confirmed breakout.
Ether is where the valuation case is strongest. It trades around $1,900 as of Thursday against a realized price near $2,450, meaning the aggregate cost basis of all coins sits above the current price and holders are underwater on paper. Bitcoin, by contrast, is roughly 17% above its $52,900 realized price, and XRP sits near $1.10 against about $0.75.
Ether's holder base is splitting, however. Wallets holding 10,000 to 100,000 ETH have risen from about 14 million ETH in mid-2025 to record highs near 19.6 million now.
The 100,000-plus cohort fell to roughly 2.6 million ETH in mid-2025 before climbing to about 4.6 million by May 2026, an addition CryptoQuant put at roughly 1.8 million. The 1,000 to 10,000 cohort has gone the other way, peaking near 15.6 million ETH in January 2026 and falling to about 12.9 million since.
Bitcoin whales, excluding exchange and mining-pool addresses, bottomed near 2.87 million BTC in December 2025 and hold about 3.06 million now, buying hardest as price fell below $60,000 in June. That remains roughly 170,000 BTC below the 2025 bull-cycle peak near 3.23 million.
CryptoQuant calls this the last stage of the decline while stating plainly that valuation leaves room for one more leg lower before a floor is confirmed.
Ether below cost basis is the thing to watch. It is the only one of the three where the market has already capitulated on paper, and CryptoQuant noted ETH bottomed in early 2025 at a similar level and a similar distance from its lower band.

title: CASHCAT jumps 120% in a week as Robinhood Chain hits $774 million of value locked
full_text:
CASHCAT jumps 120% in a week as Robinhood Chain hits $774 million of value locked
The memecoin that defined the chain's debut has recovered to an $86 million cap. Tokenized assets, the chain's stated purpose, sit at $27.6 million.
- CASHCAT, a cat-themed memecoin on Robinhood Chain, more than doubled in a week to about 8.7 cents. It remains well below its mid-July peak of roughly 22 cents.
- Even as launchpad activity and many early tokens have faded, Robinhood Chain’s total value locked has climbed to about $774 million and tokenized real-world assets to $100 million, with CASHCAT alone worth roughly 85% of those assets’ value.
- The token is still the deepest/most liquid memecoin pool on the chain.
The cat-themed token that dominated Robinhood Chain's first trading days is up 120% over the past week, recovering part of the slide that followed July's launch frenzy, even as the wave of tokens it launched alongside has thinned out.
CASHCAT trades near 8.7 cents, up 22% in the past 24 hours, with a market cap around $86 million on $9 million of daily volume. However, that is still well short of the roughly 22 cents it reached in mid-July.
The memecoin was built by outsiders around the cat-with-cash logo the company used before it rebranded, and its own website calls it "fan fiction with a ticker." It became the first breakout hit on the chain within a week of the July 1 mainnet launch, minting seven-figure returns for a handful of early wallets and prompting Robinhood Markets CEO Vlad Tenev, who had called assets without utility a dead end days earlier, to post that the chain "works great for memes too."
But most of what launched beside it is gone. Noxa, the launchpad behind July's wave, stopped accepting launches on July 11 and went dark two days later, having earned an estimated $12 million in fees.
Token deployments across the chain's launchpads have fallen from roughly 35,000 per day in mid-July to about 10,000, according to data. Noxa still holds around $137,000 of CASHCAT and has not sold; its balance has been flat over the past week while the value has risen 75%.
CASHCAT's own distribution has broadened. DEXTools data shows the token has about 41,200 holders, the full 989 million supply is circulating with no locked allocation, and the largest single holder is the Uniswap pool providing its liquidity, at 2.47%.
The biggest wallets below that hold between 1.3% and 1.5% each. That pool holds $5 million, down from the $6.6 million backing a $105 million valuation in July, but still deeper than any other memecoin pool on the chain.
Deposits kept climbing through it all. Total value locked stands at $774 million, up 20% over seven days, with lending at 43% and asset management 41.5%. Two protocols hold nearly three-quarters of it: Morpho, at $332 million, is the lending market behind Robinhood's own onchain earn product. Ethena, with $236 million in assets, issues a dollar-pegged token that pays holders a yield. Stablecoins on the chain total $575 million, up 14% from the week prior.
The tokenized real-world assets Robinhood built the chain to host now carry an active market value of $100 million, up from about $70 million in late July, when a dozen tokenized stocks were each clearing more than $500,000 a day, and GameStop's alone did $26 million.
Robinhood is covering gas fees through roughly late September. The first real read on whether any of this sticks comes after that, when users start paying to transact.

title: Here are the possible outcomes for Clarity right now
full_text:
Here are the possible outcomes for Clarity right now
The Senate has not yet indicated if it will advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, and with its summer recess looming, here are the possible outcomes.
The fate of the crypto market structure legislation is in a precarious place as the clock ticks down to the Senate's summer recess.
The U.S. Senate has not yet indicated whether it will work on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, with just two days left in session, and there is no official word on whether or when the legislative body might vote on the bill.
It's possible the Senate can take up the measure after it returns to Washington, D.C. in September, but there are limited working days before the Senate breaks again for the final stretch of the 2026 midterm campaign. It's possible the Senate will stay past its scheduled session end date of August 7 and work through next week, theoretically giving it time to hold a procedural vote on Clarity, if not run through the whole process to get the bill to the House of Representatives. It's also just as possible that the window has closed for Clarity in 2026.
At this point, the fate of the Clarity Act is up to a number of factors, both tied to the bill itself and as part of the Senate's broader work.
Some details of the Clarity Act itself are still being negotiated. Provisions addressing illicit finance and agriculture issues are still under discussion, a legislative staffer told CoinDesk on Wednesday, not to mention the ethics provision aiming to block senior government officials like President Donald Trump from profiting off of the crypto industry.
The White House is still pondering a proposal on ethics language from Senators Thom Tillis and Ruben Gallego, which the senators sent to the White House last week. If the White House accepts the proposal, or has feedback on it, that could move the needle for Democrats on the vote.
Tillis told reporters on Wednesday that the White House had begun to engage with the proposal, Punchbowl News' Brendan Pedersen reported.
Outside of the Clarity Act, the Senate is currently grappling with the nomination of Todd Blanche to become the next Attorney General, a continuing resolution to fund the federal government, a Russia sanctions bill and possibly a college sports bill.
Possible futures
If the Senate does leave town on Friday, then Wednesday night is essentially the final moment where Majority Leader John Thune can file for cloture, given that the Senate needs to let the motion ripen for a full day before it can take a first procedural vote. However, Thune can also announce that the Senate will continue working into the weekend or until next week on Thursday, which would give the Senate more time for Clarity.
In other words, no news on cloture on Wednesday night might just be no news.
In one scenario, Majority Leader John Thune files cloture on Wednesday night, gets through all of the Senate's other priorities by Friday, holds the first procedural vote on Friday night and then everyone goes back to their districts to meet their constituents and campaign for reelection.
In another, the Senate can break on Friday, Aug. 7, without taking any further steps on the Clarity Act.
In that scenario, the Senate could still return in September and take up the Clarity Act once more. The Senate will also have to deal with funding the government and other issues at that time, and there are just 14 working days when the Senate is in session in September and October. This means it would likely be difficult to get the Clarity Act through, short of Senators agreeing to push it through. It's certainly possible it can get through Clarity in that time period, however.
The legislative staffer told CoinDesk that if the outstanding issues are sorted through, the bill would easily have a chance at passage in September.
Alternatively, the Senate could extend its working session through the weekend or into next week to address outstanding issues, which may give it enough time to at least get a first procedural vote on Clarity.
It is increasingly looking like the Senate will stay for a few more days, given that Todd Blanche's nomination is still pending.
This would require Majority Leader Thune to notice a motion to proceed, wait a full day and then secure 60 votes on the second day after he notices the motion. Thune did file cloture on the college sports bill spearheaded by Senator Ted Cruz, but he has not yet invoked cloture on it, meaning he could still file cloture on Clarity with enough time to move through a vote, an industry source said.
If this vote succeeds, the Senate will break, but will be back in September, with a very excited crypto industry hoping for relatively smooth passage on the final set of votes.
If this vote fails, Clarity probably won't go anywhere until after the election. That comes with its own set of possible outcomes, depending on whether the House or Senate flips and what the margins for each party are.

title: ElizaOS token sinks 19% to record low after founder declares it ‘dead’
summary: Eliza Labs founder Shaw Walters said the project transferred its remaining treasury to settle a tokenholder lawsuit and will continue building Eliza without an associated cryptocurrency.
full_text:
ElizaOS token sinks 19% to record low after founder declares it ‘dead’
Eliza Labs founder Shaw Walters said the project transferred its remaining treasury to settle a tokenholder lawsuit and will continue building Eliza without an associated cryptocurrency.
ElizaOS fell 19% over 24 hours to an all-time low after Eliza Labs founder Shaw Walters said the token was “dead” and that the Eliza Foundation was winding down.
CoinGecko data showed the token trading at $0.000285 at the time of writing after touching a record low of $0.000284 on Thursday with a market capitalization of $2.1 million.
The drop came after an announcement from Walters that the foundation was winding down. “The token is dead. Completely,” Walters said, adding that he no longer owned or supported the token. He said the development of the open-source Eliza software would continue without the token or the foundation.
The decline represents a stark reversal for one of the AI-agent sector’s former breakout tokens. Before the project rebranded as ElizaOS, the token, then known as AI16Z, reached a peak market capitalization of $2.5 billion in January 2025, according to CoinGecko.
ElizaOS’ 24-hour price chart. Source: CoinGecko
Founder blames lawsuit and token culture
Walters said Eliza Labs privately settled with a group of tokenholders represented by Burwick Law by agreeing to give them its remaining treasury and funds.
He called the suit “ridiculous” but said the project lacked the capital to continue fighting it.
The lawsuit, filed in April, named Eliza Labs, Walters, Sebastian Quinn-Watson and the AI16Z DAO as defendants. It alleged false advertising, deceptive practices, negligent misrepresentation and unjust enrichment.
Court records show the named plaintiff’s claims were dismissed with prejudice by stipulation on July 8, while the proposed class’s claims were dismissed without prejudice.
Cointelegraph contacted Walters and Burwick Law founder Max Burwick for comment but had not received a response by the time of publication.
Related: Not every AI agent needs its own cryptocurrency: CZ
Walters said there were no more funds for token buybacks and no foundation or future supply intervention to support the token.
He also said he would not allow another token to be associated with Eliza while continuing to build its underlying operating system.
“I am starting over, since I own the IP, and I am never letting a token come close to Eliza again [...] I’m never going to support an Eliza token,” he wrote.
ElizaOS is an open-source framework for building and managing AI agents. The project launched in October 2024 as ai16z with an initial goal of raising $75,000 to build an autonomous investor.
In January 2025, it rebranded to ElizaOS after Andreessen Horowitz raised concerns about confusion with its a16z brand. The token was also later migrated.

title: Meta latest AI firm to see model go rogue during testing
summary: The incident reportedly stemmed from a misconfigured testing environment, adding Meta to a growing list of AI firms whose models have escaped evaluation sandboxes.
full_text:
Meta latest AI firm to see model go rogue during testing
The incident reportedly stemmed from a misconfigured testing environment, adding Meta to a growing list of AI firms whose models have escaped evaluation sandboxes.
Meta has become the latest major AI company to disclose that one of its models hacked another company’s systems during testing, following similar incidents involving Anthropic and OpenAI.
The model involved Meta’s Muse Spark 1.1, which launched in July, according to The Information, citing sources. The issue reportedly stemmed from a misconfiguration by Irregular, an artificial intelligence security testing and red-teaming firm, which inadvertently gave the model internet access during an evaluation.
The model “exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service, in a manner similar to previously reported instances with other companies,” Meta told Reuters in a statement.
The incident is the latest case of an advanced AI agent becoming a cybersecurity risk in its own right, and also has raised questions about where the liability lies — the companies that develop the agents, or the ones that design the sandboxes meant to contain them.
Related: Mysten Labs tech chief joins Anthropic to work on AI security
Meta’s AI breach comes just a week after Anthropic said its models got access to the internet to hack an external company, due to a configuration error relating to the Irregular’s testing environment.
In a blog post on July 30, Anthropic said it found three incidents (out of 141,006 evaluation runs) in which a Claude model reached the internet during an evaluation, before gaining unauthorized access to the systems within three different organizations.
All three incidents happened within or while interacting with the evaluation environment of Irregular, and involved a misconfiguration that left machines that Claude accessed with live internet access.
Cointelegraph reached out to Meta and Irregular for comment.
In July, AI agents developed by OpenAI broke out of their offline sandbox to hack Hugging Face in order to cheat on a security benchmark test in July.
Charles Guillemet, chief technology officer of Ledger, said the latest incident was “marketing theatre.”
“Having a model ‘go rogue’ has become the latest AI PR stunt,” he said on Wednesday.
“If your model isn’t escaping sandboxes, ‘hacking’ companies, or pulling off some headline-grabbing exploit, apparently you’re falling behind... The industry doesn’t need bigger stunts, it needs more trust.”

title: 比特幣 Red Team 挖出近 5000 個漏洞，Coldcard 被駭後生態大震動
summary:
Coldcard 硬體錢包被駭、逾 1 億美元比特幣遭竊後，由 16 名志願者組成的 Bitcoin Red […]

〈比特幣 Red Team 挖出近 5000 個漏洞，Coldcard 被駭後生態大震動〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Coldcard 硬體錢包被駭、逾 1 億美元比特幣遭竊後，由 16 名志願者組成的 Bitcoin Red Team 啟動 AI 輔助大規模安全審查，29.8 小時內在 390 個比特幣專案中找到近 5000 個潛在漏洞，其中 720 個為高危及嚴重級別。
（前情提要：Coldcard MK3 冷錢包爆「種子漏洞」：594 枚比特幣 25 分鐘掃空，官方籲使用者盡速遷移資產）
（背景補充：Boltz 暫停比特幣兌換服務：AI 駭客探測漏洞速度已超過人類開發）
比特幣生態正經歷一波安全震盪。Coldcard 硬體錢包遭駭、逾 1 億美元比特幣被盜後，一支由 16 名志願者組成的資安團隊 Bitcoin Red Team 啟動 AI 輔助的大規模安全審查，在不到 30 小時內掃出近 5000 個潛在漏洞。
Bitcoin Red Team 成員包括 AnchorWatch CEO Rob Hamilton、比特幣核心開發者 Calle 等人，他們結合 AI 工具與人工審查，針對開源的比特幣相關程式庫進行漏洞掃描。
29.8 小時、390 個專案、4962 個潛在問題
根據 Calle 在 X 上公布的資料，在行動啟動後的前 29.8 小時內：
- 掃描 390 個比特幣生態專案
- 發現 4,962 個潛在問題
- 其中 720 個被判定為高危及嚴重級別
- 目前 21.4% 的發現已可復現驗證
Calle 在週三表示：「每人平均每小時約發現 1 個嚴重漏洞利用。」他同時指出，「生態系現在很混亂，我們完全理解很多人同時被大量安全問題淹沒。」
Coldcard 事件：比特幣硬體錢包的信任危機
Bitcoin Red Team 的審查行動，是在 Coldcard 硬體錢包被駭後數天內啟動的。根據 動區先前報導，Galaxy Research 指出 Coldcard MK3 的種子漏洞至少遭 15 名攻擊者利用，損失超過 1,082 枚比特幣（約 7,000 萬至 8,660 萬美元），受害地址達 4,585 個。
這起事件引發整個比特幣社群對硬體錢包安全性的質疑，過去被視為「最安全儲存方式」的冷錢包，如今也被證明並非銅牆鐵壁。
AI 加持：漏洞挖掘速度的雙面刃
Bitcoin Red Team 大量使用 AI 工具輔助掃描，這既是防禦的利器，也反映了一個更嚴峻的現實：攻擊者同樣在用 AI 加速漏洞探測。
就在幾天前，去中心化交易所 Boltz 因 AI 駭客的漏洞探測速度超過人類開發團隊而被迫暫停比特幣兌換服務。這顯示：在 AI 驅動的攻防戰中，防禦者必須用 AI 對抗 AI，否則根本來不及修補。

由Indonesia Crypto Network（ICN）主辦的世界級加密貨幣盛會Coinfest Asia，將於2026 年 8 月 20 日至 21 日重返印尼峇里島 Melasti 海灘，匯聚機構、開發者、交易者、創辦人、投資人、開發團隊及全球 Web3 社群，共聚亞洲最具活力的加密貨幣聚會。

與會者在 Coinfest Asia 可以參與的活動
2026 年度的活動跳脫傳統會議形式，將內容劃分為三大主題軌道，旨在協助與會者依產業功能領域找到最相關的議程：
- 機構軌道（Institutional Track）
聚焦於數位資產採用、穩定幣整合與代幣化，為監管機構、金融機構、企業與產業領袖提供一系列活動，包括亞洲市場進入策略座談（Asia Go-To-Market Sessions）、主題演講、座談討論，以及由 ICEX 集團（包含 Indonesia Crypto Exchange（ICEX）、Crypto Asset Clearing International（CACI）與 International Crypto Custodian（ICC））主辦的機構峰會中的閉門穩定幣與代幣化圓桌會議。
- 開發者軌道（Builders Track）
面向 AI、區塊鏈與數位基礎設施領域的開發者與新創團隊，活動包括 Gemini AI 大師課程、「What the Hack!」Web3 開發者課程、AI Vibe 程式設計競賽、亞洲市場進入策略座談，以及聚焦產品開發與生態成長的專題會議。
- 交易者軌道（Traders Track）
專為活躍交易者與市場參與者設計，協助他們掌握市場敘事、精進交易策略並與交易社群連結。活動包括 MEXC Ventures 主辦的全球交易競賽 Alpha Arena 總決賽、Alpha Hunting 大師課程、Yapper 大師課程、比特幣速成課、Live Degen Experience，以及交易主題座談與主題演講。
透過這些主題軌道，Coinfest Asia 旨在讓盛會更容易探索，同時保持開放性，並連結更廣泛的加密產業。
開啟亞洲 Web3 市場大門
2026 年活動的核心目標之一，是提供亞洲市場的在地化洞察。活動推出「亞洲市場進入策略座談」（Asia Go-To-Market Sessions），針對特定司法管轄區的法規環境、用戶行為與成長渠道提供深度解析。
這些座談與區域生態系夥伴合作舉辦：
- 日本市場進入策略座談（與 WebX 2026 合作）
- 馬來西亞市場進入策略座談（與 MYBW 2026 合作）
- 印尼市場進入策略座談（與 Indonesia Crypto Network 合作）
- 印度市場進入策略座談（與 India Blockchain Week 2026 合作）
透過這些座談，與會者能更深入了解亞洲各地的本地用戶行為、監管方向、社群動態、合作機會與通路策略。
Coinfest Asia 活動主管 Joditha Winatajaya 表示：
亞洲並非單一市場。每個國家都有各自的用戶、法規、文化與成長渠道。透過亞洲市場進入策略座談，我們希望在同一地點為與會者連結正確的在地生態系統。
建構於產業領導地位之上
Coinfest Asia 2026 的講者陣容涵蓋區塊鏈基礎設施、交易所、錢包、穩定幣、支付、數據、AI、機構金融、創投以及 Web3 社群等領域。
已確認的講者包括 Input Output Group 創辦人 Charles Hoskinson、Trust Wallet 執行長 Felix Fan、Nansen 執行長 Alexander Svanevik、Base 亞太暨新加坡負責人 Nick See Tong、Google Web3 與 AI 策略合作主管 Iñaki Moreno、INDODAX 執行長 William Sutanto、Tether 泰國暨印度支那區域經理 Ploy Boonyavee、TRIV Group 執行長 Gabriel Rey、Tokocrypto 執行長 Calvin Kizana、BitGo 亞太區董事總經理暨新加坡總裁 Angela Ang、StraitsX 執行長 Tianwei Liu、Canton Foundation 亞太區主管 Thomas Chou、Maelstrom 共同創辦人 Akshat Vaidya，以及其他多位講者。
本次活動亦獲得來自加密貨幣、金融科技、數位資產與基礎設施領域的領導企業支持，包括 ICEX（Indonesia Crypto Exchange）、Crypto Asset Clearing International（CACI）、International Crypto Custodian（ICC）、Indodax、MEXC Ventures、Triv、Tokocrypto、Binance、Duitku、ClickHouse、CockroachDB、BYDFi、Zoomex、FundedXyz、WalletConnect、GOIDR、GudangKripto 等，更多合作夥伴將陸續公布。
自創辦以來，Coinfest Asia 已發展為全球領先的加密貨幣盛會之一，在峇里島匯聚國際企業、在地生態系統、開發者、交易者、機構與社群。
2026 年活動延續這股動能，將產業議程與節慶式環境相結合，打造更流暢的互動體驗。除了主舞台外，Coinfest Asia 還將設有展區、商業媒合、社交活動、產品展示、社群聚會及周邊活動。
Coinfest Asia 2026 門票現已開放購買。希望拓展亞洲加密市場的企業，也可透過官方活動管道了解合作與行銷機會。
關於 Coinfest Asia
Coinfest Asia 是全球最大的加密貨幣盛會，由 Indonesia Crypto Network（ICN）旗下子公司 Coinvestasi 主辦。活動每年在印尼峇里島舉行，匯聚機構、開發者與交易者，共同交流合作，推動亞洲及全球數位資產的未來發展。

title: 迪士尼破天荒合作 TikTok：開放漫威、皮克斯、星戰 IP 給短影音創作者
summary:
迪士尼與 TikTok 宣布達成合作，開放創作者在短影音中使用漫威、星際大戰等角色，精選內容並同步登上 Dis […]

〈迪士尼破天荒合作 TikTok：開放漫威、皮克斯、星戰 IP 給短影音創作者〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
迪士尼與 TikTok 宣布達成合作，開放創作者在短影音中使用漫威、星際大戰等角色，精選內容並同步登上 Disney+。
（前情提要：美版 TikTok 正式出售：甲骨文等3大美資團入主、字節跳動保留大腦，川普贏了嗎？）
（背景補充：TikTok推進電商帝國》抖音支付亮相，還支援AI生成虛擬替身，幫你廣告產品）
迪士尼與 TikTok 五日宣布達成協議，開放創作者在短影音中使用迪士尼電影與電視角色與場景，這是 TikTok 與傳統媒體公司首度達成這類合作，也是全球性的內容共享合作首例。
協議上路後，雙方還會把精選影片同步搬上 Disney+ 串流平台，這是 TikTok 短影音首度登上其他平台播出。
免費開放素材的背後，是迪士尼想借別人家的流量，把觀眾拉回自己的訂閱服務，一場關於誰替誰導流的算計，才正要開始。
合約把灰色地帶收編了
根據協議，創作者只要主動選擇加入，就能取用迪士尼數以百計電影與影集的素材，範圍涵蓋皮克斯（Pixar）、漫威（Marvel）、星際大戰（Star Wars）與 FX。試辦計畫將於未來幾個月內在美國開跑，之後再推展到其他市場，財務條款則未對外揭露。
Disney+ App 內同步新增一個名為 Verts 的直式影片專區，由迪士尼與 TikTok 共同策展，八月五日起在美國上線，鎖定用手機滑直式影片的年輕族群，之後陸續擴及其他市場。雙方另外設立「迪士尼創作者大使計畫」，依創作者表現分級，入選者能拿到更高曝光、獨家活動邀請與職涯發展資源作為回饋，說白了就是拿福利換內容產能。
值得注意的是「主動選擇加入」。沒有加入計畫的創作者，用的還是同一批角色與場景，卻仍留在原本未經授權的灰色地帶，也就是說分為「聽話創作者」與「野生創作者」，前者拿到官方掛保證，後者繼續賭平台會不會下架。
誰在替誰導流？
根據 TikTok 資料，平台用戶去年平均每天分享 650 萬則電影、電視相關貼文，調查也顯示，近半數觀眾曾在看到相關內容後，跑去看一部電影或電視劇。
這代表每一支未授權的二創，本質上都是免費的預告片。換句話說，粉絲二創早就在幫迪士尼免費做行銷，迪士尼過去幾十年的作法是睜一隻眼閉一隻眼，這次乾脆把它寫成合約，把灰色地帶的紅利收歸己有，順便把創作者從「潛在被告」升級成「編制外行銷部門」。
對迪士尼來說，這筆生意的真正產品不是影片本身，是把 TikTok 上一億七千萬美國用戶的眼球，倒進自家訂閱服務的漏斗，順便省下一筆自製直式內容的成本。曾經想打敗對手的產品，最後選擇跟對手進貨，這句話聽起來諷刺，卻是最划算的商業判斷。
對 AI 興訟，對創作者送角色
把這份協議放進迪士尼過去一年的 IP 戰略裡看，反差更明顯。
2025 年 6 月，迪士尼聯合 NBCUniversal（後續 DreamWorks 也加入）控告 AI 影像生成公司 Midjourney 侵權，訴狀點名 Darth Vader、Elsa 等角色遭未經授權生成；迪士尼還向 Google 發出停止侵權函，指控其大規模未經授權訓練，並對 Meta、Character.AI 發出類似信函，態度強硬到近乎宣戰。
同一年 12 月，迪士尼卻一百八十度轉向合作，向 OpenAI 投資 10 億美元並簽下三年授權協議，逾 200 個角色預計 2026 年初登上 Sora，米老鼠、漫威英雄與星戰角色都在名單內。
這次與 TikTok 的協議，等於把同一套邏輯搬到人類創作者身上，只是這次的價碼不是股權或訴訟費，是免費素材加曝光。至於誰來把關哪支影片符合迪士尼形象、創作者的分潤規則怎麼算，協議都沒寫清楚。
更模糊的是，TikTok 美國業務今年一月才完成新股權結構重組，Oracle、Silver Lake、MGX 各持 15% 股權，ByteDance 仍保留 19.9%，內容審核與演算法治理由這家新合資公司負責，誰真正說了算，本身就是一個問號。

title: Sui 共同創辦人、Move 之父 Sam Blackshear，宣布離職加入 Anthropic
summary:
Mysten Labs 共同創辦人暨技術長 Sam Blackshear 宣布離開自己創辦的公司，轉戰 Ant […]

〈Sui 共同創辦人、Move 之父 Sam Blackshear，宣布離職加入 Anthropic〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Mysten Labs 共同創辦人暨技術長 Sam Blackshear 宣布離開自己創辦的公司，轉戰 Anthropic 投入 AI 防禦性安全研究。後續技術方向將由共同創辦人暨執行長 Evan Cheng 接手。
（前情提要：Anthropic 開源 AI 資安工作流：七階段自動找漏洞、驗證到生成補丁）
（背景補充：YC 合夥人 Tom Blomfield 宣布離開 Y Combinator，加入 Anthropic 算力團隊）
身為 Move 語言創造者、Sui 公鏈技術心臟的 Mysten Labs 共同創辦人暨技術長，Sam Blackshear 今（6）晨在 X 宣布離開自己一手打造的公司，轉往 Anthropic 投入 AI 防禦性安全研究。他發文表示：
「回顧我的職涯，最快樂的時候都是在動手做技術、同時探索新問題領域。這是能兩者兼顧的機會，而在攻防雙方力量正在位移的此刻投入資安，讓我充滿動力。」
I am leaving Mysten Labs and joining Anthropic to work on defensive security research.
— Sam Blackshear (@b1ackd0g) August 5, 2026
誰是 Sam Blackshear？
在加入 Mysten Labs 之前，Blackshear 曾任職 Meta Principal Engineer，參與 Move 程式語言、Libra 區塊鏈與 Infer 靜態分析器的開發。
他在貼文中提到，自己一手打造、投入超過 8 年的 Move 語言至今仍是最熱愛的作品。2021 年 9 月，他與另外四位前 Meta 高階主管共同創辦 Mysten Labs，並以 Move 語言為核心打造 Sui 公鏈。
交棒給 Evan Cheng
Mysten Labs 後續技術方向將交由另一位共同創辦人暨執行長 Evan Cheng 接手。
Blackshear 在貼文中親自替接班人背書：「@EvanWeb3 將接手為 Mysten 設定技術願景。Evan 親自招募了我們許多最強的技術人才，先前也曾在 Apple 與 Meta 領導技術團隊，我很期待看到他會帶領的方向。」
為何是防禦性安全？AI 讓攻防天平開始傾斜
Blackshear 特別強調「防禦性」安全研究的定位，暗示他觀察到的變化並非單純資安需求成長，而是 AI 技術正在讓攻擊與防禦的力量對比出現結構性轉變。
當攻擊方能借助 AI 大幅提升效率與規模，防禦端同樣需要具備系統設計與程式語言背景的資深工程師投入，才能補上這道落差。
會持續擔任 Mysten 的顧問
對 Sui 生態而言，創辦團隊核心技術人物出走至 Anthropic，儘管已安排好交棒與顧問身分，市場仍難免關注 Mysten Labs 後續研發步調是否受影響。
Blackshear 對此也表示，他沒有真的離開 Move。「Mysten Labs 是我共事過最強的團隊，我會持續擔任 Mysten 的親近顧問，也對任何主動找上門的 Sui 生態開發者開放。」對於籌備中的 Move 基金會，他則表態：「Move 基金會正在籌備中，我會盡可能持續參與。」
貼文尾聲他也難掩不捨：「在 Mysten 的這段時間，是我所能期望或想像的全部冒險。我由衷感謝 Mysten Labs 與 Sui 生態的每一個人，謝謝大家所做的一切。」這波離職，也呼應近來 Anthropic 等 AI 公司持續向加密產業挖角具備系統安全與程式語言背景資深工程師的趨勢。

title: Google 首席科學家 Jeff Dean 是誰？離職竟讓 Alphabet 蒸發 1900 億美元
summary:
Google 首席科學家 Jeff Dean 宣布離職，結束 27 年任期，與三位頂尖研究員共創 AI 新創 […]

〈Google 首席科學家 Jeff Dean 是誰？離職竟讓 Alphabet 蒸發 1900 億美元〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Google 首席科學家 Jeff Dean 宣布離職，結束 27 年任期，與三位頂尖研究員共創 AI 新創 Discovery Loop，Alphabet 市值一天蒸發近 1,900 億美元，市場正在替 Google 的人才護城河估價。
（前情提要：Google DeepMind 兩大科學家出走、股價挫7%，Demis Hassabis回擊：人才我們搶得到）
（背景補充：Google AI 高層大洗牌！Hassabis 升任首席科學家專攻 AGI，AI 元老 Jeff Dean 離職創業）
Google 首席科學家 Jeff Dean 幾個小時前宣布離開，結束 27 年任期，Alphabet 股價盤中一度重挫 5.4%，終場跌 4.03%，收在 362.43 美元。同時離開的還有三位 Google 頂級研究員，Sanjay Ghemawat、Quoc Le、Oriol Vinyals。
四人將一起創辦新公司 Discovery Loop，由 Dean 出任執行長。問題是這麼大公司的股價，為什麼會被四個人的去留牽動這麼多？答案藏在他們過去二十多年做過的事情裡。
Tomorrow will be my last day at Google after 27 years, and watching it grow from 25 people to 190,000+ has been an amazing journey. Below is a note I shared with many people internally at Google today. An excerpt is:
It has been an absolute pleasure to work with you and to help… pic.twitter.com/o3aRNLkssA
— Jeff Dean (@JeffDean) August 5, 2026
Jeff Dean 是誰？蓋起 Google 的地基
Dean 現年 58 歲，1999 年以 Google 第 30 號員工身分加入，學歷是明尼蘇達大學資工學士、華盛頓大學資工博士。多數人認識他是因為 Gemini，但是他在 Gemini 出現之前，早就把 Google 的底層架構蓋了一輪又一輪。
2004 年他共同發明 MapReduce。簡單來說就是，一套讓成千上萬部電腦能同時分工處理海量資料的運算框架，沒有它，Google 搜尋不可能在幾毫秒內從整個網路撈出答案。
2005 年他共同設計 BigTable，2012 年再做出 Spanner，這兩套分散式資料庫系統，白話說就是讓資料能同時存在世界各地的機房、卻仍然像放在同一部電腦裡一樣好用，至今仍撐著 Google 搜尋、Gmail、YouTube 的底層運作。
他也是把 TPU 推上生產線的關鍵人物。2011 年，他共同創辦 Google Brain，那個團隊後來做出深度學習框架 TensorFlow。2018 年起擔任 Google AI 負責人，2023 年 Google Brain 與 DeepMind 合併後轉任首席科學家，是 Gemini 多模態模型背後的關鍵推手。
從搜尋引擎的地基，到 AI 晶片，再到 Gemini 的核心設計，Dean 幾乎參與了 Google 每一次技術轉型的地基工程，這也是為什麼他的離開被視為不只是換一個人這麼簡單。
AI 的底層是人才戰
AI 競爭的本質，是工程師密度乘以算力，再乘以資料。
當 Dean、Ghemawat、Le、Vinyals 四人同時離開，等於一家公司同時失去分散式系統的奠基者、Google Brain 的創始成員，以及曾任 Google DeepMind 副總裁的 Gemini 核心研究者 Vinyals。這是損失一整組「基礎設施派加研究派」的組合，而目前市場幾乎找不到現成的人補上。
這也是為什麼訊息一出，Alphabet 市值一天蒸發近 1,900 億美元，市場擔心的不是少了誰，而是這代表 Google 內部發生了什麼變化，是不是還有更多人正在盤算著離開？
不過反方論點也存在。Alphabet 本身就是 Discovery Loop 的創始投資人之一，同時是雲端運算夥伴，等於左手放人、右手繼續分一杯羹。Google 同步宣布領導層改組：Demis Hassabis 卸下 Google DeepMind 日常營運，轉任 GDM 董事長與 Alphabet 首席科學家，並繼續領導 Isomorphic Labs。
在 DeepMind 待了 13 年的 Koray Kavukcuoglu 升任 Google DeepMind 資深副總裁，直接向 Sundar Pichai 匯報，統管 Gemini 模型開發、前沿研究與開發者團隊。
執行長 Pichai 的說法是：「我們想用跟 Google 內部不一樣的方式來打造這件事。」官方版本對此說法是分工布局，不是人才失血。但市場信不信，股價稍早已經投了一票。
Discovery Loop 想做什麼？
Discovery Loop 註冊為公益公司，目標是用 AI 自動化科學研究的實驗迴圈，讓數千個實驗同時執行。簡單來說就是用 AI 打造更強的 AI，之後才擴充套件到硬體設計、藥物發現、乾淨能源。Dean 的說法是：「會得到更高數量、也更高品質的實驗，這會帶來科學突破。」
募資由 Radical Ventures 與 Khosla Ventures 共同領投，Kleiner Perkins、Lightspeed、Doerr Capital 與 Alphabet 都參與其中，金額未揭露。
另外 Dean 這次不是跳槽去對手陣營，而是自己另起爐灶，某種程度上比單純跳槽更值得留意，它代表頂尖研究員現在有能力、也有意願，繞過所有巨頭公司，自己成立公司來做研究，而不是繼續替誰打工。

title: 川普鎖喉半導體命脈，傳多晶矽將開徵 15% 關稅、加設進口地板價
summary:
路透披露，川普政府最快 8 月 6 日對多晶矽衍生產品課徵 15% 關稅，並對多晶矽、晶圓、太陽能電池、太陽能 […]

〈川普鎖喉半導體命脈，傳多晶矽將開徵 15% 關稅、加設進口地板價〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
路透披露，川普政府最快 8 月 6 日對多晶矽衍生產品課徵 15% 關稅，並對多晶矽、晶圓、太陽能電池、太陽能模組設下最低進口價格。這項政策直指晶片與太陽能共用的關鍵原料。
（前情提要：川普拋100%半導體關稅重拳，台積電投資2千億美元「躲過一劫」開盤拉漲5%）
（背景補充：川普政府要禁中國製光學通訊收發器！AAOI 盤前飆 18%，5 個交易日翻 7 成）
川普政府這次瞄準是藏在晶片與太陽能板最底層、多數人連名字都念不出來的原料：多晶矽。路透引述四名知情人士透露，白宮最快美東時間 8 月 6 日（週四）正式宣布，對多晶矽衍生產品課徵至少 15% 關稅，同時對進口多晶矽、晶圓、太陽能電池與太陽能模組設下最低進口價格。
地板價加關稅，四類產品全框住
目前流出的政策輪廓，其實是兩把鎖一起上：第一把鎖是關稅，針對多晶矽衍生產品課徵 15%；第二把鎖是地板價，直接對進口多晶矽、晶圓、太陽能電池、太陽能模組四類產品畫出最低價格，低於這條線的進口貨等於違規。
彭博另指出，官員同步準備了臨時抵銷機制：只要進口商願意投資美國本土的晶圓與太陽能電池產能，就能拿到抵減，沖銷這波關稅與地板價帶來的額外成本。
換句話說，這不是單純懲罰進口，而是逼買家掏錢在美國蓋產線。
多晶矽是什麼？同一塊矽，兩種身價
多晶矽是提煉過的矽料，純度拉得多高，決定了它接下來要進哪一條產線。
拉到最頂端的電子級，才夠格切成晶片，手機裡的運算核心多半靠它起家；太陽能級純度稍低一截，卻是外頭數量最大宗的矽晶太陽能板原料。
這場關稅與地板價的法源，要回到 2025 年 7 月 14 日，美國商務部工業與安全域性（BIS）依據貿易擴張法第 232 條，正式對多晶矽及其衍生品，矽晶圓、太陽能電池、太陽能模組，啟動國家安全調查，目標很直白：降低美國對外國多晶矽原料的依賴，同時防堵中國在晶片供應鏈的布局持續擴張。
目前太陽能產業的供應鏈仍由中國主導，這也是白宮選擇從最上游原料下手的原因。
15% 比市場預期溫和，成本轉嫁給誰？
不過有趣的是，15% 這個數字其實比市場預期溫和不少。
Roth Capital Partners 分析師先前預估，稅率可能落在 25% 至 35% 之間，實際傳出的版本明顯偏低，究竟是白宮手下留情，還是刻意留一手後續加碼的空間，目前沒人說得準。
地板價的衝擊反而更直接：Roth Capital Partners 估算，最低進口價會讓進口太陽能電池片每瓦成本增加 0.10 美元，換算到一整組模組，等於多出約 600 至 800 美元的成本，這筆帳最終多半會轉嫁到裝設太陽能系統的企業與家戶身上。
而能接住這波保護的美國本土產能，說穿了只有兩家：密西根州的 Hemlock Semiconductor（由康寧與日本信越半導體合資），以及總部位於慕尼黑、在田納西州設廠的 Wacker Chemie。訊息傳出當天，康寧股價一度大漲逾 9%，市場顯然已經先押注誰是受益者。
美國商務部與白宮目前都未回應置評，公告的最終條文仍可能持續變動。

title: 普丁簽署加密貨幣法案：開放散戶合法買幣、全面納管交易所
summary:
俄羅斯加密貨幣監管邁入新階段。俄羅斯總統普丁（Vladimir Putin）正式簽署加密貨幣法案，首度明確規範交易所、託管機構、券商、清算機構及投資人等市場參與者，並允許散戶在一定額度內合法投資加密貨幣。

〈普丁簽署加密貨幣法案：開放散戶合法買幣、全面納管交易所〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
俄羅斯加密貨幣監管邁入新階段。俄羅斯總統普丁（Vladimir Putin）正式簽署加密貨幣法案，首度明確規範交易所、託管機構、券商、清算機構及投資人等市場參與者，並允許散戶在一定額度內合法投資加密貨幣。
不過，這部法案同時也維持了禁止在國內使用加密貨幣作為支付手段或法定貨幣的禁令，但允許使用加密貨幣進行跨境貿易結算，以持續作為因應西方制裁的重要支付管道。
散戶可合法投資加密貨幣，每年購買額度設上限
根據《塔斯社（TASS）》報導，新法將俄羅斯加密貨幣市場正式納入監管體系。依照新規，一般散戶可透過合格中介機構購買高流動性的加密貨幣，每人每年最高投資額度為 30 萬盧布（約 3,700 美元）。不過，目前官方尚未公布哪些加密貨幣符合「高流動性」資格。
至於符合資格的專業投資人，則不受投資金額限制，可自由買賣任何加密資產。
值得注意的是，無論是一般散戶或專業投資人，都必須先通過官方規定的「適格性測驗（Suitability Test）」。此外，散戶也可依據過去的加密貨幣交易紀錄，申請升級為專業投資人，以取得更高的投資額度。
加密貨幣交易所全面納管，最低資本門檻約 18.5 萬美元
除了投資人管理，新法也同步建立交易平台監管制度。未來所有加密貨幣交易所若要在俄羅斯合法營運，必須加入政府設立的專屬登記名冊，且最低自有資本須達 1,500 萬盧布（約 18.5 萬美元）。
此外，交易所還必須加入金融市場自律組織，進一步接受市場監督與自律規範。
禁止境內支付，但跨境貿易仍可使用加密貨幣
雖然俄羅斯建立完整的加密貨幣交易制度，但政府對於支付用途仍維持嚴格限制。
根據新法，加密貨幣依舊不得作為俄羅斯境內商品或服務的支付工具，也不得取得法定貨幣地位。不過，跨境支付則仍維持開放。新法允許俄羅斯居民與境外企業進行國際貿易時，使用加密貨幣完成跨境結算。
事實上，俄羅斯自 2024 年起就已開始允許企業在國際貿易中使用加密貨幣，以降低西方金融制裁帶來的影響。
根據規劃，這部新法將於 2026 年 9 月 1 日正式生效；其中部分涉及加密資產發行與流通的規定，則將延後至 2027 年 9 月 1 日施行；針對目前已在營運的交易所，官方也將給予寬限期，業者須在 2027 年 3 月 1 日前完成合規調整與註冊程序。
俄羅斯加密監管逐步成形，但挖礦監管同步收緊
這項法案也象徵俄羅斯對數位資產政策出現重大轉變。俄羅斯國家杜馬（State Duma，國會下議院）已於上月通過法案，繼今年 4 月完成一讀後，如今隨著普丁正式簽署成法，加密貨幣交易也正式被納入政府監管架構。
事實上，俄羅斯央行近期也持續完善相關制度。上周才公布「數位資產及數位權利（Digital Rights）有組織交易」監管草案，涵蓋加密貨幣交易所及數位資產託管機構的管理規範，顯示官方正逐步建立完整的市場基礎設施。
另一方面，俄羅斯對加密貨幣挖礦的監管則持續收緊。俄羅斯政府上月已發布行政命令，自 8 月 15 日起至 2032 年底，禁止莫斯科、莫斯科州以及庫斯克州（Kursk）部分地區進行加密貨幣挖礦及參與礦池。
免責聲明：本文只為提供市場訊息，所有內容及觀點僅供參考，不構成投資建議，不代表區塊客觀點和立場。投資者應自行決策與交易，對投資者交易形成的直接或間接損失，作者及區塊客將不承擔任何責任。

title: Young women tell BBC of rape, assault and harassment at Army training college for teenagers
summary: They say the incidents happened at the Army Foundation College in Harrogate when they were aged 17.
full_text:
Women tell BBC of rape and abuse at Army teen college
- Published
Warning: This article contains sexual language and details of sexual assault
Four young women have told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an army training college for teenagers - with one saying she was raped by several fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.
The women all attended the Army Foundation College (AFC) at Harrogate, North Yorkshire, over the past five years and say the incidents happened when they were aged 17.
The college has a dangerous culture of misogyny and sexual violence, say the women, who are all speaking out for the first time.
These reports are "extremely distressing and serious", said an Army spokesperson in a statement.
The BBC can also reveal that North Yorkshire Police received 16 reports of sexual offences linked to the college in the year to June, according to a Freedom of Information request.
Those reported offences include allegations of exposure, voyeurism and sexual assault. No information was provided as to whether they had led to prosecutions.
A total of 176 complaints of inappropriate sexual behaviour at the college were made between January 2018 and June 2025, according to Ministry of Defence (MoD) data.
Thirty-two allegations were against permanent staff and 144 against junior soldiers.
"Unacceptable and criminal behaviour has absolutely no place in our Armed Forces," said the Army spokesperson.
"People join in the hope of having a fantastic career and any such reports are unacceptable and go completely against everything the Army stands for."
AFC is the largest military training establishment for under-19s in the UK and it receives all the Army's 16-year-old recruits. There are currently 70 female junior soldiers at the Harrogate site out of a total of 889.
We have changed all the women's names to protect their identities.
'I felt like a piece of meat'
Ever since she was a small child, Tilly had always wanted to be a soldier.
"I liked the idea of being challenged and had always admired women in non-traditional roles," she says. "I'd always been into action films."
But she says her dream was shattered when she was raped at AFC by several fellow soldiers.
"They were like 'do you want to come into the room?' And me being a naive 17-year-old girl was like 'yeah fine'," Tilly recalls.
"They started taking my clothes off and then this led to them doing stuff I didn't consent to. There were a lot of them. They touched me in places, made inappropriate comments, calling me a thing rather than a girl.
"And then I was raped… by multiple junior soldiers, same age as me. It went on for hours. I felt like a piece of meat."
Tilly left the Army two weeks after the attack.
"I couldn't be in there. I spoke to my mum and she was like you need to leave," she says.
"I would have just been known as the girl that shagged loads of people - that's what I would have been known for the rest of my career, and that's not what happened."
The BBC understands Tilly reported the alleged rape to police but no charges were brought, partly because of what the Crown Prosecution Service later described as an "entirely inadequate" police investigation.
Tilly reached a financial settlement with North Yorkshire Police - with no admission of liability from the force.
Two of the other three women we spoke to also went to the police, but we are not reporting any details of the investigations to protect their identities.
A second woman, Monica, says a fellow soldier trapped her in a room and attacked her.
"He stood against the door so I couldn't get out. He then pushed himself up against me, started kissing my face and touching me all over. He sexually assaulted me," she says.
"I managed to push him off. I'm not sure how because he's really strong."
Monica received an unrelated medical discharge from the college, but says this came as a relief after what she had been put through.
The third woman's story was told to us by her mother, Cheryl.
Her daughter, Amy, was sexually assaulted, she says, and had to navigate almost daily sexual harassment during her training.
Because the lock to Amy's room was not working, says Cheryl, "she found herself sleeping across the door to stop male soldiers coming in".
My daughter was "sold a dream" when she was recruited to the college, she adds, but it turned out to be the complete opposite in reality.
The fourth woman we have spoken to describes how misogynistic attitudes and behaviour of AFC staff rubbed off on some of the male teenagers.
In front of a group of new recruits in her first week at the college, Ellie - who says she was sexually assaulted and harassed at AFC - recalls one of the instructors saying: "It's all about the pussy and how much of it you can get."
Instructors would also mark girls' looks out of 10, she says, and would "walk into our dorms without knocking, and we'd be standing there just in our knickers - they would just stare".
Ellie says she had been desperate to be an infantry soldier.
"I wanted to serve my country and being a soldier meant I could do that at times of war. I wasn't a girly girl and it just seemed like a perfect fit for me."
But what happened at AFC made Ellie decide that a career in the Army was not for her.
The Army told the BBC: "We encourage anyone who has experienced or witnessed unacceptable or criminal behaviour at the Army Foundation College to come forward."
Acknowledging that this can be difficult, it said several reforms had been introduced to support victims, including the Defence Serious Crime Command, providing specialist support through the justice process, outside of the Army chain of command.
'Have you heard about that slag?'
Several adult instructors at AFC have been convicted by courts martial of physical and sexual violence in the past five years - including Cpl Daniel Conway and Cpl Simon Bartram.
In 2023, Conway was jailed for more than seven years for raping a colleague while she was sleeping. In the same year, Bartram was found guilty of sexual assault and sentenced to 20 months in military detention.
None of the allegations in our investigation relate to these instructors, but the four women say the convictions raise serious questions about the college's culture.
A sexist attitude towards women is encouraged by some male instructors, believes Tilly.
After she was raped, she says she heard an instructor going round saying: "Have you heard about that slag who shagged all those blokes?"
"Coming from an instructor is just wrong - it sends out the wrong message about women and it teaches boys this attitude that we're only good for one thing," she says.

Cheryl says her daughter, Amy, also reported being subjected to misogynistic verbal abuse from staff.
"She'd be standing in line in the corridor and she'd be picked out as a massive slag or slapper because [instructors] would say it was her fault people were looking at her.
"She was told that 'every year there is one that [the male recruits] want and it looks like this year you're the one they want.'
"It just broke my heart, because what you forget about is that she's just a child."
Serious questions need to be asked about whether the college should continue operating, says Labour MP Emma Lewell, who sits on the Defence Committee.
"If this was anywhere else, it would have been closed down by now, or someone would have been in there looking in-depth at what is going on," she says.
"As a matter of urgency there should be an independent inquiry into the college led by someone with significant safeguarding experience, and they need to be able to speak to the children there."
The UK government defines a child as anyone under 18.

title: Car washes and vape shops can still sponsor skilled foreign workers despite visa changes
summary: The rules were tightened in July 2025 to restrict the scheme mostly to graduate-level employees who would be earning at least £41,700.
full_text:
Car washes and vape shops can still sponsor skilled foreign workers despite visa changes
- Published
More than 1,900 small high street businesses including mini-marts, vape shops and car washes are licensed to sponsor foreign workers under a specialist scheme intended for high-earning individuals despite visa rules being tightened, BBC Verify has found.
The Home Office scheme allows registered employers to recruit workers from overseas who meet a certain skill level. The rules were tightened in July 2025 to restrict the scheme mostly to graduate-level employees who would be earning at least £41,700.
But a year on from the rule change, BBC Verify has found more than 1,500 grocery and convenience stores, 150 taxi operators, 100 barber shops, and dozens of car washes and vape shops are still on the register and able to sponsor people to apply for visas.
More than 100 of those businesses were added to the skilled worker sponsorship list after the rules were tightened. Being on the register does not mean applications for individual visas would be approved.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood ordered an urgent review into the presence of vape shops, barbers and car washes on the skilled worker sponsor register two months ago, following concerns over the "potential misuse of the system". The Home Office said at the time that any businesses seeking to abuse the system would have their licences revoked.
A Home Office spokesperson said: "We have raised the skilled worker threshold and over 100 occupations are now ineligible for new skilled worker visas."
It is understood some of the companies that joined the register after the rules changed may have applied before they took effect. Some companies may have also remained on the register because they were approved before July 2025 or are sponsoring workers who were already in the UK.
There are more than 120,000 businesses with licences to sponsor skilled workers. The skilled worker scheme was introduced after Brexit for employers to recruit workers after Eu free movement ended. Smaller firms must pay a £611 fee to apply to join the register while larger businesses, such as those with more than 50 staff, pay a fee of £1,682. Anyone can be visited by the UK Visas and Immigration service during the application process.
Until July last year, someone being hired from abroad could qualify for sponsorship if their qualifications met an A-Level or equivalent standard, as long as they were paid at least £38,700 in most cases. Since the rule change, non-graduate professions, such as shop managers, are no longer eligible to apply. There are also higher English-language skill requirements that were introduced in January this year.
The Home Office said there were 68,067 skilled worker visas granted in the 12 months to March this year - 29,745 to main applicants and 38,322 to their dependants - which is 30% lower than the year before. IT professionals were the most common type of people to be granted the visas, followed by those people working in finance, while the fall in approvals was mostly attributed to those in food preparation and hospitality trades no longer qualifying for the scheme.
Jobs including sales and retail assistants, taxi drivers and chauffeurs are currently listed by the government as ineligible for skilled worker visas, but there are some exemptions, such as bricklayers, carpenters or nursing assistants and other occupations where there is a shortage in the UK.
The Home Office revoked 3,299 licences in 2025 compared with 347 in 2023. Its register does not state how many certificates of sponsorship or visas have been issued for each business or what type of role it has hired for, but Home Office guidance states firms must offer genuine jobs that meet skill and salary rules, and only sponsor workers for eligible roles.
As businesses are only listed by name, it is not always clear what industry a company operates within. BBC Verify identified the more than 1,900 small high-street businesses that had retained a sponsorship licence by matching their names and locations to Companies House records and Google business listings to identify whether the mini marts, car washes and other small operations were on the list.
Around 1,700 of those were in England, more than 140 were in Scotland, over 80 were in Wales and just two were in Northern Ireland.
Separately, BBC Verify found 60 businesses on the register that had been fined for emloying illegal workers between April 2024 and December 2025. They had been fined a combined £2.5m.
A Home Office spokesperson said: "Illegal working will not be accepted, and businesses who face two or more illegal working penalties of up to £60,000, or fail to pay a penalty the first time, will have their license to hire workers revoked."
Speaking about the visa rule change, Dr Madeleine Sumption, director of the University of Oxford's Migration Observatory, said that if businesses were on the register before the rules changed, they can continue to employ people they had already sponsored. "But they can't now bring in a new person to do those jobs."
Toby Way, a lawyer at WestBridge Business Immigration which helps businesses apply to be sponsors, told BBC Verify that while most sponsorship approvals are legitimate, "We come across a lot of exaggeration and some downright lying about sponsored roles".
"Hotels and restaurants have been hit massively by the rule changes. They're now unable to sponsor a chef or a manager, but they might claim they need someone for marketing or book-keeping, because those roles are on the temporary shortage list," he said.
"We know the Home Office looks at the finances of the businesses now and whether their revenue or profit means they can pay the required salary."
Immigration lawyer Joanna Hunt of DAC Beachcroft said that it would be difficult for a high street shop to justify sponsorship at the degree level.
"Subject to a few exceptions, a job needs to be skilled to 'degree level' to allow a business to sponsor a worker to fill it and the Home Office will consider if the role fits with the type of business the sponsor operates. A high street shop may find this requirement difficult to demonstrate."
Additional reporting by Rob England

title: Michelin-star restaurant regains top hygiene rating after previous one-star inspection
summary: Ynyshir got a one-star food hygiene rating from inspectors but has since been restored to five stars.
full_text:
Michelin-star restaurant regains top hygiene rating after previous one-star inspection
- Published
Wales' only two-Michelin-star restaurant which received a one-star food hygiene rating after inspectors found flies, broken equipment and a dirty knife has had its five-star rating restored.
Ynyshir Restaurant near Machynlleth in mid Wales was previously ordered to stop serving raw lobster after the council found "significant hazards" were not properly identified.
At the time, Ynyshir, which serves Japanese-inspired raw dishes as part of its nearly £500 per head 30-course tasting menu, accused inspectors of not understanding its specialised procedures.
Ceredigion council said an inspection in February found the "business had addressed all matters identified during the original inspection".
"This outcome demonstrates the effectiveness of the food hygiene inspection process and the positive results that can be achieved through constructive engagement between regulatory officers and food businesses to improve standards," the council added.
Chef Gareth Ward previously said he was not embarrassed when the restaurant was given a one-out-of-five score.
Ynyshir has been asked to comment.
Food critic Giles Coren previously came out in support of the restaurant, claiming Michelin-starred restaurants should not have to abide by normal health and safety rules and the guidelines should "probably be modernised".
"It is not little kitchens and pots boiling away, mimsy little things being placed on plates. He is cooking with fire... he stands there in his leather apron and it's roaring like fireworks," Coren said.
Ward, who has recently announced he will be bringing fine dining to Aberystwyth Town Football Club, previously said his restaurant was working "at the highest standard in the world" and doing "something different" with how it approached raw ingredients and techniques.
He said he had faced "persistent challenges" with Ceredigion council's environmental health department, "primarily relating to documentation and a lack of understanding of our specialised procedures".
A Freedom of Information (FOI) request by the BBC revealed the one-star rating was based on factors including a dirty floor, inadequate hand-washing facilities in some areas, broken equipment and "an accumulation of dead flies".
Ceredigion council said inspections were carried out in line with national standards set by the Food Standards Agency and, between April and December 2025, 90% of inspected premises in Ceredigion achieved a food hygiene rating of between three and five out of five.

title: The 'education gap' hiding behind picture-perfect Cornwall and Devon
summary: Behind the South West's postcard image, poverty and isolation are limiting opportunities for many young people.
full_text:
The 'education gap' hiding behind picture-perfect Cornwall and Devon
- Published
This year, millions of holidaymakers will head to Cornwall and Devon for their sandy beaches and pretty coastal towns - just two reasons why the South West peninsula is England's top tourist destination.
Yet behind its wild coastal beauty and affluent towns lies a different story: one of lost opportunities and the unfulfilled potential of many growing up in the region.
On almost every measure, the region is among the weakest educationally, according to the South West Social Mobility Commission, a coalition of organisations trying to bring about change.
Disparities in GCSE results are often framed through the lens of a North-South divide, but that narrative can obscure the challenges facing children in coastal and rural parts of England.
When you look at the regional data for English and maths GCSE passes for all pupils in England, you can see that, overall, the South outperforms the North.
However, when you drill down into the data at a local authority level, and take into account children on free school meals, you see a different story.
The South West is the second worst performing region through this lens, after the South East.
Tanya Ovenden-Hope, Professor of Education at Plymouth Marjon University, describes what happens in the South West as "pretty poverty", and says this leads to fewer young people reaching their full potential.
She calls growing up in a low-income family in a coastal rural community a potentially "toxic" combination.
The government does measure the level of disadvantage in communities but Prof Ovenden-Hope says too much of that is done using measures that work for towns and cities, including transport.
"If you live in Cornwall you have to own a car. It's not a luxury, it's a necessity, because everything you do and everywhere you go involves some kind of travel. That's not measured by the government's measures of deprivation."
This matters because it helps decide how government money is allocated across England.
Tourism is the largest contributor to Cornwall's economy, but it comes at a price for local families bringing up children on the lowest incomes.
In April 2025, Cornwall Council introduced a 100% premium on council tax for second homes because of growing concern that wealthier visitors were buying up property at higher prices, reducing the affordability and availability of starter homes for local families.
Figures from the ONS show the average house price in Cornwall in May 2026 was £280,000, and across the South West region it was £303,000. The UK average was £271,000 for that same period. Meanwhile average monthly rent in Cornwall rose by 4% in the year to June 2026 to £1,005.
"It's not all ice creams and sandy beaches and turquoise seas," says Dominic Wilkes, a headteacher who moved from Greater Manchester to Bude in North Cornwall.
Higher housing costs and the need for a car impact training and teacher recruitment. While the remoteness of some communities can also act as a deterrent for young teachers to move here from other parts of England, according to recent research.
For Wilkes, who works at the only secondary school in Bude, the main upside is better teacher retention, which helps build a deep connection to the local community.
But inspiring children to think about different options for their future comes with its challenges.
As a teacher in Greater Manchester, Wilkes could hop on a tram to take pupils to museums and different workplaces, including the BBC at MediaCity in Salford, as part of the curriculum.
The nearest railway station is about 30 miles from Budehaven Community School. Pupils travel in from scattered villages and the area offers a relatively limited range of employers able to broaden their horizons or spark ambitions beyond the classroom.
Year 10 pupil Ethan, from Budehaven Community School, wants to become a marine biologist and recently completed a work experience placement at a seal sanctuary that was a three-hour round trip by car.
"I love being in the sea and just protecting its habitats and wildlife, it really makes me excited to do something like that," he said.
"I think Cornwall's amazing and all my family are here but I think I want to be able to grow as a person. I think I can only do that by leaving and exploring new adventures."
Year 9 student Burt told us he had to travel to Oxfordshire and Coventry to take part in the National Youth Choir, which meant his dad had to book a hotel to break up the journey.
He thinks there are good opportunities to be found but they're more difficult, and sometimes costly, to access from his town.
But others told us Cornwall is the perfect location for them. Poppy wants to be a florist and dreams of opening a seasonal business selling homegrown local wildflowers.
Wilkes has decided to spend above average on careers advice and trips, including to universities, to help expand pupils' horizons but it is still hard.
He had to turn down an offer of work experience from a "brilliant company" because although it didn't look too far on a map, it was five hours each way by road, without a direct bus service.
This kind of challenge potentially deepens the divide between families who have the money to afford petrol for long-distance trips or holidays abroad, and those who are just about managing the basics with a rising cost of living.
In the South West, much of the local employment is in farming or tourism, with young adults looking to leave and build their careers elsewhere.
In 2024, jobs related to the visitor economy made up approximately 20% of employment in Cornwall.
The South West Mobility Commission has other concerns about children who receive free school meals in the region.
It warns that 46% of secondary pupils (and 27% of primary pupils) are persistently absent, which means missing 10% of their school time.
While suspensions, exclusions and home education are also among the highest in England "raising important questions about school engagement, belonging and access to education".
In young adulthood, the potential impact can be seen in the proportion who go on to university, one of the biggest long-term drivers of improved earnings and life chances between generations.
In the South West, 19% of those who grew up receiving free school meals go on to get a degree, the lowest level in England, and below the North East. The national average is 29%.
This is what motivated Nick Wakeling, a teacher at Colyton Grammar School, to get in touch.
He runs the Colyton Foundation, a charity that supports young people into university.
One of the foundation's schemes is Your Future Story, backed by schools and universities to support 1,000 secondary school pupils from lower income families through to university with targeted support.
Libby is now considering a creative degree after Your Future Story arranged for her to go on a trip to Falmouth, a 1 hour 40 minute drive away. It "gave me an idea of what university would be like," she says.
There is a big push for locally generated solutions from the South West Social Mobility Commission, funded by a coalition including Exeter University, which warns the region is near the bottom on most measures of educational attainment from early childhood onwards.
While this can limit life chances in terms of getting to higher earnings, fewer young people in the South West are not in education, employment or training than most other parts of England. This is at a time when the national concern about what are called NEETs has reached an all-time high.
The report found the South West has the highest proportion of people who received free school meals as children in sustained work by the age of 28.
A Department for Education Spokesperson said: "This government believes every child should grow up with opportunity on their doorstep and hope for the future, with an education system that opens doors and cuts the link between background and success."

title: In Odesa, no-one is safe from Russia's new Black Sea strikes
summary: Blackened ships and smashed docks mark Russia's recent surge of attacks on Ukraine's coastline.
full_text:
In Odesa, no-one is safe from Russia's new Black Sea strikes
- Published
"My crane operator, my partner, died five metres from me… The driver remained in the cabin. He also died."
Svitlana Halchenko winces as she remembers the Russian ballistic missile which exploded at work in Odesa, killing her colleagues.
Svitlana works as a warehouse shift manager at the city's main port.
Despite her injuries – she walks with a limp, pieces of shrapnel still embedded in her leg and back – Svitlana is determined to keep working.
But her normally bustling workplace is largely silent.
Russia is ramping up its efforts to strangle Ukraine's commercial links to the outside world, launching attacks all along the country's Black Sea coastline.
From damaged port infrastructure to listing ships with bridges blackened and containers still smouldering, the evidence is everywhere. Nowhere more so than out towards the horizon, where the approaches to Ukraine's once bustling ports – Odesa, Chornomorsk, Pivdennyi – are almost devoid of ships.
Svitlana maintains a brave smile throughout our conversation, but her distress is painfully obvious. Her fingers constantly twist a tissue as she tries to maintain her composure and she gazes into the distance as tears well up behind her glasses.
The last few weeks have been worse than ever.
"It's been very difficult for morale," she says with a deep sigh. "A lot of sirens, a lot of shaheds [drones], a lot of hits. People are very tense."
My crane operator, my partner, died five metres from me… The driver remained in the cabin. He also died
According to Ukraine's port administration, July saw 57 Russian attacks on civilian vessels, 22 of them at sea, and a further 67 hits on port infrastructure.
While there have been Russian attacks on international vessels before, they've never been so numerous or so deadly.
On July 19, a Turkish-owned cargo vessel, Golden Leo, was struck by three Russian missiles, killing nine Indian and Syrian crew members and a Ukrainian pilot.
The ship, carrying Ukrainian corn, sank off Odesa a week later.
According to the global shipping journal Lloyd's List, the Black Sea may now be the most dangerous place for shipping in the world - with July the deadliest month for merchant seamen, external since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.
At his union's offices in the port city, Oleg Grygoriuk, Chairman of the Marine Transport Workers Union of Ukraine, says his members are suffering.
"There are a lot of veterans who already served their country," he says, "and they literally say that being in the port is more scary than being on the front line."
Odesa's proximity to Russian-occupied territory means that workers often have little time to react.
"A missile flies from Crimea within a minute," he says. "If you are sitting in a crane, you need three and a half minutes to get down and go to the shelter. There's literally no time to do that."
On a rare visit to one of the area's main ports, we saw almost no sign of movement. Hundreds of metres of berths sat empty and towering gantry cranes stood idle as a skeleton crew conducted maintenance.
The military authorities allowed the visit on strict condition that we neither name the facility nor film anything. Ukraine doesn't want Russia to know what has and hasn't been damaged or reveal details that might aid Moscow in further targeting.
Two damaged cargo vessels were moored nearby. Both had suffered severe damage to the superstructure, where the bridge and crew quarters are located.
Just one lone freighter was seen moving towards the port.
"My heart is broken," a senior manager told us on condition we didn't name him.
"Normally there's a queue, even out at sea, waiting for a berth."
"There was a deal," he said, referring to the UN-brokered 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, under which Russia agreed to lift its blockade on Ukraine's agricultural exports. The agreement established safe maritime corridors to Odesa's main ports.
"They stopped the deal in the middle of 2023, but they didn't start attacking it until recently," the manager said.
"Today they do it systematically."
Halfway through our tour, sirens sounded, forcing us to seek shelter for several minutes as a Russian jet-powered drone flew overhead.
Weary dock workers scanned their phones for updates until the all-clear sounded.
The manager said recent alerts have forced the port to shut down for 15 out of 24 hours.
Technically, the port is open, as are all the others in the area. There is no prohibition on commercial ships attempting to use them. But the risks are clearly too great for most shipowners.
"There is barely anybody who wants to call because there is a huge problem with people getting killed," says Andrey Stavnitser, co-owner and CEO of one of the largest ports in the area.
"We can see that the whole supply chain is on hold."
Stavnitser says Russia is almost certainly retaliating for Ukraine's recent, highly successful attacks on Russian shipping, including sanctioned vessels carrying oil, as well as other ships involved in ferrying supplies to Russian-occupied Crimea.
Using its own drones, Ukraine's Operation MoLoChKa (which roughly translates as "Moscow will fall through Crimea") has struck around 200 Russian vessels, bringing traffic in the strategic Sea of Azov to a virtual standstill.
Ukrainians bristle at the suggestion that Russia and Ukraine are playing the same game. Kyiv is attempting to loosen Moscow's grip on occupied territory, they point out, while Russia is preventing Ukraine from exporting badly needed grain to the international market.
With Ukraine's summer grain harvest well under way, this is all happening at the worst possible time.
"It's the most sensitive period," says Volodymyr Slavinskyi, trading director for Nibulon, one of the country's leading grain exporters.
"Farmers need to quickly harvest grains from the fields, not to lose the crop. They need to be able to sell the crop they harvested and reinvest money in the next production cycle."
The impact of a prolonged shutdown of Ukraine's ports are likely to be severe. Ukraine is one of the world's largest producers of grain and oilseeds, supplying around 6% of global wheat exports before Russia's full-scale invasion and 10% of corn exports.
But reports suggest, external its export capacity has dropped by at least a third since Russia launched its full-scale invasion.
The Black Sea remains a vital export route for the country. Last year, the Greater Odesa ports accounted for more than 73 million tonnes of Ukraine's maritime exports, with grain accounting for 38 million tonnes.
With almost no vessels currently moving on Ukraine's Black Sea shipping corridor, traders are already counting the cost of this summer's closure.
"I would say we've already lost the ability to deliver to global customers around half a million or 700,000 metric tons of Ukrainian grains and oilseeds," Slavinskyi says.
Away from the port, Odesa is determined to show off a very different side. The summer season is in full swing. The beaches are packed as visitors descend on the Black Sea from all over Ukraine.
Buskers perform on the city's famous Potemkin Stairs, while sunbathers barely flinch as the sirens sound and explosions rumble in the distance.
In a video published on Monday, swimmers were seen removing a Russian drone from the water as holidaymakers look on.
They know the risks. In late June, 26-year-old Daria Kravchenko was killed when shrapnel from an intercepted Russian drone landed on the beach.
This week, holidaymakers on Russia's equally Black Sea coast suffered a similar fate when an intercepted Ukrainian drone crashed onto a busy beach.
Local authorities said seven people were killed, including three children.
It's not clear what Ukraine was targeting, but this war on ships and ports has many casual victims. Sailors, dockworkers or people simply unlucky enough to live or work nearby.
