title: 美光關掉 Crucial 後出保固改退現金！網友送修 DDR5 只拿回「當下市價」的 17%
summary:
一名 Reddit 網友 8 月 5 日發文指出，他依 Crucial 的「終身保固」送修一組 48GB DD […]

〈美光關掉 Crucial 後出保固改退現金！網友送修 DDR5 只拿回「當下市價」的 17%〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
一名 Reddit 網友 8 月 5 日發文指出，他依 Crucial 的「終身保固」送修一組 48GB DDR5 記憶體，卻收到美光通知說即日起不再提供替換產品，唯一方案是退還原始購買金額 241.86 美元，理由是 Crucial 已於今年稍早關閉消費者業務、剩餘庫存售罄。他表示同規格記憶體現在要價約 1,400 美元，退款只有市價的 17%，而且他為了整組更換已經交出原本還能用的另一條，非常不爽。
（前情提要：傳台灣美光工會「醞釀罷工」！不滿獎金慘輸三星、SK 海力士，訴求取消分紅上限）
（背景補充：亞馬遜警告：記憶體危機將殺死遊戲主機與PC，雲端遊戲是唯一出路）
重點摘要
- 網友保固送修 48GB DDR5，美光只退原價 241.86 美元，不再提供替換品。
- 同規格記憶體現價約 1,400 美元，退款僅約市價的 17%。
- Crucial 保固條款原本就寫明退款取原購買價與公平市價的較低者。
在記憶體漲成這樣的年份，保固到底保了什麼，變成很現實的問題。一名 Reddit 網友 8 月 5 日在 r/pcmasterrace 發文，說他依 Crucial 的終身保固送修一組 48GB DDR5 記憶體，結果收到美光的這封信。
請注意，即日起，我們無法再為保固索賠提供替換產品。唯一可行的解決方案是退還原始購買價格，包含所有適用稅金。這是因為 Crucial 已於今年稍早關閉其消費者業務，且剩餘庫存已售罄。
照他的說法，這組 kit 裡只有一條壞掉，但依規定整組更換必須整組寄回，所以他把還能正常運作的那條也一起送了出去。美光原本已經提議換三條 CP16G64C32U5B 給他，容量相同、速度更好，最後卻改成現金買斷 241.86 美元。他還付了來回的運費。
這則貼文引發許多自組電腦的網友回應，硬體評測頻道 Gamers Nexus 創辦人 Steve Burke 也在留言區表示想報導這件事並已聯繫當事人。
保固退款是怎麼算錢的？
241.86 美元這個數字本身沒有問題，網友不爽的是這價格已經是過去式。
當事人說，今天要買一組同等規格的 DDR5 kit 大約要 1,400 美元，退款金額只剩市價的 17%，中間差了 1,158 美元。這個落差不是特例，而是整個記憶體市場在過去一年發生的事。
模組化筆電廠 Framework 的 48GB 記憶體升級選項，2025 年 6 月報價 250 美元，到同年 12 月變成 620 美元，半年漲了 148%。Gartner 預估 2026 年記憶體成本將上漲 130%，DDR5 在今年第一季的漲幅達到 110%。TrendForce 估計 AI 相關應用在 2026 年會吃掉全球 DRAM 晶圓產能約兩成。
換句話說，241.86 美元大概是 2025 年中買 48GB 的價格。保固賠的是你當初付的錢，不是你現在買得回來的東西。在以前這兩個價格不會差太多，但今年差了將快要 6 倍。
條款其實站在美光那邊
留言區很快有人翻出 Crucial 的保固條款原文，內容是這樣寫的。
Micron CPG 得自行選擇維修、更換、提供店內折抵，或退還原始購買價格與公平市價之中較低者。
關鍵在「較低者」三個字。條款從一開始就把選擇權留給廠商，也預先把退款金額綁在兩個數字的下限。有做過多年 RMA 的網友補充，這種寫法在業界是標準做法，不是美光獨有。
網友也給了當事人實際建議，要求把原本送修的硬體原封退回通常是可行的選項，就算要自付運費，也比手上完全沒有記憶體划算。當事人目前已正式拒絕退款方案，要求退還實體硬體、換等值的美光企業級 DDR5、或是換回和「當下成本」差異不大的和解金，並在等待客服回電。
所以這件事的性質，並不是廠商片面翻臉不認帳，而是對自己有利的條款，撞上了之前全球沒有預知到的大漲價。美光 2025 年 12 月宣布退出 Crucial 消費者業務時，官方說法是已售出的產品會繼續依原條款享有保固與售後支援。八個月後條款確實照走了，只是走到了對消費者最不利的方式。
台灣消費者要注意什麼
美光退出消費通路的出貨期限落在 2026 年 2 月，之後消費級記憶體市場實質上只剩三星與 SK 海力士兩家大廠在供貨。這代表台灣手上還持有 Crucial 記憶體或 SSD 的人，未來若送修，遇到相同狀況的機率並不低，庫存不會再補了，只會退款，而且是退以前買入的牌價。
比較務實的做法是先確認自己的保固主體是誰。如果是透過台灣代理商購買，處理窗口與求償對象跟直接向原廠申請並不相同；如果打算送修，也值得先問清楚一旦沒有庫存，對方提供的是退款還是原物退回，再決定要不要把還能用的模組一起寄出去。
美光最近在台灣還有另一條新聞，台灣美光工會傳出因獎金與分紅上限問題醞釀罷工。
常見問題
Crucial 終身保固現在還有效嗎？
保固本身仍在，但美光已關閉 Crucial 消費者業務且庫存售罄，實務上無法提供替換品。依條款廠商可選擇退還原始購買價與公平市價之中較低者，因此在記憶體大漲的當下，退款金額可能遠低於重置成本。
送修前可以做什麼保護自己？
先確認保固主體是原廠或台灣代理商，並事先詢問若無庫存會提供退款還是原物退回。若整組送修的規定會迫使你交出仍可正常使用的模組，可評估是否值得，必要時要求退回未維修的原品。

蘋果財報亮眼股價卻下挫，庫克謝幕之戰形容記憶體遇「百年大洪水」

title: 比特幣漲回 6.4 萬鎂沒有新錢進場！8.5 萬枚 BTC 沉睡，反彈全靠沒人賣
summary:
CryptoQuant 分析師 Axel Adler Jr. 今日發文指出，比特幣雖然反彈至 64,600 美 […]

〈比特幣漲回 6.4 萬鎂沒有新錢進場！8.5 萬枚 BTC 沉睡，反彈全靠沒人賣〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
CryptoQuant 分析師 Axel Adler Jr. 今日發文指出，比特幣雖然反彈至 64,600 美元，但兩項流量指標都沒有確認新需求進場。需求發行比率為 -5.43、幣齡淨流量為 -85,500 枚 BTC，雙雙從 7 月低點回升卻仍在負值區，前者已在零以下約五個月，後者更長達七個月。他的結論是這波反彈由供給老化與累積行為撐起來的，不是新資金推動，若沒有新需求進場，反彈可能會逐漸失去動力。
（前情提要：USDT 總市值 60 日大減 40 億鎂逼近歷史極值，比特幣面臨流動性不足問題）
（背景補充：比特幣交易所流入低於年均 24%！賣壓沒來，買盤也乾了）
重點摘要
- 需求發行比率 -5.43、幣齡淨流量 -85,500 枚 BTC，兩項指標仍在負值區。
- 過去 30 天有 8.55 萬枚 BTC 轉入一年以上持有，約當礦工 190 天的產量。
- 分析師稱需求發行比率要站上 1 才算真正復甦，目前距離還很遠。
比特幣漲回 6.4 萬美元，但買盤沒有跟上來。CryptoQuant 分析師 Axel Adler Jr. 今日發文，用兩項流量指標指出這波反彈的支撐並不是新錢。
第一項是需求發行比率，30 日讀數為 -5.43。第二項是幣齡淨流量，30 日總和為 -85,500 枚 BTC。兩項都從 7 月的低點明顯回升，需求發行比率當時一度接近 -16，幣齡淨流量則跌到接近 -22 萬枚。
回升幅度分別是 66% 與 61%，看起來不小。問題是起點太低，走了六成的路，兩項都還在零以下。
兩個指標在說什麼
先把術語翻成白話。需求發行比率比較的是「年輕幣的量」跟「礦工新挖出來的量」。這個數字低於零，代表年輕幣的萎縮速度比新發行還快，簡單說就是新進場的買盤連消化新產量都不夠。這個狀態已經持續約五個月。
幣齡淨流量算的是過去 30 天有多少 BTC 從短期持有跨進一年以上的長期持有類別。-85,500 枚的意思是，這個月有 8.55 萬枚比特幣沉了下去，按現價換算約 55 億美元。這項指標已經在負值區待了七個月，比前一項還久。
8.55 萬枚是什麼概念。比特幣目前每天新產出約 450 枚，8.55 萬枚等於礦工挖 190 天、超過六個月的總量。這些幣在一個月內全部轉進不太會動的口袋裡。
反彈是沒人賣撐出來的
Axel Adler Jr. 在文中寫得很直接，供給持續老化，其中的流動部分持續萎縮，價格是在供給老化與累積持續的情況下回升的，但沒有新資本流入。
若沒有新需求湧入，當前的反彈可能會逐漸失去動力。
換句話說，這波漲勢的來源不是有人積極買，而是願意賣的人變少了。籌碼被鎖住，掛單變薄，同樣的買量就能推高價格。這種漲法在流動性回來之前都是脆弱的。
他也給了兩道門檻。兩項指標回到零以上，算是第一個改善訊號；需求發行比率要持續站上 1，才能確認真正的復甦，因為那代表年輕幣的擴張速度終於超過新發行量。以 -5.43 的位置來看，這段距離還很長。
值得對照的是，這已經是近期第二份指向同一結論的鏈上分析。CryptoQuant 研究主管 Julio Moreno 昨日才指出 USDT 總市值 60 日內大減 40 億美元、逼近歷史極值，同樣認為比特幣面臨的是流動性不足。一個看穩定幣供給，一個看幣齡流量，兩個獨立指標得到同個答案。
最後補個，比特幣現報約 64,887 美元，過去 7 天漲 1.48%、30 天漲 2.93%，距離 126,080 美元的歷史高點仍有 48.5% 的差距。所謂反彈，得看是從哪裡開始算的。
常見問題
需求發行比率是什麼意思？
它比較年輕幣的量與礦工新發行量。低於零代表年輕幣萎縮速度超過新發行，也就是新買盤連消化新產量都不夠。分析師指出這項指標要持續高於 1，才能確認需求真正復甦。
幣齡淨流量為負代表什麼？
代表過去 30 天有大量比特幣從短期持有轉入一年以上的長期持有。本次讀數 -85,500 枚，約當礦工 190 天的產量，意味著流通中的可交易供給正在持續收縮。
*本文僅供參考，不構成投資建議。鏈上指標反映的是已發生的資金流向，不保證未來走勢，加密貨幣市場波動劇烈，投資前請審慎評估風險。*

title: Maicoin MAX 等交易所公告「虛幣轉帳超過3萬」需登記個資！用戶暫時無感
summary:
金管會 8 月 4 日公告虛擬資產轉帳規則（Travel Rule）分階段實施規劃後兩天，MAX 數位資產交易 […]

〈Maicoin MAX 等交易所公告「虛幣轉帳超過3萬」需登記個資！用戶暫時無感〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
金管會 8 月 4 日公告虛擬資產轉帳規則（Travel Rule）分階段實施規劃後兩天，MAX 數位資產交易所發出用戶公告，說明平台的準備進度。MAX 表示將依主管機關規範與時程進行系統建置及作業流程調整，並配合中華民國虛擬通貨商業同業公會推動境內業者間的技術對接，目前各項服務與操作流程維持不變，實際上線時間、適用範圍與所需資料將於確認後另行公告。
（前情提要：台灣虛擬貨幣轉帳「超過3萬」要登記生日住址！金管會 Travel Rule 十月上路）
（背景補充：銀行局長童政彰詳解《虛擬資產服務法》穩定幣監理藍圖：要穩更要「真正上路」）
重點摘要
- MAX 發出用戶公告，說明 Travel Rule 準備進度，目前操作流程維持不變。
- 第一階段預計 2026 年 10 月上路，適用境內業者間移轉，境外要等 2027 年底。
- 單筆逾新台幣 3 萬元須依身分類型提供額外資訊，實際欄位待各平台另行公告。
政策公告兩天後，交易所開始通知用戶了。MAX 數位資產交易所今日發出公告，說明金管會 8 月 4 日公布的虛擬資產轉帳規則（Travel Rule）分階段實施規劃，以及平台目前的準備狀況。
親愛的 MaiCoin 用戶您好，
金融監督管理委員會於 2026 年 8 月 4 日公告虛擬資產轉帳規則（Travel Rule）的分階段實施規劃。第一階段預計自 2026 年 10 月起，適用於臺灣境內虛擬資產服務商間的虛擬資產移轉；後續預計於 2027 年底前，進一步擴及臺灣境內與境外虛擬資產服務商間的移轉。
Travel Rule 實施後，用戶進行虛擬資產轉入或轉出時，平台將依相關規範取得、傳遞及核對轉出人與接收人的必要資訊。單筆移轉價值超過新臺幣 3 萬元時，則須依轉出人及接收人的身分類型，取得並核對額外資訊。
MaiCoin 將依主管機關規範與實施時程，持續進行相關系統建置及作業流程調整，並配合中華民國虛擬通貨商業同業公會推動境內業者間的技術對接。目前平台各項服務與操作流程維持不變，後續實際上線時間、適用範圍、所需資料及操作方式，將於確認後另行公告。
公告內容分成三塊，時程、資料要求、以及平台端的進度。時程與資料要求跟金管會的規劃一致，第一階段預計 2026 年 10 月起適用於台灣境內虛擬資產服務商之間的移轉，2027 年底前擴及境內與境外業者之間；用戶轉入或轉出時，平台會依規範取得、傳遞及核對轉出人與接收人的必要資訊，單筆移轉價值超過新台幣 3 萬元時，須依身分類型取得並核對額外資訊。
對用戶來說，最實際的一句是這個。
目前平台各項服務與操作流程維持不變，後續實際上線時間、適用範圍、所需資料及操作方式，將於確認後另行公告。
卡了五年的反洗規則
公告裡最值得注意的其實是這句，MAX 將配合中華民國虛擬通貨商業同業公會推動境內業者間的技術對接。
Travel Rule 並不是新規定。台灣早在 2021 年就把相關條文放進《提供虛擬資產服務之事業或人員防制洗錢及打擊資恐辦法》，但五年來一直沒有實際執行，金管會給出的原因包括各國法規不一致、資訊傳輸標準不統一，以及跨境系統整合困難。
這條規則要成立的前提是收付兩端的業者能互相通訊。只要對手方沒有相容的系統，資料就送不出去，法條寫得再細也是空的。所以 10 月能不能如期上路，真正的變數不在法規，而在八家業者的系統能不能接得起來。
公會 8 月 4 日的聲明也把自己的角色講得很清楚，將積極協助會員展開技術對接與流程優化，並擔任監理機關與業界之間的溝通橋樑，同時執行第一階段、為第二階段做準備。聲明還提到個別會員將各自公告實施細節，MAX 這份公告正是其中一家的動作。
而台灣其他合規交易所，先前也發出預告通知。如 BitoPro 預告之後會另行公告。
常見問題
MAX 用戶現在需要做什麼？
目前不需要任何動作。MAX 公告明確表示平台各項服務與操作流程維持不變，實際上線時間、適用範圍、所需資料及操作方式都會在確認後另行公告，屆時再依指示提供資訊即可。
Travel Rule 上路後轉帳會有什麼改變？
轉出或轉入虛擬資產時，平台會取得、傳遞及核對雙方必要資訊。單筆超過新台幣 3 萬元時須提供額外資訊，自然人為出生日期與住所地址，法人為官方識別碼與設立登記地址。

title: 香港爆 Fun Coffee 加密貨幣騙局！拋年利 222% 吸 USDT，報案損失破 1 億港元
summary:
標榜植根越南、要研發咖啡裝置與咖啡基因技術的投資專案 Fun Coffee，用 USDT 收錢、喊出年回報 1 […]

〈香港爆 Fun Coffee 加密貨幣騙局！拋年利 222% 吸 USDT，報案損失破 1 億港元〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
標榜植根越南、要研發咖啡裝置與咖啡基因技術的投資專案 Fun Coffee，用 USDT 收錢、喊出年回報 197% 到 278%，App 在 7 月 20 日突然停擺。香港警方指截至 8 月 5 日已收到 255 宗報案、涉案損失 1.04 億港元（約 1,333 萬美元），單一受害人最多賠掉 963 萬港元，港澳兩地共逮捕 8 人。
（前情提要：JPEX詐騙案新進展》15人提堂、8人列首案被告，網紅林作交30萬港元保釋後笑稱：牢房比家舒服）
（背景補充：幣想交易所為詐團洗錢！主謀施啟仁一審重判 22 年，金流超過 23 億元）
重點摘要
- 香港警方截至 8 月 5 日接獲 255 宗報案，涉案損失 1.04 億港元，單宗最高 963 萬港元
- 證監會 7 月 13 日已把該專案列為可疑投資產品，7 天後 App 就停止運作
- 報案金額只佔媒體估算的一成，多個投資群組合計約 4,000 人，多數尚未報案
根據香港媒體報導，聲稱研發多功能咖啡裝置與咖啡基因技術的越南投資專案 Fuu Coffee，用 USDT 向香港人收錢，喊出年回報率 197% 到 278%，然後在 7 月 20 日讓 App 直接停止運作。香港警方指出，截至 8 月 5 日傍晚已收到 255 宗報案，涉案損失達 1.04 億港元（約 1,333 萬美元），單一受害人最多賠掉 963 萬港元，當事人 51 歲。
Fun Coffee 在 2025 年底進軍香港，港澳警方聯手行動後，香港逮捕 6 名男女、包括公司董事與股東，全部准予保釋候查，澳門司法警察局另外逮捕 2 名女子。澳門的報案損失約 360 萬澳門元。
平均年化報酬 222% 吸金
Fun Coffee 設計了「啟航」「成長」「遠航」三級方案，投資金額越高、鎖倉時間越長，宣稱回報越高，另外還有入金獎勵、推薦獎勵與每日簽到。
以「成長」方案為例，投入 10,800 個 USDT（約 8.4 萬港元），10 天後聲稱可拿到 680 個 USDT（約 5,300 港元）。被廣泛引用的版本是 2,800 美元投資 42 天賺 717 美元，換算年化 222%。
問題在於，這種報酬率如果真的複投，本金一年會滾成 7 倍以上。世界上沒有任何咖啡生意做得到這件事，能夠持續付出這種數字的方法只有一種，就是拿後面進來的錢付給前面的人。
以反詐騙之名行詐騙
Fun Coffee 在香港的推廣手法相當高調，它辦投資簡介會與社交聚會、鼓勵成員介紹親友換取獎金，2025 年 12 月底在西九辦跑步活動、還找來藝人主持撐場面。該名藝人事後發宣告澄清，主持稿件全部以馬拉松賽事為主，沒有涉及任何公司產品介紹或促銷成分，警方則表示會聯絡受害人及相關人士協助調查。
Fun Coffee 更曾經到香港各區派發傳單，宣傳的主題是反詐騙。
香港證監會 7 月 13 日就把「Fun Coffee GCM 專案」列入可疑投資產品名單，公開警告投資人可能血本無歸。App 在 7 天後的 7 月 20 日停止運作。已經把錢押進去的人拿不回資金。
*本文僅供參考，不構成投資建議。加密貨幣市場波動劇烈，投資前請審慎評估風險。文中所述案件均為警方偵辦中的指控，相關人士尚未經法院認定有罪。*
常見問題
Fun Coffee 是什麼樣的騙局？
它聲稱是植根越南的咖啡裝置與咖啡基因技術投資專案，要求投資人下載 App、以 USDT 轉入指定錢包，宣稱年回報 197% 到 278%。App 於 2026 年 7 月 20 日停止運作，投資人無法提領。
香港警方目前掌握的損失金額是多少？
截至 2026 年 8 月 5 日為 255 宗報案、1.04 億港元，單宗最高 963 萬港元。澳門另有 9 宗、約 360 萬澳門元。港澳兩地共逮捕 8 人，媒體估算實際規模約 10 億港元。

title: 香港第二批穩定幣牌照傳10月落地！金管局按兵不動，首批兩家還沒發幣
summary:
市場傳出香港第二批穩定幣發行商牌照可能在國慶前後落地，香港金融管理局發言人今日回函《財聯社》表示不評論市場傳聞 […]

〈香港第二批穩定幣牌照傳10月落地！金管局按兵不動，首批兩家還沒發幣〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
市場傳出香港第二批穩定幣發行商牌照可能在國慶前後落地，香港金融管理局發言人今日回函《財聯社》表示不評論市場傳聞，但對是否增發牌照與時間安排「持開放而謹慎的態度，現階段未有明確傾向」。金管局強調目前工作重點是推進兩家持牌發行商完成業務準備，等它們成功發行合規穩定幣後，再觀察應用場景落地、營運成效與市場反應。而首批牌照 4 月 10 日發出至今將滿四個月，兩家持牌機構一枚合規穩定幣都還沒正式上市。
（前情提要：滙豐、渣打拿下香港首批穩定幣牌照！渣打走合資路線、聯手 HKT 與 Animoca）
（背景補充：香港首批合規穩定幣下半年登場！財庫局：今年將提交「虛資全面規管法案」，防範銀行資金外流）
重點摘要
- 金管局回應第二批牌照傳聞，稱持開放而謹慎態度、現階段未有明確傾向。
- 首批牌照 4 月 10 日發出，36 家申請只給 2 張，落在滙豐與渣打系的 Anchorpoint。
- 渣打系穩定幣 HKDAP 已從第二季延到 7 月底、再延到 8 月，尚未正式上市。
香港金管局今日回函《財聯社》，正面回應了近期市場流傳的「第二批穩定幣發行商牌照可能於國慶前後落地」說法。發言人表示不對市場傳聞做出評論，但對是否增發牌照以及時間安排，金管局「持開放而謹慎的態度，現階段未有明確傾向」。
這裡的國慶日指的是 10 月 1 日中國國慶，香港每年這天放假。
香港金管局發言人說，目前的工作重點是推進兩家持牌穩定幣發行商開展業務準備，並在其成功發行合規穩定幣後，觀察相關應用場景落地、營運成效以及市場反應等情況。至於未來是否增發牌照，需要綜合考慮申請是否符合發牌要求、市場對穩定幣的需求、實際應用情況，以及國際層面的發展趨勢和監管討論。
金管局要觀察的東西「還沒實際跑」
這段回應裡最關鍵的是「在其成功發行合規穩定幣後」這個前提。金管局等於明說，第二批的門要不要開，取決於第一批發得出來、而且發得夠好。
問題是第一批到現在還沒發出來。金管局 4 月 10 日發出首批兩張穩定幣發行人牌照，一張給碇點金融科技（Anchorpoint Financial Technology），一張給香港上海滙豐銀行。當時共有 36 家機構遞件，最後只有 2 家過關，兩家都有銀行背景，也都參與過金管局的央行數位貨幣與代幣化存款測試計畫。36 砍到 2，這個比例本身就是金管局風格的答案。
碇點是渣打銀行（香港）持股逾五成、聯手香港電訊 HKT 與 Animoca Brands 在 2025 年 8 月成立的合資公司，要發的港元穩定幣叫 HKDAP。滙豐則計畫在下半年推出港元穩定幣，接進 PayMe 與手機銀行 App 兩個既有入口。
HKDAP 連兩次跳票
碇點原本喊的是第二季推出 HKDAP，第二季過完沒動靜。7 月中旬香港媒體再傳最快 7 月底上線，OSL 與 HashKey 可望擔任分銷商，7 月底也過了。目前渣打方面的說法是 HKDAP 將在 8 月宣布，碇點正在推進區塊鏈測試、敲定分銷網路。
HKDAP 走的是 B2B2C 模式，不直接發給散戶，而是透過核可的合作夥伴分銷，主打跨境結算與代幣化資產。每一枚由 1 港元現金或港府債券、外匯基金票據這類高流動性低風險港元資產支持，由渣打的信託子公司獨立託管，支援 T+0（當日即時）贖回。
四個變數決定第二批什麼時候開
金管局這次把評估條件列得比以往清楚，可以直接當成後續的追蹤清單。
- 申請是否符合發牌要求，這是門檻題，36 選 2 已經示範過標準有多緊
- 市場對穩定幣的實際需求，看的是有沒有企業真的拿去做跨境結算
- 實際應用情況，也就是首批兩家上線後的場景落地成績
- 國際層面的發展趨勢和監管討論，包括美國 GENIUS 法案與歐盟 MiCA 的執行進度
《穩定幣條例》2025 年 8 月 1 日生效，到本月剛好滿一週年。這一年裡香港把制度、牌照、託管與贖回規則都架好了，唯獨還缺真的在市場上流通的合規港元穩定幣。
常見問題
香港第二批穩定幣牌照什麼時候發？
目前沒有時間表。市場傳可能在 10 月 1 日中國國慶前後落地，但金管局回應稱對是否增發牌照與時間安排持開放而謹慎態度，現階段未有明確傾向，要先看首批兩家發行後的營運成效與市場反應。
香港首批穩定幣牌照發給了誰？
金管局 2026 年 4 月 10 日發出兩張，分別給渣打香港、HKT 與 Animoca Brands 合資的碇點金融科技（Anchorpoint），以及香港上海滙豐銀行。當時共 36 家機構遞件申請，通過率不到 6%。

title: 孫宇晨身價超車前中國首富王健林！7年前被王思聰笑傻逼，如今冷回：心無波瀾
summary:
富比士即時富豪榜今日顯示，波場 TRON 創辦人孫宇晨（Justin Sun）身家來到 85 億美元、全球第 […]

〈孫宇晨身價超車前中國首富王健林！7年前被王思聰笑傻逼，如今冷回：心無波瀾〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
富比士即時富豪榜今日顯示，波場 TRON 創辦人孫宇晨（Justin Sun）身家來到 85 億美元、全球第 435 名，正式超越萬達集團董事長王健林的 44 億美元（全球第 973 名）。孫宇晨隨後在 X 發文回應「沒有波瀾，只有警醒」，稱王健林當年也曾是版本之神，並直接點名王思聰，說自己「很難再有王思聰這種自信」。
（前情提要：年賺 950 萬鎂「睡後收入」！孫宇晨再向 Lido 存入 13,000 枚 ETH，stETH 持倉飆破 4.3 億美元）
（背景補充：孫宇晨從亞軌道太空返回地球，刷新華人宇宙飛行紀錄）
重點摘要
- 富比士即時榜：孫宇晨 85 億美元排全球 435 名，王健林 44 億美元排 973 名。
- 孫宇晨發文稱「傲慢永遠是最先被清算的資產」，並自比當年不被相信的年輕人。
- 2019 年王思聰曾轉發批評文並留言「這不就是個傻逼」，孫宇晨當時反嗆靠爹。
富比士即時富豪榜今日刷新數字。波場 TRON 創辦人孫宇晨（Justin Sun）身家 85 億美元，全球排名第 435 位，36 歲，財富來源標註為「加密貨幣，白手起家」。
萬達集團董事長王健林 44 億美元，全球第 973 位，71 歲，財富來源是房地產。從萬達集團全盛時期到如今帝國崩塌，王健林身家的確縮水了 10 倍。讓新一代的孫宇晨超車趕過。
不少網友討論此事，認為這是種「世代復仇」，畢竟王建林的兒子王思聰，號稱中國第一富少，曾經在微博上嘲諷孫宇晨。
孫宇晨隨後在 X 上發了標題為「一代版本一代神」的貼文回應這件事，全文語氣跟他過去的風格差距不小。
看到富比士榜單上位次互換，我心裡沒有波瀾，只有警醒。王健林當年也曾是版本之神，正如我曾是不被相信的年輕人。版本更迭最殘酷之處，是身處巔峰的人總是最後察覺。我憑什麼是例外？
所以今天若有個年輕人對我講一些我聽不懂、甚至想嘲笑的東西，我很難再有王思聰這種自信。我會給他端一杯茶，聽他講講他的世界。因為傲慢是永遠是最先被清算的資產。我們永遠無法預知未來，但是相信年輕人，永遠是沒錯的。
七年前被王思聰酸爆
要看懂這篇貼文為什麼點名王思聰，得回到 2019 年。
那年孫宇晨以 456 萬美元標下巴菲特慈善午餐，創下該拍賣歷年最高價。消息傳開後，一篇題為《孫宇晨巴菲特的餐桌上，全是「韭菜」》的文章在中國社群流傳，王思聰轉發時只留下一句評語，「這不就是個傻逼」。
2019 年王思聰轉發批評孫宇晨的文章並留言 | 圖片來源：微博截圖
孫宇晨當時的回應完全不是端茶那一套。他連發三條微博反嗆，其中最廣為流傳的一句是「靠爹的還敢罵靠自己的，80 後還敢罵 90 後，搞個直播就倒閉的敢罵還在創業的，誰給你的勇氣，梁靜茹嗎？」
七年前他罵王思聰靠爹，七年後他拿王思聰當傲慢的代名詞，孫真的是辯才無礙。
順帶一提，那頓午餐最後沒吃成。2019 年 7 月 23 日孫宇晨宣布因故取消，成為巴菲特慈善午餐自 2000 年開辦以來第一次被取消的紀錄。
王健林高處不勝寒
孫宇晨說「身處巔峰的人總是最後察覺」，這句話放在王健林身上真的是很貼切。
王健林曾是亞洲首富，2015 年前後萬達的擴張速度是中國民營企業的標竿。富比士的個人頁面現在這樣描述他，近年來透過大規模出售資產顯著縮減了投資組合。從亞洲第一到全球第 973 名，中間是連續賣掉的萬達廣場、酒店與海外影視資產。
值得注意的是兩人資產的形態差異。孫宇晨的身家主要押在流動性代幣上，這代表這個數字每天都在跳動，富比士的即時榜也註明數據反映的是前一交易日下午 5 點以來的變化。王健林的 44 億美元則綁在商業地產裡，跌得慢，但要變回現金也慢。
換句話說，今天這個超越是即時榜上的瞬間，不是永遠的定局。孫宇晨自己顯然也清楚這點，所以他還是「稍微謙虛」寫了自己需要警醒而不是慶功。
去過太空版的孫宇晨
如果把這篇貼文跟 2019 年那三條微博一起看，孫宇晨最明顯的變化不是身家，是他的語氣。
孫宇晨現在的 X 顯示名稱是「孫宇晨（去過太空版）」，他把那趟出大氣層的飛行當成自己更新了版本。
2021 年他以 2,800 萬美元標下藍色起源首航席位，等了四年，直到 2025 年 8 月 3 日才真正搭上 New Shepard NS-34 從德州升空，全程 10 分 14 秒，成為最年輕的華人商業太空人。當年那筆競標金額，他全數捐給了藍色起源的 Club for the Future，用於全球青少年的 STEM 教育。
把時間軸拉開來看，2019 年的孫宇晨在意的是「誰給你的勇氣」，2026 年的他在意的是「我憑什麼是例外」。從次軌道往下看一次地球，人對自己在座標系裡的位置大概真的會改觀。這是他對外的敘事新路線，也是他最擅長的行銷包裝，但這次的敘事至少往謙遜的方向長。
貼文最後他自己加了一行註腳，《孫學》+1，還是那個熟悉的孫哥。
常見問題
孫宇晨的身家是怎麼算出來的？
富比士即時榜將他的 85 億美元列為「加密貨幣，白手起家」，資產主要是流動性代幣，因此數字每日隨幣價波動，榜單註明反映前一交易日下午 5 點以來的變化，並不是經審計的結算值。
王思聰和孫宇晨之間發生過什麼？
2019 年孫宇晨以 456 萬美元標下巴菲特午餐後，王思聰轉發批評文章並留言「這不就是個傻逼」，孫宇晨連發三條微博反嗆對方靠爹。該場午餐最終在 2019 年 7 月 23 日被取消。

title: 只剩 2 天！美國《CLARITY 法案》能否過關？「這 3 大劇本」一次看懂
summary:
美國加密貨幣市場結構法案《 CLARITY 法案 》迎來關鍵倒數，距離夏季休會僅剩 2 個工作日，參院卻仍未表態是否審議法案，也尚未排定任何表決時程，《CLARITY 法案》能否在今年內完成立法？目前看來，變數依然不少。

〈只剩 2 天！美國《CLARITY 法案》能否過關？「這 3 大劇本」一次看懂〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
美國加密貨幣市場結構法案 《CLARITY 法案》迎來關鍵倒數，距離夏季休會僅剩 2 個工作日，參院卻仍未表態是否審議法案，也尚未排定任何表決時程，《數位資產市場明晰法案（CLARITY 法案（）》能否在今年內完成立法？目前看來，變數依然不少。
參議院原定 8 月 7 日休會，但可能延長會期至下周，理論上仍有時間進行程序性投票，甚至完成全院表決後送交眾議院。
然而，若周五如期休會，9 月復會後也僅剩 14 個工作日，何況屆時還得面對政府撥款、俄羅斯制裁案等其他優先議題，要擠出時間推動《CLARITY 法案》難度不低。換言之，2026 年這扇門很可能會就此關上。
爭議條文
目前，《CLARITY 法案》部分內容仍持續協商中。根據一名國會幕僚向《CoinDesk》表示，涉及打擊非法金融活動、農業相關規範，以及政府高層利益衝突等內容，目前仍未取得共識。
其中，最受矚目的爭議非「倫理條款」莫屬，這主要是為了禁止包括美國總統川普（Donald Trump）在內的高階政府官員，利用職務之便透過加密貨幣產業牟利。
共和黨參議員 Thom Tillis 與民主黨參議員 Ruben Gallego 上周已將「倫理條款」修正方案送交白宮。若白宮接受提案，或提出可讓雙方接受的修訂版本，將有望爭取更多民主黨議員支持，提升法案過關機率。
根據《Punchbowl News》記者 Brendan Pedersen 引述 Thom Tillis 的說法稱，白宮是否點頭放行或提出修改意見，將是牽動民主黨議員投票意向的絕對關鍵。據報導， Thom Tillis 周三向媒體證實，白宮已開始針對該提案與團隊進行討論。
參院議程塞滿，《CLARITY 法案》恐遭排擠
除了《CLARITY 法案》，美國參議院近期仍有多項重大法案等待處理，包括：處理布蘭奇（Todd Blanche）的司法部長提名案、維持聯邦政府運作的臨時撥款法案，以及俄羅斯制裁法案與大學體育法案。
在有限議程下，《CLARITY 法案》是否能排入表決時程，仍充滿變數。目前市場關注的焦點，落在參院多數黨領袖 John Thune 是否提出終止辯論程序（Cloture）。
在美國參議院制度下，提出終止辯論程序後，必須等待完整一天才能進行首次程序性表決，且需取得至少 60 票支持，才能終止冗長辯論並推進法案正式審議。
若參院仍按原定計畫在 8 月 7 日休會，則周三晚間幾乎就是提出終止辯論程序的最後時機。
不過，也存在另一種可能：John Thune 可在周四宣布延長本周議程，讓參院持續開會至週末、甚至延至下周，替《CLARITY 法案》爭取更多審議時間。
《CLARITY 法案》3 種劇本
情境一：休會前完成首次程序表決
若 John Thune 本周提出並先完成其他優先議程，參院最快可於周五晚間完成首次程序性投票。完成程序後，議員仍可依原定計畫返回選區，展開期中選舉造勢。
情境二：休會、不表決，9 月再戰
另一種可能是參議院直接在 8 月 7 日休會，不再推動《CLARITY 法案》，讓法案延至 9 月復會後重新排入議程。
然而，9 、 10 月參院合計僅有約 14 個工作天，還必須優先處理政府預算等重大議題，因此法案推進難度將大幅提高。
不過，國會幕僚認為，只要目前幾項爭議條文能順利取得共識，法案仍有相當很高機率能在 9 月完成表決。
情境三：參院延長會期
另一個越來越受到關注的可能性，則是參院延長本周會期。由於 Todd Blanche 的司法部長提名案仍未完成審議，市場預期參院可能繼續開會數日。
若真如此，John Thune 仍有足夠時間提出《CLARITY 法案》的程序動議，等待一天後進行首次程序性投票。目前，John Thune 雖已就 Ted Cruz 主導的大學體育法案提出終止辯論動議，但尚未正式啟動相關程序，因此仍保有調整議程、改推《CLARITY 法案》的空間。
若《CLARITY 法案》首次程序投票未能取得 60 票支持，法案很可能將一路延後至美國期中選舉結束後才有機會重啟。
屆時，加密貨幣監管立法的命運，將取決於選後國會版圖是否改變，包括兩黨是否取得參、眾兩院多數席次，以及雙方席次差距。
《CLARITY 法案》被視為美國近年最重要的加密貨幣市場結構法案，目的在於為數位資產建立監管框架，釐清美國證管會（SEC）與商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）的監管權限，為交易平台、發行人與投資人提供更明確的法規環境。
目前尚無法確定《CLARITY 法案》能否趕在夏季休會前取得突破，但未來幾天的程序安排，將直接決定法案能否在今年內完成立法。

title: Majority of England's rivers and lakes fail new environmental review
summary: A comprehensive assessment of England's waterways is the first in six years and shows little improvement.
full_text:
Majority of England's rivers and lakes fail new environmental review
- Published
England's rivers, lakes and coastal waters remain in a challenging state with only around one in seven classed as being in good ecological condition, according to the first comprehensive assessment of their health in six years.
Data from the Environment Agency shows that while 15% of rivers are classed as good, fewer than 7% of lakes reached that level. No single waterway passed a separate test for chemical pollution.
The biggest individual problem is phosphate - a nutrient from sewage and farm runoff - with around half of rivers still exceeding safe levels.
Despite a record £22bn earmarked for water company environmental improvements by 2030, the overall picture has changed little since 2019.
- How much sewage is spilled near you? 
  - Published26 March
- UK's biggest ever environmental pollution claim reaches High Court 
  - Published27 April
The government is already on course to miss its legally binding target of restoring 77% of England's waters to good ecological status by 2027 - a goal the environmental watchdog, the Office for Environmental Protection, has warned will be missed by a "considerable margin".
It's now investigating both the government and the Environment Agency over possible rule breaches.
Environment Secretary Angela Eagle said the figures "underline the need for wholesale change across the water sector".
She pointed to new laws the government has introduced to hold water companies to account and record investment. "We will drive forward a system that puts the public interest first," she said.
Much of the debate about the state of England's waters has centred on water companies and the sewage they release into rivers.
But campaigners and scientists also point to agriculture as an equally large source of pollution - one that attracts far less public attention.
Erica Popplewell, of the campaign group River Action, said some farming, particularly intensive poultry units - vast sheds housing hundreds of thousands of birds - were a growing threat to rivers such as the Wye and Severn.
"There's a lot of poo that comes out of the chickens," she said. "If it goes straight into a river, it causes eutrophication. The whole ecology of the river is damaged, and the river is dying." She called on the government to tackle sewage and farming "with the same urgency".
The National Farmers' Union of England and Wales has been approached for comment.
Other types of pollution affecting England's bodies of water, the Environment Agency pointed to, include petrol, garden pesticides and contaminated water running off roads picking up microplastics.
The Environment Agency stressed that this year's data could not be directly compared with 2019 because it had changed its methods.
In particular, it said the steep fall in the number of lakes ranked as good - down about half from 2019 - largely reflected a change in how its experts now assess them, rather than a genuine decline in their condition.
Its chair, Alan Lovell, acknowledged too many water bodies were "still not achieving the standards we want to see", adding that the agency was "transforming our enforcement work" with its largest ever workforce.
But Prof Penny Johnes, a leading water quality scientist at the University of Bristol, told BBC News the true picture was almost certainly worse than the classifications suggested.
The scheme was "not fit for purpose", she said, measuring too few pollutants too infrequently, and missing nitrogen and other substances scientists have long understood to be driving rivers' decline.
The findings come as much of England sits in official drought, with rivers running low and more than 20 million people facing hosepipe bans.
Lower flows can concentrate the very pollution the new data is designed to track, leaving fish and other aquatic life exposed to more dangerous levels.
Climate change is expected to bring drier and hotter summers which could further exacerbate this issue.
Asked directly whether England's waters were healthier than six or seven years ago, Prof Johnes said: "No, definitely not."
Chemicals building up
Every river and lake failed the test for chemical pollution.
The Environment Agency said this is because legacy substances, such as heavy metals from mining, take decades to break down, and some are building up.
But Prof Johnes said it was also a "failure to regulate effectively" the new chemicals entering rivers, from antibiotics to the "forever chemicals" known as PFAS - many not routinely monitored.
There are currently 23 enforcement notices against water companies requiring them to lower the levels of PFAS to reduce the danger to human health.
Water UK, which represents the water companies, has called for PFAS use to be banned to limit their build-up and reduce water treatment costs, but the chemicals are currently used in thousands of products, from school uniforms to medical devices.
It said it was spending record amounts of money on improving the country's waterways.
"Water companies are investing £22bn in environmental improvements by 2030. This will help to secure our water supplies, support economic growth and end sewage entering our rivers and seas."
The Environment Agency also noted that other European countries are doing even worse in terms of the good health of their waterways, with only 8% in Germany and just 1% in the Netherlands.
But Prof Johnes said such a comparison is misleading, because of varying methodologies across nations.

title: Meredith Kercher's sister criticises Amanda Knox's Edinburgh comedy show
summary: Stephanie Kercher asks Amanda Knox to think about Meredith's family ahead of staging a show in Edinburgh.
full_text:
Meredith Kercher's sister criticises Amanda Knox comedy show
- Published
The sister of Meredith Kercher has criticised a solo comedy show by Amanda Knox, who was convicted and later acquitted of murdering the British student in Italy in 2007.
The Edinburgh Festival Fringe website says Knox's show, Cartwheel, is about motherhood and how she will explain what happened in Perugia to her daughter.
Stephanie Kercher, addressing Knox directly on BBC Breakfast, said: "What I would say [to Knox] is to think about the family here, think about her friends and to turn the tables if it was your sister that this had happened to, because I know you have a sister as well."
A spokesperson for Knox said the show, set to run over 11 days from Friday, honours Kercher's memory.
Her comedy show's title Cartwheel references a story that once claimed she did cartwheels in the police station after her friend's death.
Knox told the Telegraph newspaper, external last week: "I don't joke about Meredith's death. I joke a lot about how I was vilified, but I don't joke about her murder."
Asked if Meredith Kercher would have found her comedy funny, she added: "Yeah, I think so. I mean, it is funny!".
Responding to that suggestion, Stephanie Kercher told the BBC: "Meredith absolutely wouldn't find these topics of any comedy value."
She said: "Our family's pain is immense. I can't explain to you how much pain our family have been through, and also we're talking two decades later now, this pain."
A petition against the show, set up by a friend of Meredith, has been signed by just over 2,400 people, and says the show disrespects her memory and also risks normalising violence against women by making light of such a harrowing event.
Referencing the petition, Stephanie Kercher told BBC Breakfast: "It's not just our family that feels this pain, and I do think this is something that needs to be looked at, because it sets a precedent for anyone else to do a show like this."
She urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to explore the issue and said she would like to meet him.
"I think that if it was a generic theme, as many comedy shows are, even when they're pushing the boundaries, it would be different," she added.
"Because this is associated with an individual case and individual person, I think that's where the worry lies here for me, because who else is this going to then open up this opportunity for."
The venue for the show next week, the Gilded Balloon Teviot, said Edinburgh Festival Fringe provides a platform for a wide range of voices in line with the commitment to freedom of expression.
Since Meredith Kercher's death, Knox has written two books about her imprisonment and served as an executive producer on the biographical drama The Twisted Tale of Amanda Knox.
Now 39, she is married with two children and lives in Washington state.
Knox, from Seattle in the US, and Meredith Kercher, from Surrey in the UK, were both language exchange students sharing a house in the university town of Perugia.
Alongside her then-boyfriend, Raffaele Sollecito, Knox was arrested on suspicion of murdering Kercher, 21, who was found dead in their house. Her throat had been cut and she had been sexually assaulted.
After being found guilty, Knox served four years in an Italian prison before she and Sollecito were acquitted through an appeal. She returned home to the US in 2011.
A retrial in 2014 reinstated Knox and Sollecito's convictions but Italy's top appeals court finally overturned their convictions in 2015.
Ivory Coast-born Rudy Guede served 13 years of a 16-year sentence for Kercher's murder after his fingerprints were found at the scene.
The court ruled that he did not act alone, but after Knox and Sollecito were acquitted no other accomplices were convicted.

title: Farmer jailed for lodger's 'body in barrel' murder
summary: Richard Dyson's body was not found until nearly six years after he disappeared in rural Hoyland.
full_text:
Farmer jailed for lodger's 'body in barrel' murder
- Published
A farmer who shot his lodger and dismembered his body has been jailed for 35 years.
Richard Dyson, 55, disappeared in November 2019, but his remains, kept inside a concrete-filled barrel in a trailer on a farm near Barnsley, were not discovered for nearly six years.
A trial at Sheffield Crown Court heard how Christopher Wright killed Dyson when he tried to steal a gun from him before disposing of the body with the help of his childhood friend Karl Schwalbe.
Last month, Wright, 73, was convicted of murder and Schwalbe, 72, was found guilty of perverting the course of justice.
Wright, a former butcher, was also found guilty of conspiracy to pervert the justice, preventing a lawful burial and six firearms offences.
Schwalbe was jailed for three years for perverting the course of justice.
Bethany Dainty, Dyson's daughter, said her life had become a "living nightmare".
She had issued numerous appeals for help tracing her father in the years he was missing.
In a victim impact statement read to the court, she said: "Someone watched me suffering for years and said nothing. That level of cruelty is impossible for me to understand."

title: Raleigh owner starts insolvency proceedings
summary: Accell, based in the Netherlands, has owned the famous bike brand since 2012.
full_text:
Raleigh owner starts insolvency proceedings
- Published
The company that owns iconic Nottingham bike manufacturer Raleigh has begun insolvency proceedings.
Accell, based in the Netherlands, bought Raleigh for $100m in 2012 but said on Wednesday it had "exhausted all the available options" and was "no longer able to meet its financial obligations".
It comes after a difficult period for Raleigh, which saw redundancies in 2024 and losses of £30m in accounts released the following year.
Jonas Nilsson, chief executive of Accell, said it was "a deeply sad and frustrating situation".
Raleigh was founded in Nottingham in 1887 and at one stage was the biggest bicycle maker in the world, employing about 8,000 people at its peak.
It stopped making bikes in the city decades ago, and in 2024 it vacated its headquarters on Church Street in Eastwood to move to new premises less than a mile away.
Announcing plans to initiate insolvency proceedings, Nilsson said Accell had worked "to restructure [its] operations and finances".
"Every realistic option for the future of the business has been tirelessly explored, and none have resulted in a solution to continue the group in its current form," he said.
"Our immediate focus is to support an orderly process, provide clarity wherever possible, and work with the relevant court-appointed administrators to preserve viable activities and employment where circumstances allow."

title: England recall Pope & Lawrence for Pakistan Tests but Bethell out
summary: Surrey duo Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence are recalled to the England squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan.
full_text:
England recall Pope and Lawrence for Pakistan Tests
- Published
Surrey duo Ollie Pope and Dan Lawrence have been recalled to the England squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan.
The pair have been named in a 16-man squad before the series opener at Headingley on Wednesday 19 August but Jacob Bethell will miss the entire series through injury, with Jordan Cox to be promoted to number three.
The three-match series marks England's first Test outing since the retirement of captain Ben Stokes and sacking of head coach Brendon McCullum.
Joe Root will captain the side for the first time since being reappointed to the role in July, with Marcus Trescothick serving as interim head coach. McCullum's replacement, Stephen Fleming, will begin his tenure against South Africa in December.
———————————————————
England's 16-man squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan: Joe Root (c), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Shoaib Bashir, Harry Brook, Brydon Carse, Sam Cook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Matthew Fisher, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Ollie Pope, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue.
———————————————————
Lawrence, who earned the last of his 14 Test caps in September 2024, is rewarded for his domestic form. The 29-year-old is the second-highest run-scorer in Division One of the County Championship, with 788 runs at 65.66, including five centuries, in 13 innings.
He is slated to bat at six, filling a middle-order vacancy created by Stokes' retirement, but is far from a like-for-like replacement for the former captain.
Only Gus Atkinson (79 wickets) has taken more Test wickets for England than Stokes (78) since the start of June 2022. Lawrence, who bowls right-arm off-spin, has taken nine wickets from 178.2 overs in the County Championship this season.
Former vice-captain Pope was replaced by Bethell at number three for the final two Ashes Tests in Australia following an extended period of poor form and was subsequently dropped from the squad against New Zealand.
Like Lawrence, he has performed well in the County Championship, scoring 510 runs at 56.66, including five 50+ knocks, for Surrey, but will not automatically slot back into the side in Bethell's absence.
Bethell suffered a knee injury during the ODI series against India in July and is set to be replaced by Cox, who made his Test debut against New Zealand at The Oval.
England's men's national selector, Marcus North, said: "We have selected a squad for the first two Tests that balances rising talent with the experience needed against a quality Pakistan team.
"Dan Lawrence returns following an exceptional season so far with Surrey and we believe he has the right level of experience, maturity and skill to complement our middle order.
"Jordan Cox is well regarded as one of the most exciting talents in English cricket and will have the opportunity to bat at three in place of Jacob Bethell, who sadly misses this series through injury."
Essex's Sam Cook returns to the squad for the first time since last summer. The 29-year-old seamer made his international debut against Zimbabwe in May 2025 and was named in the squad for the five-match series against India but did not feature.
Brydon Carse returns after a broken wrist ruled him out of the Indian Premier League and the start of the Test summer while England are sticking with spinner Shoaib Bashir, who featured in the first and third Tests against New Zealand after being overlooked during the Ashes.
'No brave new world for England'
Analysis by BBC cricket reporter Henry Moeran
For those who were hoping for a brave new world, there may be disappointment. This is a squad with plenty of familiar faces and no potential debutants.
Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse return for the first time since the Ashes and Dan Lawrence is selected two years on from his last Test appearance
The big question was who was going to replace Ben Stokes as the all-rounder but that much isn't entirely obvious.
There is no place for Sam Curran, James Coles or Rehan Ahmed, who is dropped, which means Lawrence, if selected, might find his part-time spin plays a significant role.

title: Who was Cesar Gastelum, Mexican TikToker shot dead mid-livestream?
summary: Gastelum's death comes after the killing of TikToker Valeria Marquez last year.
full_text:
Who was Cesar Gastelum, Mexican TikToker shot dead mid-livestream?
Gastelum’s death comes after the killing of TikToker Valeria Marquez last year.
Mexican influencer shot dead during livestream
A popular Mexican TikTok influencer has been shot dead by men on a motorbike near the northern city of Culiacan while he was livestreaming an event for his followers.
Culiacan is at the heart of ongoing violence between factions vying for control of the city. Mexican media have reported that at least 12 social media influencers have been killed in Culiacan since September 2024.
The latest incident follows other similar killings, including that of beauty influencer Valeria Marquez in the western state of Jalisco in May 2025.
Here is what we know so far.
Who was Cesar Gastelum?
Gastelum, 24, was a Mexican social media influencer who created comedy and lifestyle content, primarily on the social media platform TikTok.
Gastelum’s TikTok account, which last posted a video on Sunday, has more than 700,000 followers on his TikTok account.
What happened to him?
Gastelum was filming a regular livestream for his followers from a KFC car park in Tres Rios, Culiacan, northern Mexico, with two of his friends on Tuesday.
At about 8:15pm local time (2:15 am GMT), in the middle of the livestream, Gastelum was shot dead by men who approached on a motorbike, Mexican media reported.
The three men were wearing bright orange clothes and carrying delivery bags in the livestream, typically worn by drivers. This reportedly led the police to initially believe that Gastelum was a delivery driver.
A video of the moment of Gastelum’s death, seen by news agencies, shows him laughing with two other men in the car park when two men wearing helmets pull up on a motorcycle. One is seen pulling out a gun and shooting at Gastelum. The attackers then flee the scene.
The shooting took place close to the local prosecutor’s office.
The two men with Gastelum during the livestream were unharmed in the attack, local media reported.
What do we know about the motive for this killing?
So far, the authorities have not reported any arrests or assigned any motive behind Gastelum’s killing.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum told reporters on Wednesday that authorities are investigating the case.
“The actual perpetrators – and, if applicable, the mastermind – must be arrested, and the reason behind this tragic homicide must be uncovered,” she said during the morning news conference.
Mexico’s Federal Security Cabinet released a statement on X on Wednesday saying it was analysing various social media posts by Gastelum. The statement added that some of these posts made reference to a faction in a criminal group, but did not name the faction or criminal group, or provide further details.
Additionally, the Security Cabinet is assessing surveillance camera footage as part of the investigation.
The cabinet said that it is conducting the investigation alongside the attorney general’s office of the State of Sinaloa.
Sinaloa has suffered a severe internal turf war between rival factions of the Sinaloa cartel following the July 2024 arrest of cofounder Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, which has left a power vacuum.
In one of Gastelum’s social media posts, he can be seen at the grave of Leobardo Aispuro, or “El Gordo Peruci”, an influencer who was shot dead in December 2024.
Police said his killing may have been linked to violence between warring factions of the Sinaloa cartel.
Have other similar incidents taken place in Mexico?
Aispuro, or “El Gordo Peruci”, was a social media influencer who was shot dead in December 2024. Police said his killing may have been linked to cartel violence.
In May 2025, Mexican beauty influencer Valeria Marquez, 23, was shot dead also during a TikTok livestream at the salon where she worked in Zapopan, in the western state of Jalisco. A man had entered the salon and opened fire, according to prosecutors.
Her death was investigated under Mexico’s femicide protocols.
In July, Mexican authorities announced the arrest in Jalisco of Ramon Angel Alvarez Ayala, known as “El R-1” whom Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch identified as the leader of a criminal cell linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).
Authorities have linked Alvarez Ayala to the killing of Marquez and accused him of ordering and financing the November 2025 murder of Uruapan Mayor Carlos Manzo.

title: What the CJP protests reveal about India’s next generation
summary: The politics of aspiration is reshaping Generation Z worldwide, and India may still have an opportunity to respond.
full_text:
What the CJP protests reveal about India’s next generation
Why governments across the world are struggling to understand Generation Z, and why India may still have an opportunity.
Thousands of young Indians gathered on the streets of Delhi carrying placards demanding accountability, transparency, and justice. To many observers, the protests were simply another chapter in India’s familiar contest between the government and the opposition. That interpretation, however, misses the larger story.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests were not merely about one organisation or one controversy. They revealed a profound shift in how India’s youngest generation understands politics, institutions, and the social contract itself. Around the world, governments are discovering that Generation Z is reshaping democratic politics in ways few had anticipated. From Hong Kong to Santiago, Paris to Dhaka, youth-led movements have become less ideological, more digitally connected and increasingly driven by questions of fairness, accountability, and opportunity. Delhi was not an exception; it was the Indian expression of a much larger global phenomenon. Yet reducing the CJP protests to a global trend would also miss something uniquely Indian.
At the heart of the demonstrations lay a deep personal anxiety that resonates across millions of households: The fear that merit itself may no longer be enough. The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET), India’s nationwide entrance test for undergraduate medical courses, was never just about a single examination. It touched something far more fundamental: The belief that education remains the surest path to opportunity. Across the country, parents invest years of savings, students sacrifice their adolescence, and entire households organise their lives around the hope that hard work will be rewarded fairly.
When allegations of a question paper leak surfaced, the outrage was therefore not confined to those who had sat the examination. It resonated with every family that saw merit as the foundation of aspiration.
In that sense, NEET was less the cause of the protests than the catalyst that brought a deeper anxiety into public view. The demonstrations reflected a growing fear that institutions entrusted with safeguarding merit must not only be fair but also be seen to be fair. Once public confidence in that principle begins to weaken, the consequences extend far beyond a single examination or a single cohort of students.
History suggests that movements born out of genuine public concern rarely remain confined to their original grievance. As they gather momentum, new actors inevitably enter the arena, each seeking to influence the narrative and shape its political consequences. The CJP protests followed a familiar democratic pattern. They began with legitimate anxieties over fairness and accountability but gradually became part of a wider political contest.
This is neither unusual nor uniquely Indian. The anticorruption movement led by Anna Hazare began as a citizens’ campaign demanding institutional reform before reshaping India’s political landscape. Internationally, Hong Kong’s anti-extradition movement, Chile’s demonstrations over metro fares, France’s Yellow Vest protests and Bangladesh’s student mobilisations all followed a similar trajectory. Each began with a specific grievance but evolved into a broader debate about governance, trust, and institutional legitimacy.
The tragedy is that genuine public anxiety and political opportunity often arrive together. Students and their families were seeking reassurance that merit would prevail and wrongdoing would be punished. At the same time, organised political actors recognised an opportunity to amplify the issue and influence the broader political conversation. As often happens in democracies, the politics surrounding the protests gradually began to overshadow the concerns that had brought young people to the streets in the first place.
That distinction is important. Democracies are strengthened when genuine grievances are acknowledged and addressed. They are weakened when prolonging public distress becomes an end in itself, or when the search for solutions is eclipsed by the contest for political advantage.
The CJP protests will eventually disappear from the headlines. What will remain is what they revealed about this generation. Governments that recognise this transformation will shape the politics of the coming decade. Those that dismiss it as merely another protest may discover that history has already moved on.
The real challenge for any government is therefore twofold: To respond decisively to legitimate concerns and to ensure that institutional reform, rather than political theatre, remains at the centre of the national conversation.
The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

title: Cambridge professor Jason Arday quits amid plagiarism allegations
summary: The scholar announced his resignation amid a new investigation into his qualifications.
full_text:
Cambridge professor Jason Arday quits amid plagiarism allegations
The scholar announced his resignation amid a new investigation into his qualifications.
Jason Arday has resigned from his post as professor of sociology at the University of Cambridge, following the announcement of a new investigation into his academic qualifications and career.
Arday, who became the youngest Black professor in Cambridge’s history when he was appointed in 2023, announced on Wednesday that he had stepped down “with immediate effect” from his post at the university and his fellowship at Jesus College.

- list 2 of 3FAA says Trump’s Marine One briefly flew too close to passenger jet
- list 3 of 3Ex-Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib’s home petrol-bombed in Hasina fallout
Arday, who has faced a growing series of questions over his academic writings and credentials, said in a statement posted on the Good Law Project website that the scrutiny had become unsustainable, describing months of “relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary” that had taken a toll on him and his family.
The announcement came hours after the university said it had received “new information” about Arday’s qualifications and honorary appointments and would launch a new investigation, which is separate from an existing academic misconduct review already under way.
His decision to step down comes after a series of media reports alleging he plagiarised his PhD thesis and other research and statements.
Liverpool John Moores University, which awarded the doctorate in 2015, investigated the plagiarism allegations but did not uphold them, attributing the issues instead to “honest and reasonable error”. Arday has consistently denied wrongdoing, pointing to that finding as vindication.
Cambridge University had robustly defended Arday in June, claiming “a vile campaign to undermine his credibility” and insisting plagiarism claims regarding his “thesis and journal publications” had been investigated and dismissed by “the relevant institution” and journals.
It did not specify on Wednesday what new information had prompted its investigation, while Jesus College said separately that it was starting its own inquiry.
US academic and self-defined “race realist” Nathan Cofnas is behind some of the allegations. He was a Cambridge research affiliate, but his tenure ended in 2024 amid racism accusations. He has claimed multiple sections of Arday’s doctoral dissertation were copied from other works.
Some of Arday’s claims about his personal life, including that he ran 30 marathons in 35 days and raised millions for charity, have also come under scrutiny.
In an interview with The Times newspaper on Saturday, Arday admitted making academic “mistakes” but said he was being wrongly “portrayed to be a liar and a fantasist and an academic fraud”.
He also alleged the “campaign to unseat me from my position” was “racially motivated”.
The resignation also raises questions about the release of Arday’s memoir, Great and Unfortunate Things, which Simon & Schuster was planning to publish later this month.
In his statement, Arday framed his resignation as a pause, writing that he needed “time to heal” and that he “will return”.
“When I accepted the extraordinary honour of becoming professor of sociology at Cambridge, it was, without question, the greatest professional privilege of my life.”
He says the scrutiny of his work has made him “conclude that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away”.

title: Hormuz deal ‘close’: What’s the latest on each side’s positions?
summary: US officials say they would not accept any arrangement on the waterway that would leave Iran in control.
full_text:
Hormuz deal ‘close’: What’s the latest on each side’s positions?
US officials say they would not accept any arrangement on the waterway that would leave Iran in control.
Iran says a deal with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is “on the verge of being finalised” after both countries confirmed they had agreed coordinates for shipping routes through the critical waterway.
The strait links the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman with Oman and the United Arab Emirates on one side and Iran on the other. It flows through the territorial waters of Iran and Oman with some of its outskirts in UAE waters.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Could the Iran war derail Donald Trump’s legacy?

- list 3 of 3Iran anthem protest: Female footballers ‘proud’ to become Australian
It has become a major flashpoint in the war between Iran and the United States because one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies are shipped through it in peacetime. Iran closed the strait after the US and Israel began strikes on Iran at the end of February, sending oil prices spiralling and causing havoc in global energy markets.
In recent weeks, negotiations have been under way to arrive at an agreement that would restore a ceasefire and reopen the strait.
Here’s what we know:
When will the agreement be announced?
It is unclear when a deal will be announced, but on Wednesday, Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei signalled that Tehran and Muscat were close to finalising an agreement on a new commercial shipping corridor through the strait.
Baghaei told reporters the negotiations between Iran and Oman were “moving forward” and highlighted that “if certain third parties do not obstruct the process, the two countries are also in the final stage of reviewing and drafting a joint statement covering the main points of agreement” in an apparent reference to recent US strikes on Iran.
Talks between Iran and Oman began after Washington and Tehran signed a June 17 memorandum of understanding (MoU) that is supposed to be a framework for a peace agreement. The MoU stipulated that Iran would ensure the strait would be open to shipping for at least 60 days, but it fell apart last month. The two countries primarily disagreed on which routes ships should take, and Iran attacked several ships that had taken an Oman-approved route that was backed by the US.
Baghaei said on Wednesday that the talks with Oman covered the technical, legal, security and environmental aspects of the proposed shipping corridor.
Will the Strait of Hormuz reopen immediately once an agreement is announced?
Baghaei has dismissed claims that a bilateral agreement with Oman would automatically lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
A potential deal with Oman, he stated, “cannot in itself be interpreted as meaning the waterway has become safe for passing vessels”, arguing that the main source of instability remained the US and its naval deployments, maritime blockade of Iranian ports and other “hostile measures against the country [Iran] and its interests”.
Will an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz mean peace between the US and Iran?
No, far from it.
Once an agreement on the strait is reached, broader peace talks could begin again. Furthermore, it is unclear whether an agreement over Hormuz would be temporary and whether future arrangements for shipping through the waterway would need to be further hammered out.
Reporting from Tehran, Al Jazeera’s Mahmoud Abdelwahed said a deal on the Strait of Hormuz does not mean an “end to the crisis”.
“These discussions are now at the final drafting stage, pending a joint final statement,” he said. “But Iranian officials argue that these discussions are exclusively with Oman, without any foreign or outside interference.”
“On the other hand, Washington rejects reports suggesting that Iran would have control over traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, and they say that any temporary route should not require any permits, approvals or fees,” he noted.
“So while a final agreement on a temporary route in the Strait of Hormuz is now in the making, the dispute remains unresolved. That means that any agreement on a shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz does not necessarily mean the end to the crisis,” he added.
What do we know about each side’s positions?
What Iran wants
While Tehran has said it has agreed on the coordinates for shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, Iran also continues to insist it is negotiating only with Oman, not directly with Washington, and maintains that Iran and Oman should jointly manage the strait according to their respective territorial waters and they should retain control of navigation there.
Iran has also stated that it will not reopen the strait until the US naval blockade of its ports is lifted.
On Wednesday, Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs, told Iran’s IRNA state news agency that an understanding between Tehran and Muscat is that large parts of the shipping route would go through Iran’s territorial waters and some parts would pass through Oman’s waters.
While existing temporary routes would be closed, the new inbound and outbound shipping routes would be used for two to four months or potentially longer, Gharibabadi said.
Furthermore, Iran has intimated that it plans to introduce some form of fee system for ships. Under international maritime law, tolls for passage cannot be levied on international straits, such as Hormuz, but coastal states may charge for services they provide, such as navigational assistance, pilotage and environmental protection.
What the US wants
US officials have said President Donald Trump’s administration wants total freedom of commercial navigation through the waterway without Iranian tolls or any arrangement requiring ships to obtain Tehran’s approval before transiting the strait.
A US official familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press news agency this week that any temporary arrangement would not involve Iranian approval for ships to transit or charges for using the waterway. The official said Washington remained committed to restoring the previous system in which “no party controls the lanes or the ability to transit through them”.
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump rejected any suggestion that Iran should be allowed to charge vessels using the strait.
“I’m not going to let them charge,” he said. “Anybody’s going to charge, we’ll charge.”
Eight of the world’s largest shipping associations have also urged the United Nations to oppose tolls in the Strait of Hormuz amid reports that Iran and Oman are nearing a deal to manage the critical waterway.
In a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the head of the International Maritime Organization that was sent on Monday and made public on Wednesday, the groups said allowing authorities to charge vessels to transit the strait would violate international norms and harm the global economy.
What Oman wants
Chris Featherstone, a political scientist at the University of York, told Al Jazeera that for Oman, this deal is an opportunity to bring some stability to the region.
“They were involved in mediating negotiations between the US and Iran prior to this new phase of the conflict, and these new negotiations could represent a return of stability to the region. Similarly, this could establish stepping stones for future negotiations between Washington and Tehran,” he said.

Both sides are thought to be showing willingness to make some concessions.

title: Uganda football star Owori killed, weeks after death of rugby’s Gongodyo

Uganda football star Owori killed, weeks after death of rugby’s Gongodyo
SC Villa captain and Ugandan international David Owori was found unconscious by passers-by, but later pronounced dead.
Uganda international David Owori, captain of one of the country’s biggest football clubs, has died after an assault in the capital Kampala, police said.
The 28-year-old, who was captain of Uganda’s record-breaking champions SC Villa, was critically injured by unidentified assailants in a suburb of Kampala on Tuesday, police spokesperson Racheal Kawala said.

His death comes only weeks after the killing of Rugby international Sydney Gongodyo in the Ugandan capital.
Owori was found unconscious by passers-by, who took him to a nearby hospital. He was transferred to another hospital where he was later pronounced dead, Kawala said.
“David was not just a footballer. He was both a leader and an inspiration to a generation. As Captain of SC Villa, he led with courage, humility and passion. In the Uganda Cranes jersey, he carried the hopes of a nation,” the Federation of Uganda Football Associations said in a statement.

“Sadly, Ugandan sport has been hit with many such tragedies lately, and we hope for justice and a lasting solution,” the state-run National Council of Sports Uganda said.
Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa asked authorities to address the wider security challenges in the country, according to a statement on parliament’s website.
SC Villa extended a 20-year wait for the Uganda league title last season, when Owori lifted the trophy as captain.

title: Sudan war threatens ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO Heritage Site
summary: More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.
full_text:
In Pictures
Sudan war threatens ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO Heritage Site
More than 200 ancient Meroe pyramids are imperilled by Sudan’s escalating war and neglect.
Sudan’s war is endangering the ancient pyramids of Meroe, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as fighting and a lack of security have brought all preservation work to a halt and left the fragile structures exposed to the elements.
“The site may face a disaster, and collapses are possible,” archaeologist Mahmoud Suleiman said, warning that the more than three-year conflict has prevented experts from carrying out basic maintenance.
Located about 200km (125 miles) north of Khartoum, Meroe is home to more than 200 narrow, steep-sided pyramids built between 800 BC and 350 AD as tombs for rulers of the Kingdom of Kush.
Guards said windblown sand and encroaching vegetation are accelerating their decay. “The sand has thickened heavily on the pyramids and even inside the temples, and the grass grows thick,” guard Mustafa Ahmed said.
“The pyramids have deteriorated greatly, and stones have begun to fall.”
Antiquities inspector Mohamed Mubarak said salt released from accumulated sand is attacking the “inherently fragile” stones, eroding ancient inscriptions.
Suleiman said climate change, the dispersal of Sudan’s archaeological workforce and the halt of foreign missions have all contributed to “significant deterioration”.
UNESCO has warned that more than 100 cultural sites have been damaged and at least 22 museums looted or destroyed since the war began in April 2023.

title: US-Israel war on Iran upends Europe’s summer holiday travel patterns
summary: Holidaymakers are sticking closer to home as the conflict rages, while tourism operators adapt.
full_text:
US-Israel war on Iran upends Europe’s summer holiday travel patterns
Holidaymakers are sticking closer to home as the conflict rages, while tourism operators adapt.
London, United Kingdom – Nadia Waleed had set off from London with her husband and three daughters for a holiday in Bali, before continuing on to Pakistan, with stopovers in Dubai.
“A family holiday with multiple flights and stopovers is stressful at the best of times, but the situation in Iran resulted in multiple last minute changes in flight schedules by [the Emirates] airline,” she told Al Jazeera about her trip this summer.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Strait of Hormuz tolls would harm livelihoods worldwide, shipowners warn
- list 2 of 4In Bandar Abbas, the ceasefire never came
- list 3 of 4Wildfires in Spain and France force evacuation of more than 267,000 people
- list 4 of 4Hindus take holy dip in India’s rivers on sacred holiday
Days before flying, her return flight schedule had changed. A three-hour stopover in Dubai was now extended to 18 hours.
“A two-hour-long phone marathon ensued whereby we managed to get earlier return flights from Pakistan which reduced the layover duration,” she said.
But the next day, one family member’s schedule was changed again – their return flight was pushed back by a month.
“We have also had emails informing us of changes in flight details during our holiday by one hour, requiring rearranging of taxis and pickups,” she said.
Her experience is a small, personal illustration of a larger disruption.
The United States-Israel war on Iran has forced airlines to abandon huge stretches of airspace, sending commercial traffic on longer, costlier detours and upending the plans of families, retirees and honeymooners.
At Trailfinders, a UK travel company, the shockwaves arrived in bulk.
“The Middle East conflict meant Trailfinders had thousands of bookings to rearrange or cancel,” said Nikki Davies of the agency, pointing to Dubai, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, destinations in their own right but also crucial transit points for travellers heading on to Australia and Asia.
Once the UK’s Foreign Office advised against travel to the region, which invalidated insurance if ignored, the clients postponed in droves.
That advisory has since been lifted, and Davies described “incredible pent-up demand” for travel through the Gulf again.
But the disruption appears to have shifted where people choose to travel to.
“Europe is proving extremely popular as it’s closer to home and the standout destinations are Italy, Spain, Greece and Norway,” she said.
TUI, Europe’s largest tour operator, is seeing the same shift at scale.
“Traditionally, 75 percent of the European travellers at TUI book their summer holidays in Europe,” said TUI spokesperson Aage Dunhaupt. “This trend for package holidays is even stronger this year and shows that holidaymakers flock to the all-inclusive and protected package holidays.”
‘Almost like COVID’
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency this week told airlines to avoid Jordanian airspace after renewed attacks, extending its existing warning against Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and Oman until August 31.
British Airways has suspended flights to Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv, and will permanently drop its London-Jeddah route. Its twice-daily London-Riyadh service will be cut to once a day when it resumes in August. Virgin Atlantic has suspended its London-Dubai route through the coming winter season.
For independent travel agent Assra Satti, the anxiety showed up in the fine print. A family booking a July holiday to Vietnam via Istanbul wanted written guarantees before committing, wondering if they would be rerouted or reimbursed should the war disrupt their flights.
Satti secured written confirmation of both options, and the family flew as planned. As the holiday approached, the same clients expressed concern about a rumour circulating on social media that jet fuel surcharges might land them with an unexpected bill after booking. Satti’s advice to nervous clients has been to book everything as a single protected package, even at a slightly higher price, “because then the whole holiday is protected”.
The mechanics of avoiding conflict airspace are counted in tonnes of fuel and hours in the air, according to Moiz Hamid, a pilot with Pakistan International Airlines.
He says rerouted flights typically add an extra one to two hours flying west, and burn an additional 2,500 to 7,000kg (5,500-15,500lb) of fuel depending on the aircraft, a cost some airlines offset by cutting cargo payload.
The rerouting has also brought congested frequencies, GPS jamming and heavier workloads for pilots and controllers alike.
“Flying a longer, safer alternate route does come with its own risk, the biggest factor being unfamiliarity,” Hamid says. “In normal situations you’re not flying through certain areas, but in these unusual circumstances you have to be rerouted through areas that would be deemed safe by your company, your operator and your regulator. The fatigue does go up, the extended workload does go up.”
Hamid pointed to the downing of Azerbaijan Airlines flight 8243 in December 2024, blamed on navigational errors from military jamming, as a reminder of the stakes when aircraft stray off course.
The ripple effects also reach destinations with no direct stake in the conflict.
UK-based tourism operator Jean-Marc Flambert said that for Sri Lanka, 77 of the 87 weekly flights connecting Europe to the island run through the Middle East, and nearly all of them were disrupted.
“It was almost like COVID in the initial stages,” he said.
Bookings for this summer are down 20 to 30 percent industry-wide, a blow that lands hardest on those who depend on tourism.
Flambert recalled a fisherman turning up at his hotel with a catch, but nobody was there to eat.
“What does a fisherman do? He’d just dig a hole and chuck it.”
Families with young children, he said, have been the most likely to cancel outright, while young couples and retirees have proved far more willing to take the risk of a longer layover or a missed connection.
It is a small mercy for operators like his, patching together new routes through Thailand, Singapore and India to keep clients coming.
Based in London, Flambert is personally weighing that calculation this summer. He has booked a family holiday to Tanzania through Emirates, and has been holding off paying the hotel for as long as he can.
“What if something happens?” he said. “We’ve not done a package, so obviously if the airline changes and the hotel is still there, we’re going to lose our hotel money.”
His children are aged 15 and 18, “old enough to manage”, so he is prepared to take the risk.
“If I get stuck in Dubai for three days, I have friends in Dubai, I’ll just go and stay at a friend’s house, it’s not a big deal.”
But he is clear about where the real cost lands.
“If you lose $500, it’s going to hurt, but it’s not going to kill you,” he said. “The affected countries are feeling that. So let’s be a little bit empathetic.”

title: Sheikh Hasina vows to return, but will Bangladesh accept fugitive ex-PM?
summary: Awami League leader plans to return from India exile despite facing death sentence over 2024 protest crackdown.
full_text:
Sheikh Hasina vows to return, but will Bangladesh accept fugitive ex-PM?
Awami League leader plans to return from exile in India despite facing a death sentence for a bloody crackdown on the 2024 uprising that ousted her.
Dhaka, Bangladesh – Two years after she was ousted and forced to flee to India following a student-led uprising, former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has made her strongest commitment yet to return, saying she is prepared to face arrest, imprisonment or even death, but cannot remain away from her supporters.
“I know I may be detained, I may be sent to prison,” Hasina, 78, said in an audio address to journalists from New Delhi on Wednesday. “They may try to enforce verdicts issued in fabricated cases. But fear cannot decide my duty to the people.”
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Ex-PM Sheikh Hasina announces plan to return to Bangladesh
- list 2 of 4Ex-Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib’s home petrol-bombed in Hasina fallout
- list 3 of 4India denies involvement in ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina’s planned speech
- list 4 of 4Condemned ex-PM Hasina plans December return to Bangladesh
Hasina’s address at an event hosted by New Delhi’s Foreign Correspondents’ Club of South Asia marked the second anniversary of the end of her 15-year rule, which saw widespread allegations of killings and arrests of political opponents, human rights violations and rigged elections.
In November, Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal – a notorious court Hasina herself founded to try her rivals – found her guilty of crimes against humanity and sentenced her to death for ordering the killing of more than 1,400 people during the 2024 uprising.
Bangladesh has repeatedly asked India for Hasina’s extradition, but New Delhi, a close Hasina ally, says the request is under examination.
As Hasina spoke, protesters in capital Dhaka burned her effigy, while Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government expressed “outrage” over New Delhi allowing the event, warning it could further strain diplomatic ties.
In Magura town, about 170km (105 miles) southwest of Dhaka, the ancestral house of former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan was attacked by a mob angry over Hasina’s address.
Shakib, a former parliamentarian from Hasina’s Awami League party, has remained outside Bangladesh since the uprising. He has been accused of murder, embezzlement, fraud and money laundering by the authorities.
Hours before Hasina’s address, which Shakib also joined, Prime Minister Rahman inaugurated a memorial museum dedicated to the 2024 uprising at Hasina’s official residence. Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus, who headed the interim administration after Hasina’s ouster, also attended the ceremony.
‘No political future’
Against such a backdrop of a rival government, widespread anger and a death sentence looming over her head, Hasina delivered a defiant address, rejecting the widely accepted accounts of the July 2024 uprising, arguing instead that it was not a popular movement but a coordinated campaign to topple her government.
“They may put me in jail, or they may kill me. Anything may happen. But still I have to go back,” she said in response to a question asked by a journalist covering the New Delhi event.
The former prime minister repeatedly framed her planned return as an effort to “restore democracy and promote national reconciliation”, arguing that Bangladesh needed “healing rather than confrontation”.
Among the members of Hasina’s now-banned Awami League party, her announcement has rekindled hopes of a political comeback.
Al Jazeera reached out to five Awami League leaders. Three declined to comment. One senior leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, said: “The leader will definitely return, and we will all come out of our hiding places.”
Another party activist, Shajidul Islam Shobuj, who has been hiding since the uprising, told Al Jazeera: “We are eagerly awaiting her return and are already working to reorganise the party.”
But leaders of the 2024 uprising say reconciliation cannot come before accountability.
“Sheikh Hasina can return to Bangladesh at any time if she has the ability to do so,” Akhter Hossain, a former student leader and now a legislator from the National Citizen Party (NCP), told Al Jazeera. “She will have to face Bangladesh’s judicial process.”
Akhter said the Awami League had “no political future” unless it was held accountable for the “crimes committed during its time in power”.
Many others who protested during the uprising have also received Hasina’s announcement with scepticism.
“She previously said she would not flee the country, yet she did. We do not believe she will return simply because she says she will,” said Atikul Gazi, a 23-year-old who survived being shot at point-blank range by the security forces on August 5, 2024, but lost his left arm.
Whether Hasina returns voluntarily or not, he said the government should ensure she faced the judicial process.
‘Difficult to see how’
Experts say Hasina’s “high-risk political gamble” could determine the future of the Awami League while also testing the durability of the political order that emerged after her fall.
“She does intend to actually return to Bangladesh,” journalist and political analyst David Bergman told Al Jazeera.
“Returning to Bangladesh gives her a chance of remaining politically relevant, of creating significant challenges and difficulties for the country’s new government, and possibly changing the current political dynamic to the advantage of the Awami League,” he said.
But Bergman also argued that the Awami League continues to misread the political mood.
“Until it recognises its own responsibility for the party’s current demise, and acknowledges that Bangladesh is not the dystopian, failed country it seeks to portray, it is difficult to see how the Awami League can carve out a new role for itself in Bangladesh.”
If she returns to Bangladesh, it would not be Hasina’s first return from exile.
After the assassination of her father, Bangladesh’s founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, and most of her family members in 1975, Hasina spent years in exile before returning to Bangladesh in 1981 to lead the Awami League, which was then in opposition.
She was repeatedly arrested during the military rule in Dhaka before she stormed to power in 1996, governing the country for most of the next three decades.
This time, however, the political landscape is markedly different as Hasina no longer faces just political opposition.
Mubashar Hasan, a political observer and adjunct researcher at Western Sydney University’s Humanitarian and Development Research Initiative, says Hasina’s political challenges extend beyond the courtroom.
“Basically, Sheikh Hasina’s vow to return is a political strategy aimed at motivating and inspiring Awami League activists, many of whom have become demoralised since she left the country,” he said.
Hasan said many party activists felt abandoned when Hasina fled Bangladesh in a military helicopter on August 5, 2024, reportedly without warning senior party leaders.
But he also wondered if Hasina’s gambit would work.
“In my view, this announcement is intended to boost the morale of party supporters,” he said. “Personally, I do not think that strategy will succeed.”
‘Nothing more than empty rhetoric’
Meanwhile, Hasina’s speech has also triggered new diplomatic tensions between New Delhi and Dhaka.
“Bangladesh is outraged,” the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement. “Convicted mass murderer Hasina and her mafia enterprise will never have a place in the polity of Bangladesh.”
The ministry said India allowing Hasina to use its territory to attack the Bangladeshi state was “an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh” and “a grievous insult to the martyrs of the July Revolution”.
It also criticised New Delhi for failing to respond to Dhaka’s request to extradite Hasina under the 2013 bilateral extradition treaty.
