title: Coldcard’s Dice-Roll Safeguard Can Backfire on Holders Who Roll Too Few Times
summary:
On Uneasy Money, security researcher Taylor Monahan warned that the fix Bitcoiners are urging on Coldcard owners, adding dice rolls, is what left many of the earliest victims exposed, because the device warns but never stops you from rolling too few.

The post Coldcard’s Dice-Roll Safeguard Can Backfire on Holders Who Roll Too Few Times appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
The theft of more than $100 million in bitcoin from Coldcard hardware wallets has reopened the debate over self-custody and sent Bitcoiners repeating the same advice: harden your seed by adding your own randomness with physical dice rolls. On the August 5 episode of Unchained’s Uneasy Money, security researcher Taylor Monahan warned that the same ritual is what sank many of the earliest Coldcard victims, because rolling too few dice can leave a seed as guessable as the firmware bug now draining wallets.
Coldcard lets an owner feed dice rolls into a new seed, but each roll of a six-sided die adds only about 2.585 bits of randomness. Coinkite, which makes the device, says it takes at least 50 rolls to reach the 128-bit minimum it considers safe, and 99 rolls for 256-bit security. The device does not enforce that floor. Per Coldcard’s own documentation, it “does not limit the number of rolls, but will warn you if you apply too few rolls.”
The device warns, but it won’t stop you
That gap, Monahan said on the show, is where the pre-2026 thefts came from. The small number of Coldcard owners who lost coins in earlier years were, in her experience, the ones who had tried to protect their seeds this way. “In almost all cases, those people were the dice rollers,” she said on the podcast. The trouble with a half-hearted effort, she explained, is that “if you don’t roll the dice enough, then you still don’t have enough entropy” to begin with, and seeds like that were “trivial to crack” once an attacker went looking.
The distinction matters because Coldcard offers two dice paths. In the standard flow, the rolls are hashed together with the device’s own randomness, so extra rolls only add protection on top of the flawed generator. But Coldcard also offers a dice-only seed that, as Coinkite describes it, “hashes the roll sequence directly; it does not use the device’s generator.” Choose that path and stop early, and the seed’s security rests entirely on those few rolls.
A five-year-old flaw still spreading
The underlying bug, introduced in a March 2021 firmware change, made Coldcard skip its hardware randomness and fall back on a predictable software generator, cutting seed strength from an intended 128 bits to as low as roughly 40 bits on older models. Updating the firmware does not repair a seed already created with it. Galaxy Research has traced more than 1,596 BTC stolen from about 7,300 addresses across three confirmed waves, with an unconfirmed fourth wave that could push losses toward $130 million.
Monahan stopped short of certainty on whether Coldcard had since tightened the dice flow, saying “50 plus is probably safe, probably.” Her larger point was that the damage is still unfolding. “We are gonna see losses for the coming weeks and even months,” she said on the show.

title: Breaking Down Ethereum's New Issuance Debate
summary: EIP-8363 would cap Ethereum's staking ratio by burning issuance past 50% staked. Here's where the debate around this proposal stands today.
full_text:
Subscribe to Bankless or sign in
The Ethereum community has found itself in the middle of a new issuance debate, this time centered on EIP-8363.
This Tapered Issuance Burn concept traces back to at least 2023, when Ethereum Foundation researchers first started publicly worrying about the ETH staking ratio having no ceiling. Bankless Summit even held talks on this in 2024!
So why EIP-8363, why now?
If you consider Ethereum's issuance curve today, there's no ratio at which the incentive to stake stops. Yield falls as more ETH gets staked, sure, but Ethereum wizzes say this yield would only ever bottom out around 1.5%, no matter how close to 100% of the ETH supply gets locked up.
Right now, Ethereum's staking ratio is already past 33% of the ETH supply, and with no signs of slowing down. The idea is that if this ratio uptrend continues unabated, it poses two problems:
- It could push a majority of ETH into the hands of a small number of companies and liquid staking providers, such that the Ethereum community's fork threat would be weakened in the hypothetical scenario of fighting back against a captured validator set.
- Past a certain staking threshold issuance serves as a de facto and permanent dilution tax on anyone who isn't staking, meaning at that point every ETH holder must face the choice of joining in or watching their share of the network shrink.
This is where EIP-8363 would come in. If enacted, the mechanism would keep calculating validator rewards exactly as is done today, then burn a rising slice of them. The burn would grow as total stake grows, until it would fully cancel consensus rewards once staked ETH hits ~50% of the total ETH supply.
If ever that line gets crossed, EIP-8363 would make it so validators earn purely from transaction tips and MEV (i.e. the extra value block producers can earn by including, excluding, or reordering transactions) and not from new issuance until the stake ratio drops below 50% again.
Accordingly, under this paradigm there would still be incentives for validators, though less ETH would get minted along the way. Again, the big idea is that this model is ultimately aimed at reining in the staking ratio and ETH's dilution specter. Good intentions, yes. Yet more than a few critics have come forward in recent days, panning the proposal as ill-conceived.
The main "against" argument I've seen is that EIP-8363 threatens the vitality of DeFi. Staking yield has become ETH's reference rate, around which onchain lending, liquid staking tokens, and beyond get priced against. Aave founder Stani Kulechov has argued the proposal would make staking yield unpredictable for institutional buyers and could kill the case for borrowing ETH.
"Ethereum should not be punished for its growth," he wrote.
I've also seen skeptics contend that EIP-8363 would destroy the practicality of solo staking. Of course, the crux here is that a home staker's hardware and electricity bills don't shrink along with yield, so any downward move in net rewards eats into a smaller margin than it does for, say, a centralized exchange running 1,000s of validators.
Plus, as consensus issuance declines, MEV becomes a larger slice of what's left for validators to earn from. Critics have pointed out that this dynamic can catalyze a centralizing effect of its own, since MEV capture rewards scale and sophistication more than raw issuance does.
On the flip side, proponents of EIP-8363 maintain it would bolster the moneyness of ETH by protecting non-staked ETH from dilution while also giving it a bona fide supply ceiling, in turn honing ETH's case as "hard money" even further.
Proponents have also contested that solo stakers would be hit harder than large operators, arguing that since the burn scales with total stake, the point where adding more validators stops paying off arrives earliest for whoever already holds the most.
That point suggests home stakers would still have an incentive to grow all the way to the 50% ratio threshold, while the same wouldn't be true for large stakers. Under today's curve, by contrast, the design rewards growth no matter who you are or how much is already staked.
All that said, some of the best discourse I've seen on EIP-8363 so far came by way of the EF's DeFi specialist ivangbi, who threaded a reasonable middle position in a new (personal, not official EF) post out today. He suggested the model could theoretically work and DeFi could weather it, but only "if the fix and the arguments [were] more solid" and not based on "pseudo-economics." Worth the full read, I say.
From what I can tell, today is EIP-8363's cutoff for receiving PFI status (i.e. Proposed for Inclusion, Ethereum's lowest procedural bar, meaning "put this on the agenda for discussion") for the Hegotá upgrade. That said, nothing has been approved yet, and Hegotá itself isn't expected to be live on mainnet until next year.
If EIP-8363 does move forward, there will be a long runway either way, as its arrival would kick off an 18-month transition period. However, it's also possible that the proposal stalls after this week and the staking ratio keeps uptrending. Then we'll have to see if this same debate resurfaces down the road.
Whatever happens, the grand question is whether Ethereum is overpaying for security right now, and if so, is this fix worth the pain of finding out? Nobody's settled that yet, so keep this thread on your radar in the months ahead.

title: MetaMask Launches Agent Wallets
summary: MetaMask launched Agent Wallet, giving AI agents self-custodial access to onchain trading within user-defined limits and security controls.
full_text:
Subscribe to Bankless or sign in
MetaMask launched early access for Agent Wallet on Thursday, a self-custodial wallet configured for AI agents to execute onchain while abiding by user-set permissions. General access will go live later this summer.
What’s the Scoop?
- Constrained Agent Execution: Users can set daily spending limits and whitelist specific protocols before letting an agent swap, use perpetuals, prediction markets, DeFi, etc.
- Two Control Modes: Guard Mode requires human approval when a transaction falls outside the user’s rules. Beast Mode reduces approval interruptions, though flagged or malicious transactions still require two-factor authentication.
- Built-In Security: Supported EVM transactions pass through transaction simulation, Blockaid-powered threat scanning, and MEV protection: "fixed" checks which agents cannot override.
- Chains and Agent: Agent Wallet works across all supported EVM chains, as well as Hyperliquid, and lists support for frameworks like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and OpenCode.

title: Uniswap's Pools.Trade Launchpad Goes Live on Robinhood Chain
summary: Uniswap launched Pools on Robinhood Chain, offering two token launch formats, locked liquidity, lower fees, and built-in distribution.
full_text:
Subscribe to Bankless or sign in
Uniswap debuted Pools on Wednesday, their Robinhood Chain-centric launchpad.
Every token begins with a fixed supply of 1 billion and ultimately trades through a Uniswap v4 pool with permanently locked, autocompounding liquidity.
What's the Scoop?
- Two Launch Formats: Crowd Launch distributes tokens through bids submitted over four hours, with earlier bids receiving better prices. It must reach a $10K FDV or bidders are refunded. Instant Launch, on the other hand, uses a bonding curve, goes live immediately, and has no minimum.
- Lower, Autocompounding Fees: Each pool charges a 0.25% trading fee. Creators can choose to receive 0.05%, while the remainder automatically compounds into the permanently locked liquidity position, helping deepen liquidity and reduce spreads.
- Launch Protections: Crowd Launch’s gradual bidding process intends to limit bundled purchases, protecting against snipers, while Instant Launch lets creators buy in the launch block so outside bots cannot purchase first.
- Built-In Distribution: Tokens become available through Pools, Uniswap’s Web App, Wallet, Launches feed, API, and integrations with wallets and aggregators.

title: Eigen and Lighter Launch Autoresearch Challenge to Speed up Exchange
summary: Eigen Labs’ Lighter challenge has already made its ZK prover 3.3x faster, with developers and AI agents competing for 15K LIT.
full_text:
Subscribe to Bankless or sign in
Eigen Labs and Lighter launched an open “autoresearch” challenge on Wednesday, offering 15K LIT for developers and AI agents to compete to improve the performance of Lighter’s production zero-knowledge prover. Participants have already made the prover roughly 3.3 times faster.
What’s the Scoop?
- How it Works: Participants login with GitHub, clone a repository of Lighter’s prover and circuit code, and then set their agents to work finding and testing optimizations. Submissions are then independently benchmarked to ensure they remain correct and actually improve performance.
- Raising the Benchmark: When a submission establishes a new verified high score, its changes are promoted to the repository’s main branch, raising the circuit's benchmark that every future improvement must build on.
- The Objective: The challenge targets Lighter’s proving throughput, or how quickly its infrastructure can generate cryptographic proofs showing that exchange transactions were processed correctly.
- Part of a Series: The competition follows earlier Eigen Labs challenges focused on optimizing quantum circuits, making Poolside’s Laguna model run faster on Apple Silicon, and improving post-quantum proof systems in partnership with Succinct.

title: MetaMask 推出「Agent Wallet」！支援 AI 自主 DeFi 交易，守護模式防禦鏈上風險
summary:
AI 代理（AI Agent）鏈上交易迎來全新里程碑！加密貨幣自託管錢包龍頭 MetaMask 於 6 日宣布 […]

〈MetaMask 推出「Agent Wallet」！支援 AI 自主 DeFi 交易，守護模式防禦鏈上風險〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
AI 代理（AI Agent）鏈上交易迎來全新里程碑！加密貨幣自託管錢包龍頭 MetaMask 於 6 日宣布推出專為 AI 設計的「MetaMask Agent Wallet」早期存取計畫。該方案結合了 TEE 可信執行環境與 Transaction Shield 威脅掃描，允許 AI 代理在使用者自訂的消費限額與策略邊界內自主執行 Swap、永續合約與預測市場等 DeFi 操作，同時保有 2FA 人工審核與私有金鑰控制權。
（前情提要：嚇死！MetaMask 母公司「誤聘北韓工程師」核心程式碼遭滲透 1 個月，啟動緊急調查）
（背景補充：MetaMask 推出全新自託管 Money Account！享 mUSD 4% 收益、無縫刷卡消費）
隨著人工智慧（AI）與區塊鏈技術加速融合，鏈上 AI 代理的自主交易需求正急遽增加。台北時間 8 月 6 日，知名加密貨幣錢包 MetaMask 官方發表聲明，正式透過早期存取計畫推出專為 AI 代理設計的自託管錢包方案 ——「MetaMask Agent Wallet」。這項全新工具建立在 MetaMask 的安全架構之上，旨在讓 AI 代理能以高效且安全的方式，於使用者定義的規則範圍內自主執行鏈上操作。
自託管加持 TEE 安全機制，支援多鏈與熱門 AI 框架
MetaMask 官方強調，Agent Wallet 的核心理念是「代理可以自主行動，但必須在使用者定義的邊界內運作」。在安全性方面，該錢包堅持自託管原則，使用者始終掌控私鑰並可隨時匯出助記詞，同時結合可信執行環境（TEE）進一步強化金鑰防護。
在上線初期，開發者與交易者可透過命令列介面（CLI）進行連接。該系統具備「框架無關（Framework-agnostic）」的特性，支援包括 OpenAI Codex、Claude Code、Cursor、OpenClaw 以及 Nous Research Hermes Agent 等多種主流 AI 代理框架。支援的網路則涵蓋 Ethereum、Linea、Arbitrum、Avalanche、Optimism、Base、Polygon、BSC、Sei 等各大 EVM 相容鏈，同時亦支援去中心化衍生品平台 Hyperliquid，功能涵蓋代幣兌換（Swap）、永續合約、預測市場以及流動性提供（LP）等完整 DeFi 操作。
兩種防衛模式：Guard Mode 與 Beast Mode
為了兼顧操作靈活性與資產安全，MetaMask Agent Wallet 推出了兩種操作模式。首先是預設的「守護模式（Guard Mode）」，使用者可預先設定每日消費限額、白名單協議與具體交易策略。一旦 AI 代理發起超出規則許可的交易，系統便會自動暫停，並透過 MetaMask Mobile 推播通知或電子郵件發送雙重驗證（2FA）請求，交由使用者人工核准。
第二種則是針對高級交易員與開發者設計的「野獸模式（Beast Mode）」。在此模式下，系統在策略邊緣情況下會給予 AI 代理更大的自主彈性，減少交易中斷頻率。不過，MetaMask 特別指出，每一筆交易都會經過交易模擬、Blockaid 驅動的 Transaction Shield 威脅掃描與 MEV 保護；經判定為安全的交易，還享有每月最高 10,000 美元的交易保護保障。任何被標記為惡意或嚴重的違規交易，AI 代理皆無法繞過 2FA 人工審核。
限量開放測試，預計今夏全面上線
目前，MetaMask Agent Wallet 的早期存取計畫已開放獲准的加密原生交易者與開發者參與，申請者可至官方入口進行測試並設定策略限制。官方團隊表示，早期階段除了測試 CLI 穩定度外，重點在於收集真實使用者的策略控制回饋，並預計於今年夏季正式向全球廣大用戶全面開放。

title: 特斯拉、SpaceX 聯手砸 168 億鎂自建晶片廠「Terafab」！馬斯克要打造地表最大建築
summary:
為了滿足未來龐大的人工智慧算力需求，馬斯克決定自己造晶片！據外媒 TechCrunch 報導，Tesla 與 […]

〈特斯拉、SpaceX 聯手砸 168 億鎂自建晶片廠「Terafab」！馬斯克要打造地表最大建築〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
為了滿足未來龐大的人工智慧算力需求，馬斯克決定自己造晶片！據外媒 TechCrunch 報導，Tesla 與 SpaceX 於 6 日正式宣布，雙方將共同投入 168 億美元的初始資金，在德州興建名為「Terafab」的先進半導體工廠。馬斯克豪言這將是「地表最大建築」，未來將專為 Optimus 人形機器人與自駕車提供關鍵晶片。
（前情提要：特斯拉財報今晚來襲！馬斯克會將 SpaceX 與 Tesla 合併、組建 3 兆美元 AI 帝國？）
（背景補充：投資不碰馬斯克！華爾街兩檔ETF「隔絕Tesla、SpaceX」，賣點是政治立場？）
在人工智慧與自動駕駛需求爆發的推動下，科技狂人馬斯克（Elon Musk）正試圖將最核心的晶片供應鏈牢牢掌握在自己手中。台北時間 8 月 6 日，據外媒 TechCrunch 報導，電動車巨頭 Tesla 與太空探索公司 SpaceX 正式宣布，雙方將聯手投入高達 168 億美元的初始資金，在德州休士頓郊外的 Grimes County 興建一座名為「Terafab」的先進半導體晶圓廠。
打造地表最大建築，面積破 1 億平方英尺
對於這項極具野心的計畫，身兼兩家公司執行長的馬斯克在社群平台 X 上豪言，這座 Terafab 工廠將成為「地球上目前最大、最有價值的建築」。根據官方規劃，該廠房的製造空間將超過驚人的 1 億平方英尺，並預計從 Grimes 縣及鄰近的 Brazos 縣招募至少 3,000 名員工。
在環保與資源消耗方面，SpaceX 承諾這座超級工廠將使用當地 Gibbons Creek 水庫的水源，而不會抽取地下水，以減輕對德州當地水資源的衝擊。
解決 AI 算力焦慮：專供 Optimus 與自駕車
這座百億美元級別的晶片廠究竟要做什麼？SpaceX 在官網中明確指出，這是一座先進半導體晶圓廠，其核心目標是「彌合目前全球晶片供應與未來運算需求之間的差距」。Terafab 將打破傳統，把製造、封裝與測試先進邏輯與記憶體元件的流程整合於同一地點，大幅提升快速迭代與改善的效率。
報導指出，Terafab 未來生產的晶片將主要鎖定兩大應用領域：首先是針對邊緣運算與推論用途，專門供應給 Tesla 備受矚目的 Optimus 人形機器人以及 Cybercab 全自動駕駛計程車；其次則是生產高功率晶片，以支援 SpaceX 未來的太空資料中心。
總投資或破千億美元，Intel 確認參戰
馬斯克的終極願景是透過數百萬台機器人取代人類勞動力，並讓衛星成為全球 AI 訓練與推論的資料中心節點。這種規模的願景需要遠超目前全球產能的龐大算力，也成為他決心大規模自建晶片產能的關鍵動機。事實上，SpaceX 先前曾在文件中暗示，這項「多階段」的建設計畫，最終的總投資額可能高達 1,190 億美元。此外，傳統晶片製造巨頭 Intel 也已表態將參與 Terafab 專案，但目前對具體的貢獻細節仍保持低調。
儘管 Terafab 有望帶來龐大的經濟效益，但地方上的反應卻呈現兩極。在計畫宣布前夕，數百名當地居民在縣政會議上，對專案獲得的數千萬美元稅收優惠及決策透明度表達了強烈關切。不過，當地學區督學 Sarah Borowicz 博士則透過德州州長辦公室發表聲明表達支持，強調這項協議將強化學區資源、擴大學生未來的機會，並承諾將以透明且審慎的態度進行管理。

title: OpenAI 傳下週推出最強模型「Astra」！內部代號 mewfour 已進入發布候選階段
summary:
OpenAI 即將投下 AI 界的震撼彈？據知名科技爆料帳號於 X 平台透露，OpenAI 正準備在下週正式發 […]

〈OpenAI 傳下週推出最強模型「Astra」！內部代號 mewfour 已進入發布候選階段〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 即將投下 AI 界的震撼彈？據知名科技爆料帳號於 X 平台透露，OpenAI 正準備在下週正式發布全新大型模型「Astra」！爆料指出，這將是自 GPT-4.5 以來最大規模的預訓練模型，其內部代號為「mewfour」的版本已成為發布候選版（Release Candidate）。
（前情提要：白宮告訴 OpenAI、Anthropic：中國的開源模型，不必接受美國政府安全測試）
（背景補充：蘋果殺紅眼！申請禁制令封殺 OpenAI 產品，怒控 11 名前員工涉嫌竊密）
在人工智慧軍備競賽持續白熱化之際，全球 AI 霸主 OpenAI 似乎正準備亮出最新的底牌。台北時間 8 月 6 日，專門發布科技內幕的 X（前 Twitter）帳號 @synthwavedd 釋出了一則獨家爆料，直指 OpenAI 的下一個主要模型「Astra」已箭在弦上，最快將於下週正式對外發布。
🚨 EXCLUSIVE: OpenAI are preparing to launch Astra imminently, targeting next week.
Their next major model, Astra is a new pretrain – the largest model OpenAI have trained since GPT-4.5. Their most recent dogfood checkpoint of the model, internally known as "mewfour", is the…
— leo 🐾 (@synthwavedd) August 6, 2026
獨家爆料：mewfour 成為發布候選版
這則迅速在社群發酵的貼文指出，Astra 是一個全新的預訓練模型（New pretrain），且規模超越以往，是 OpenAI 自 GPT-4.5 以來所訓練過最大的模型。更引人矚目的是，爆料者明確提到 Astra 最新一期的內部 dogfood（內部員工測試）檢查點代號為「mewfour」，並且該版本已經確認為最終的發布候選版本（Release Candidate）。
熟悉 OpenAI 內部文化的觀察家都知道，該公司常以知名動畫《寶可夢》中的「夢幻（Mew）」及其衍生角色來作為模型的內部非正式代號。此前，社群中就曾流傳著一段被刪除的 ChatGPT 預覽影片，畫面中短暫閃過了「mewthree」的字樣；如今「mewfour」的出現，進一步提升了這則爆料的討論熱度。
官方早有預熱：Astra 解開 10 大數學難題
事實上，這則「下週發布」的傳聞之所以能引起軒然大波，很大程度上歸功於 OpenAI 官方日前的預熱動作。就在 8 月 1 日，OpenAI 在其官網發表了一篇題為《數學與理論計算機科學的十項進展》的研究報告。在該報告中，官方首度公開承認了 Astra 的存在，並明確將其定位為「我們的下一個主要模型（Our next major model）」。
報告指出，Astra 的內部版本成功解決了 10 個長期未解（部分甚至超過 30 年）的數學與理論計算機科學難題，並附上了完整的 Lean 4 形式化證明供機器驗證；而這一切的計算成本，若以當時的 API 價格估算僅約 2,000 美元。多家外媒隨後也跟進報導，推測 Astra 極可能就是具備多代理（Multi-agent）協作能力、專門處理長時間運行任務的新模型家族，甚至有望對應未來的 GPT-5.7 或 GPT-6 級別。
市場期待拉滿，最終時程仍待官方揭曉
儘管官方已用強悍的數學解題能力證實了 Astra 的實力，但對於確切的發布日期卻始終三緘其口。此前，預測市場與多數社群意見普遍認為，考量到執行長 Sam Altman 先前曾向華盛頓政策制定者展示新模型，Astra 可能還需要經過嚴格的美國政府安全審查，因此正式公開時間可能會落在 9 月或 10 月。

title: 比特幣活躍地址創 2024 年來新高！Glassnode：Coldcard 漏洞引發「恐慌性轉移」
summary:
比特幣活躍地址飆升，是牛市回歸還是恐慌蔓延？據知名區塊鏈數據分析平台 Glassnode 於 6 日發布的最新 […]

〈比特幣活躍地址創 2024 年來新高！Glassnode：Coldcard 漏洞引發「恐慌性轉移」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣活躍地址飆升，是牛市回歸還是恐慌蔓延？據知名區塊鏈數據分析平台 Glassnode 於 6 日發布的最新報告指出，近期比特幣每日活躍地址數激增至近 100 萬，創下 2024 年底以來的新高。但分析師警告，這波鏈上活動激增並非市場需求轉強，而是受到知名硬體錢包 Coldcard 韌體漏洞事件所引發的「恐慌性資金轉移」。
（前情提要：慎防去風險化拋售！分析師揭比特幣週期魔咒：每月 5 號常爆反向行情）
（背景補充：礦企 Cipher Digital 上半年狂賣 1,619 枚比特幣！慘賠 4,770 萬鎂，急轉型 AI 資料中心求生）
在加密貨幣市場中，鏈上數據的異常波動往往暗示著潛在的趨勢變化。台北時間 8 月 6 日，區塊鏈數據分析機構 Glassnode 在社群平台 X 上發布了最新的圖表分析，揭露了比特幣（BTC）網路上一個引人注目的現象：每日活躍地址數量出現了異常的尖峰。然而，與以往市場熱絡時的數據增長不同，這次的激增背後卻隱藏著使用者的資安恐慌。
Following the Coldcard firmware exploit, the number of active Bitcoin addresses surged to 0.98M/day, the highest since December 2024.
This is fear-driven on-chain activity. Holders migrating seeds and moving funds to alternative custody reflects an operational security response,… pic.twitter.com/BoKql7UpDH
— glassnode (@glassnode) August 6, 2026
活躍地址創 2024 年來新高，幣價卻未見起色
根據 Glassnode 釋出的圖表數據顯示，在 8 月初，比特幣網路的每日活躍地址數量呈現出近乎垂直的攀升，最高飆升至每日 98 萬（0.98M）個，一舉創下了自 2024 年 12 月以來的最高水準。然而，與這波活躍度形成強烈對比的是，截至發稿時，比特幣的價格卻依然在 6 萬多美元的區間震盪，並未跟隨鏈上活動的暴增而展現出強勁的上漲動能。
Glassnode：安全防禦行為，非市場信念改變
針對這個看似矛盾的現象，Glassnode 在貼文中給出了明確的解答。分析指出，這波活躍地址的激增，主要是受到近期知名硬體錢包 Coldcard 爆出韌體漏洞（Firmware exploit）事件的直接影響。
「這是一次由恐懼驅動的鏈上活動（Fear-driven on-chain activity），」Glassnode 解釋道。大量的比特幣持有者為了保護資產安全，被迫緊急遷移他們的助記詞種子（Seeds），並將資金轉移到其他更安全的替代保管方式。Glassnode 強調，這種數據的攀升純粹反映了使用者的「操作安全（OpSec）回應」，絕不能被解讀為整體市場情緒的轉好或是投資信念的改變。
社群熱議：後續應關注交易所流入與洗錢動向
這份分析報告在社群中引發了熱烈討論。有部分社群成員在回覆中認同 Glassnode 的觀點，指出這波 98 萬的活躍度主要是因為漏洞事件迫使網路處理大量新的未花費交易輸出（UTXO）以及恐慌性轉移，在評估市場實際需求上的意義十分有限。
更有資深投資人提醒，目前真正需要密切觀察的指標，應該是漏洞修補後，比特幣流入各大交易所的數量是否增加，以及網路手續費壓力是否持續升高。同時，也有人呼籲相關數據機構應進一步追蹤駭客是否正透過隱私幣等管道進行洗錢，以釐清這起資安事件對市場流動性的實質衝擊。

title: CFTC 力挺加密貨幣與預測市場！主席 Michael Selig：美國應追求「金融創新」而非國際監管共識
summary:
美國金融監管正迎來重大轉向！據權威財經媒體《經濟學人》於 6 日刊登的專欄文章，美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFT […]

〈CFTC 力挺加密貨幣與預測市場！主席 Michael Selig：美國應追求「金融創新」而非國際監管共識〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國金融監管正迎來重大轉向！據權威財經媒體《經濟學人》於 6 日刊登的專欄文章，美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）主席 Michael Selig 撰文表態，美國將不會「進口」那些阻礙市場發展的外國監管模式。他強調，在加密資產與預測市場等新興領域，美國必須以「創新」為優先，而非一味追求全球監管的「共識」，以確保其在全球高達 1.2 千兆美元衍生品市場的絕對領先地位。
（前情提要：紐約起訴 Kalshi！預測市場遭控「無照賭博」，CFTC 也出馬擋人）
（背景補充：Binance.US 8 月申請 CFTC 執照，進軍預測市場挑戰 Polymarket）
在全球加密貨幣與新興金融監管的十字路口上，美國最高級別的監管首長之一發出了明確的力挺訊號。台北時間 8 月 6 日，權威財經雜誌《經濟學人》（The Economist）的「By Invitation」專欄，刊登了一篇由美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）主席 Michael Selig 親自撰寫的重磅文章，標題直指核心：「金融新時代需要創新多於共識（The new era of finance needs innovation more than consensus）」。
拒絕「進口」阻礙發展的外國監管潮流
這篇文章的副標題明確點出了 Selig 的政策底線：「美國不會進口那些會阻礙市場發展的監管潮流。」自 2025 年 12 月接任 CFTC 主席以來，Selig 首度透過國際媒體完整闡述其監管哲學。
他在文章開篇便震撼點出衍生品市場的龐大體積。數十年來，期貨、選擇權與交換合約等衍生品，一直是企業、農民與投資者管理風險與配置資本的關鍵工具。這個曾經被視為小眾的領域，如今已成長為名目價值高達 1.2 千兆（Quadrillion）美元的超級市場，其中近半數更是直接處於 CFTC 的管轄範圍內。Selig 霸氣宣告：「全球衍生品市場已進入新時代，而美國正引領這個時代。」
點名加密資產與預測市場，創新重於共識
要如何維持美國的領先地位？Selig 的答案是「創新」。他認為，面對瞬息萬變的金融科技，美國不應為了一味追求國際監管的「共識」，而犧牲了市場的活力與競爭力。
在這份政策宣示中，Selig 特別點名了三大創新重點領域：加密資產（Crypto assets）、預測市場（Prediction markets）以及 24 小時無休交易。他主張，美國的監管機構應該優先促進這類負責任的創新，為這些新興金融工具提供發展空間，而不是盲目引進其他國家那些可能過度保守、扼殺創新的監管模式。這番表態無疑為正尋求在美國擴張版圖的加密貨幣衍生品平台，以及近期備受矚目的 Polymarket 等預測市場，打下了一劑強心針。

title: Tom Lee 喊美股 8 月強彈至 7800 點！重申年底標普 500 破八千大關
summary:
美股多頭大將再度拋出重磅預測！據 CNBC 報導，知名研究機構 Fundstrat Global Adviso […]

〈Tom Lee 喊美股 8 月強彈至 7800 點！重申年底標普 500 破八千大關〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美股多頭大將再度拋出重磅預測！據 CNBC 報導，知名研究機構 Fundstrat Global Advisors 共同創辦人兼研究主管 Tom Lee 於 6 日發表最新展望表示，在企業獲利強勁與 AI 投資潮的推動下，標普 500 指數（S&P 500）預計將於 8 月迎來一波強勁反彈並下看 7,800 點；即便隨後面臨約 10% 的正常回調，年底仍有望攻上 8,000 點大關。
（前情提要：Tom Lee 喊話：以太坊正進「ETH 2.0 階段」，目標價上看 25 萬美元）
（背景補充：Tom Lee 讚賞以太坊基金會：基礎設施是金融升級關鍵，EF正扮演政策市場中的關鍵角色）
華爾街最著名的多頭策略師之一、Fundstrat Global Advisors 共同創辦人暨研究主管 Tom Lee，再度對美股後市開出極度樂觀的藥方。台北時間 8 月 6 日，據外媒 CNBC 報導，Tom Lee 在最新專訪中直言，經歷了 6 月與 7 月的橫盤整理，加上近期部分 AI 對沖基金平倉引發的去槓桿拋售後，當前的美股市場就像一個「被壓縮的彈簧（Coiled spring）」，即將迎來劇烈的爆發性反彈。
8 月彈簧蓄勢發力，看好強彈至 7,800 點
Tom Lee 分析指出，雖然過去兩個月美股整體走勢相對平淡，但企業的實質獲利與資本支出 —— 特別是在人工智慧（AI）相關領域 —— 卻一直在大幅上升。近期市場出現的清算事件（Clearing event），例如大型 AI 對沖基金的強制平倉，實質上反而幫市場清除了主要賣壓，為後續的上揚奠定了堅實基礎。因此，他預期標普 500 指數將在 8 月份展現強勁動能，率先拉升至 7,800 點附近。
健康回調 10% 屬正常波動，年底目標鎖定 8,000 點
不過，Tom Lee 也提醒投資人，市場不會一走到底。在他預想的路徑中，指數在衝上 7,800 點後，可能隨之面臨約 10% 的階段性修正（Drawdown）。但他強調，這種大幅度的回調屬於多頭市場中的「正常波動與健康整理」，絕非熊市來臨的訊號。
對於全年的最終終點，Tom Lee 堅定地重申了他早在年中就提出的目標：標普 500 指數在 2026 年底前必將收在 8,000 點以上。他從估值角度進行解析，若 2026 年標普 500 預估每股盈餘（EPS）能達到約 400 美元左右，搭配合理的 20 倍本益比（P/E ratio），即可穩穩撐起 8,000 點的估值；若市場願意給予更高的本益比溢價，指數甚至有機會衝上 8,400 至 8,800 點的高空。
AI 獲利與通膨放緩助攻，2027 年迎更大牛市
支撐 Tom Lee 看多立場的底氣，主要來自三大宏觀支柱：首先是 AI 產業帶動的企業獲利爆發力；其次是通膨數據有望進一步趨緩，消除聯準會（Fed）重啟升息的潛在疑慮；最後則是市場籌碼面的優化。他甚至大膽預測，隨著 SpaceX 相關股票解鎖與新任聯準會主席過渡等政經不確定性在今年消化完畢，2027 年極可能成為美股歷史上「表現最好的年份之一」。
雖然 Tom Lee 的大膽預估為市場注入了一劑強心針，但也有部分市場分析師提醒，若未來企業獲利預期遭到下修，或是國際油價與利率再度反彈，美股的估值結構仍可能遭遇考驗，投資人宜在樂觀中保持對總體經濟數據的密切關注。

title: 三星 Galaxy AI 新方向！未來手機不需打字輸入，AI 代理會全自動操作
summary: 三星積極規劃 Galaxy AI 段發展藍圖，期望改變用戶必須對話框輸入文字指令互動模式。三星 MX 部門顧客 […]
full_text:
三星積極規劃 Galaxy AI 段發展藍圖，期望改變用戶必須對話框輸入文字指令互動模式。三星 MX 部門顧客體驗辦公室主管兼副總裁 Jay Kim 於 AI 圓桌會議表示，推動智慧手機由傳統應用程式互動，過渡至全自動化代理智慧體架構。三星正在開發新 Galaxy AI 技術，目標是讓用戶減少手動操作與文字輸入，由系統自動跨應用程式執行任務，邁向全自動化代理智慧體時代。
應用程式不會消失，重點在減少手動操作
Jay Kim 回答 AI 普及後應用程式會否消失問題，流動應用程式短期內不會消失。由於應用程式已針對流動裝置高度最佳化，整個業界亦圍繞建立商業模式，因此未來會在應用程式使用習慣與 AI 進化之間取得平衡。轉變重點在於減少用戶手動操作精力，以往用戶需要頻繁切換不同應用程式處理事務，而代理智慧體則可協助用戶省卻繁瑣流程，自動完成跨應用程式工作。
從手動對接走向 MCP 標準與螢幕自動化
三星最初嘗試將 AI 手動對接至個別應用程式功能，但很難規模化推廣。為突破限制業界開始推動流動上下文協定（Mobile Context Protocol，MCP），透過統一行業標準讓生態圈夥伴共同參與開發。跨行業標準成熟前三星也推出過渡性質自動化，辨識手機螢幕內容幫用戶執行叫車等。Jay Kim 坦言 Galaxy S26 首次登場自動化功能研發過程艱辛且未臻完美，但是邁向全自動化體驗關鍵第一步。
▲ Galaxy S26 率先引入螢幕辨識與自動化，代替用戶完成複雜操作。
跨越語音與視覺介面，擴展至穿戴式裝置
三星全球有超過 10 億日活用戶，變更使用者介面時必須展現負責任態度，並與整個產業鏈夥伴同步前進。印度等語言極度多元複雜市場，團隊亦積極與當地研發中心合作，以滿足本地化語音與語言需求。Jay Kim 展望未來代理智慧體介面將不限手機，擴展至智慧手錶、智慧眼鏡等穿戴式裝置，結合語音、視覺與空間感測，打造無縫跨裝置自動化體驗。

title: Thousands of rail passengers hit by power failure disruption
summary: An outage in Manchester caused delays and cancellations, with services expected to be affected throughout the evening.
full_text:
Thousands of rail passengers hit by power failure disruption
- Published
Thousands of rail passengers have described "nightmare" journeys, after being hit by delays and cancellations following a power failure at a signalling centre that caused major disruption across northern England.
A 90-second power outage occurred in the area covering Network Rail's Manchester Rail Operating Centre just before 14:00 BST on Thursday. The BBC understands there was then a delay to back-up systems kicking in, meaning affected trains had to stop while signalling was down.
Network Rail said "engineers are making good progress fixing the signalling issues" but warned that major disruption was expected until the end of the day on Friday.
At least eight rail operators remained affected on Thursday evening.
"We've got to really understand what's gone wrong here, because clearly something has and we've got to make sure we investigate that thoroughly to understand why things haven't restored as we would have expected," said Chris Wright, Route Director NW at Network Rail.
Network Rail said services may continue to be disrupted "because many trains and crews are not where they would normally be after this unexpected incident".
It has advised passengers hoping to travel on Friday to continue to check online for information on any further disruption, external: "As soon as we have information, we will keep you updated."
Manchester Rail Operating Centre was opened in July 2014 and houses all the controls to safely operate the railway in the region, including signalling.
According to Network Rail, its operational control boundary spans from Crewe in the south to Carlisle in the north, and from Todmorden in the east to the Welsh border in the west.
The initial power outage on Thursday afternoon was part of a wider power supply outage in the Ardwick area, but the BBC understands there was a delay to the back-up supply kicking in - which exacerbated the problem.
'Ripple effect'
SP Electricity NW released a statement, detailing a power outage which had affected "around 5,000 customers in the Manchester area at 1:40pm today - all power was fully restored within 90 seconds," the company said.
BBC transport correspondent Katy Austin said the disruption caused a "ripple effect", with some trains outside the area directly affected - including the Midlands - impacted.
Trains travelling north from stations including Birmingham New Street and London Euston were subject to delays and cancellations, and National Rail initially said the Midlands was also affected by the power failure.
To add to the chaos, Network Rail said "a wartime bomb" near the railway track between Tamworth and Burton-on-Trent had blocked all lines between the two stations for a time on Thursday.
The incident and the disruption has since ended, Network Rail said.
Sarah Nelson, who was unable to get to work in Manchester, was one of a number of affected passengers who told BBC Your Voice about their disruption.
She said she faced a "nightmare" five-hour round trip to just get back to her home in Blackpool.
The remedial massage therapist's train was stuck at Horwich Parkway for more than 90 minutes.
Chris, a technology consultant, travelled to Manchester from Scotland on Wednesday on business.
He said he would likely book a hotel for the night, despite the expense and inconvenience, describing the delay as "costly, inconvenient... frustrating".
"We're still being told there is no power to any of the trains, no electricity - and they don't expect anything to run today until the end of the day," he said.
"I will have to get a hotel here and see if I can get home tomorrow."
A couple returning from a trip to Gibraltar were planning to get a train home to Clitheroe, Lancashire, after landing at Manchester Airport.
But Matt and Sarah had to book an Uber to take them home instead, adding it was "costing a fortune".
Stacey was among passengers who were evacuated from a train that stopped prematurely in Manchester when signalling failed.
The 38-year-old office worker, who was travelling from Deansgate to Leyland, Lancashire, paid £60 for a taxi home.
"The train stopped when the signals went," she said, praising the "phenomenal" staff for their "calm and professional" efforts organising a controlled evacuation from the viaduct.
'Cannot happen again'
Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander posted on X, external she was "sorry to hear passengers in the North West are affected by a power outage, with trains cancelled or delayed".
"The focus rightly needs to be on getting trains back up and running as soon as possible," said Bev Craig, the new mayor of Greater Manchester
Craig said she would be asking both Network Rail and the train operating companies for an investigation into the cause and their response.
"We need assurances that this cannot and will not happen again."
Some train operators were continuing to advise against travel on Thursday night, with Northern Rail advising do not travel until 10:00 on Friday 7 August.
Passengers whose journeys have been affected as a result of the disruption may be entitled to some money back.
The amount may depend on the type of ticket and the length of delay. Each train company has its own compensation threshold.
"Claims can be made online, or by post, using a form that you can download from a train company website or get from a staffed station," according to National Rail.
Claims could also be made via the nationwide scheme Delay Repay.

title: Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support
summary: Fifa's backing of president Gianni Infantino at a meeting on Wednesday "changes nothing", says European governing body Uefa.
full_text:
Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support
- Published
European teams could still boycott competitions including the World Cup as Uefa says Fifa's defence of its president Gianni Infantino "changes nothing".
The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino in reaction to the plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
European governing body Uefa said in a statement its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino's plan being aborted.
"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn and secondly," Uefa's statement said. "Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.
"These conditions have not been met."
Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a "shabby, back room, opaque deal".
- Infantino sorry for errors but stays Fifa president 
  - Published1 day ago
- If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president? 
  - Published3 days ago
Infantino had offered all associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups, through the FFE subsidiary.
World governing body Fifa said during Wednesday's meeting "mistakes" regarding FFE were "acknowledged", saying it was "not the intention" for the Fifa Council and members association to "feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently".
Uefa's statement in response added: "Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.
"Yesterday's announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."
Fifa has been approached for comment.
Why Fifa's statement did not impress Uefa
Infantino arrived at Fifa's offices in Rabat, Morocco on Wednesday in now-familiar fashion, chauffeured to the building in a motorcade, sitting in the back of a Mercedes with blacked out windows.
Some questioned whether he would still be the Fifa president when he left.
Yet if anything, on the surface at least, Infantino appears emboldened.
This was not the 56-year-old being ordered to a hearing to explain his actions.
It was Infantino who summoned members of the Fifa management board to sit around the table with him, to talk through the events of the last week.
Secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, Infantino's right-hand man, had been critical in an internal memo to staff, calling the FFE proposals "a sad and reproachable series of events".
After the meeting finished it appeared to be water under the bridge, with Infantino and Grafstrom pictured sat next to each other and smiling at a Women's Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia.
If there were clear-the-air talks, they appear to have worked.
Other members of the Fifa management board to attend the meeting included finance chief Thomas Peyer, legal chief Emilio Garcia Silvero, chief of staff Daniel O'Toole, chief of member associations Elkhan Mammadov and media relations director Bryan Swanson.
BBC Sport has been told that Fifa's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, was not invited.
Lamour strongly criticised Infantino's FFE plan, saying it was "the project of one person", and "the time has now come for football's political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions".
He added: "I lose my job, then so be it. At least I'll sleep well tonight."
Lamour has declined to comment to the BBC. Fifa has been approached for comment.
What concerns Uefa is that this meeting was a gathering of employees who are themselves part of the regime.
It is unknown if Infantino was forced to answer difficult questions about his plan. Questions such as: who was involved? Whether there was a competitive tender process? And if he stood to benefit personally?
While Fifa said "mistakes made were acknowledged" and an "apology was made", there was no direct accountability for the controversy.
Uefa still wants answers to those key questions and will not be content until it gets them - or Infantino leaves.
A boycott remains Uefa's one key asset
Uefa is in something of a pickle as it tries to get rid of Infantino.
The easiest route to success was the slow turning of the vice throughout this week, hoping to exert enough pressure to force him to quit.
Yet the Swiss appears to have no intention of walking away.
European football looks like an outlier, struggling to gain enough support to topple him.
On Thursday, Lamin Kaba Bajo, the president of the Gambia Football Federation, praised Infantino's "courage" and for the U-turn, and said he was "willing to give him my support more than ever".
Only Jordan, one of the few countries which did not back Infantino before last week, has publicly stated it will not vote for his re-election in March.
Concacaf, which oversees football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, also issued a public statement after the proposal was aborted but, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president.
Conmebol, the South American confederation, said on Thursday it would not support "any action or procedure that disregards" Fifa's mechanisms before the presidential election.
The Confederation of African Football (Caf) said its executive committee "unanimously reconfirmed" its support for Infantino and thanked him for his support for African football over the years.
Ideally, Uefa would force an emergency meeting of the Fifa Council, to provide what it would consider to be a true chance to hold Infantino to account.
But getting the necessary 19 of 36 confederation and football association heads to support it has proven to be exceptionally difficult.
Uefa has also kept on the table the option of a vote of no confidence, which it can trigger via an extraordinary congress any time it wishes.
However, it would need a majority of Fifa's 211 member associations - 106 votes - to pass the motion. It would be a de facto presidential election without a second candidate.
If Uefa does not think it can get to 106, which looks a stretch, then there is little point in triggering the vote.
The other option is to try to find a unity candidate to stand against Infantino in the election next March. The favourite would be Concacaf president Victor Montagliani.
Any option which takes time gives Infantino space to build bridges, and with Fifa due to announce new funding to member associations by the end of the year he could dangle another carrot for his re-election.
Unless Uefa sticks by the nuclear option - and goes through with its threat of a boycott.
This has issues, and it is not a lever you can pull very often, otherwise it gives the impression of riding roughshod over the rest of the world.
It is one thing to use it to jettison the FFE proposal, another entirely to effectively dethrone the president with it.
Uefa's stance will soon be tested, with the Fifa Women's U20s World Cup kicking off in Poland on 5 September. Six European countries are due to take part, including England.
Analysis: A feeling Infantino is trying to swerve responsibility
Some at the European confederation claim Wednesday's statement shows exactly why the beleaguered president must step down.
The feeling within Uefa is that the statement was far from representative of the entire world governing body, and that there has been a lack of consultation with the council or membership.
There is also a view that Infantino is trying to swerve personal responsibility by sharing out the blame for the aborted proposals, and that he alone should have apologised - rather than issue his expression of regret alongside his deputy Grafstrom.

title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
summary: A New Mexico judge ordered the Instagram, Facebook and Whatsapp parent company to pay another $567m for the way it has harmed children.
full_text:
Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
- Published
A US judge in New Mexico on Thursday ordered Meta to pay another $567m (£421m) for its failure to warn the public about dangers its platforms posed to children, marking the largest ruling against the company over child safety.
Judge Bryan Biedscheid said the social media giant is a "public nuisance" akin to air pollution and that it must put the money in a fund aimed at reducing future harms.
The ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.
Judge Biedscheid compared Meta to a factory, with advertising and content as its product and "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children to be the pollution that must be abated".
Meta, which owns and operates Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, has been contacted by the BBC for comment.
Regarding the earlier $375m verdict against in the case, Meta had said it intended to appeal the ruling. It was the first time that a state had successfully sued Meta over child safety issues.
The case stems from a 2023 lawsuit brought by attorneys for the State of New Mexico, arguing Meta should be held liable for the way in which its platforms endangered children and exposed them to sexually explicit material and contact with sexual predators.
In the first phase of the trial, Meta was found to have repeatedly violated New Mexico's Unfair Practices Act as its recommendation algorithms essentially "steered" young users toward harmful content and contacts.
Recommendation algorithms are the tools that Meta uses to automatically curate the content a user sees on its platforms.
In ruling on this second phase of the trial, Judge Biedscheid found that Meta's harms reached the level of "public nuisance", or an issue of health and safety that has become so widespread it is negatively impacting a general public.
In addition to being the largest fine Meta has received over child safety issues, the ruling also appears to be the first time that a social media company has been deemed a public nuisance.
"Just as noxious pollution produced by the factory can harm the common public right to reasonably clean air, the harmful effects of Meta's platforms on children do not stay contained by its platforms and, instead, migrate to the internet as a whole and, perhaps most concerning, to the real world and create a common, societal burden on and harm to the affected children and their families and schools, as well as hospitals and law enforcement," the judge wrote.

title: Arrests in Norfolk town as disorder continues for third night
summary: The arrests follow disorder linked to anti-immigration protests in the Norfolk market town.
full_text:
Further arrests in Thetford as disorder continues for third night
- Published
More arrests have been made in Thetford as disorder linked to anti-immigration protests continued for a third night in the Norfolk market town.
A further two men in their 40s were arrested on Thursday evening, Norfolk Police said, taking the total number of people arrested in relation to the disorder to five.
One of the pair was arrested on suspicion of racial hatred, relating to offences on Wednesday, the force said. The other man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and failing to give his details to police when asked.
Policing powers were stepped up in Thetford on Thursday evening following the disorder earlier in the week.
It came after police officers were "subjected to significant aggression" on Wednesday, including a female police officer who was "seriously bitten".
Crowds also attempted to storm homes linked to alleged asylum seekers on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings.
Police removed some people from a property on Thursday evening.
Amid the disorder, pictures appeared to show a heavy police presence in the residential area of Canterbury Way on Thursday night.
A Home Office spokesperson condemned the behaviour, warning that "anyone taking part in this criminal activity will face the full force of the law".
Norfolk Police has imposed public safety measures in the town, including requiring people to remove face coverings if asked to do so or face arrest.
They will also be permitted to direct anyone committing, or who they suspect may commit, anti-social behaviour, to leave the area.
The measures were put in place from 18:00 BST on Thursday and remain until 07:00 on Friday.
Two police officers were injured in the second night of disorder on Wednesday, with the force confirming that "significant police resources" were deployed as a result.
Witnesses reported a crowd of more than 200 people on Clover Way, with eggs and rocks thrown at houses and chants of "we want them out".
The force said members of the group "became physically aggressive towards officers – a male officer was struck with a rock and a female officer was seriously bitten, breaking the skin."
Assistant chief constable Julie Dean, said: "We will not stand by and allow violence to take place, whether that is directed towards members of the public, local residents or police officers carrying out their duties."
A spokesperson for the Home Office said: "The right to protest is fundamental to our democracy and the concerns of communities are central to our immigration reforms.
"However violence and disorder are never acceptable, and we absolutely condemn the behaviour seen in Thetford, including attacks against frontline police officers."
The attacks on officers followed unrest on Tuesday in St John's Way, Bracken Road and Elm Road, when properties were damaged with windows smashed and fences broken, and people attempted to break into a residential property, police said.
The Labour MP for South West Norfolk, Terry Jermy, also said the "ugly scenes in Thetford over the past few days have been difficult to watch and are deeply concerning".
A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence on Wednesday afternoon following Tuesday's disorder. He was released and issued with a conditional caution.
In the early hours of Thursday, two further arrests were made following Wednesday's unrest.
One man aged in his 40s remains in custody, and a 68-year-old man from Thetford has been charged with possession of an offensive weapon, namely a wooden bat.
ACC Dean promised "robust action" to the disorder, adding: "We will always facilitate and support the right to peaceful protest, and we recognise that people may hold strong views and feelings about issues.
"Our role is to keep people safe. We have a duty to protect everyone in our communities, maintain public order and prevent harm. We will not stand by and allow violence to take place, whether that is directed towards members of the public, local residents or police officers carrying out their duties."
Witnesses also claimed the police response on Wednesday was "heavy-handed" and a woman on a mobility scooter had been pepper-sprayed.
In response, the police said Pava spray was "deployed proportionately" in response to a person's behaviour in the crowd.
A spokeswoman added: "We understand that concerns have been raised about a woman using a mobility scooter who was affected during the incident.
"It was not the intention for any bystander to be impacted, however, where people remain within an area of active disorder and do not follow police instructions to move away, there is a risk they may be affected by tactics deployed to protect public safety."
Scott Hussey, a Reform councillor for the nearby Brecks division on Norfolk County Council, said a "peaceful protest" had started at the town's police station on Wednesday night before it moved to Clover Way.
"I counted up to the 30 officers lined up on one side of the street and on the other side maybe up to 100 protesters," he said.
"There were some skirmishes, it was a spirited protest but I didn't see any violence."
He accused the Home Office of "opening a number of these HMOs across Thetford" and "trying to rush through the site for asylum seekers at Barnham".
"We fully support their right to protest. I'd encourage people to protest peacefully and most of what I saw yesterday was peaceful."
Jermy has previously called on the Home Office to end "secrecy and confusion" around plans to house more asylum seekers in former military barracks – including at RAF Barnham, near Thetford.
In a statement he condemned the unrest, saying: "People have been pulled from their homes – a place of safety – and forcibly removed, with reports of members of the public breaking into homes, taking property and smashing windows.
"This would have been utterly terrifying for the people in these properties and also very worrying for neighbouring residents.
"I do not know the immigration status of the people placed in these properties or their legal status, but I know they are human beings that must be afforded the same rights that we all expect in this country.
"Whatever our own individuals views on immigration - mob rule and vigilantism is not acceptable."

title: South Korea space agency shares Moon images after SpaceX rocket debris crash
summary: Seoul's lunar orbiter captured images of the Moon before and after part of SpaceX's rocket hit its surface on Wednesday.
full_text:
South Korea space agency shares Moon images after SpaceX rocket debris crash
- Published
South Korea's space agency has released images that show the Moon after part of a SpaceX rocket crashed into its surface on Wednesday.
The Korean AeroSpace Administration (KASA) said lunar orbiter Danubri captured images after the impact, which it shared, external alongside photos of what the Moon's surface looked like before the crash.
Rocket debris struck the Moon at around 06:35 GMT on Wednesday, according to the South Korean space agency.
SpaceX has said the impact was not intentional.
Re-usable Falcon 9 rockets were designed to allow part of the rocket to return to Earth (the upper stage) and other sections to be shed in space. SpaceX has used this type of rocket on several missions.
The empty upper stage of this Falcon 9 rocket, which scientists predicted would hit the Moon at a speed of about 5,400mph (8,700km/h), is about the size of a five-storey building and weighs approximately 4,000kg (630st) on Earth.
The short, dramatic flash created when the rocket part hit the Moon would have been hard to catch by amateur astronomers even with high-end telescopes, but larger observatories - including Seoul's space agency - are analysing the information.
While the impact did not pose any danger to Earth, Matt Bothwell, astronomer at the University of Cambridge, raised concerns about space debris.
"Space is getting more and more crowded," he said, as each year "we launch more stuff into space".
"It could feasibly be within a few decades that it's actually quite hard to get past Earth's orbit because space is so crowded," Bothwell warned.
This Falcon 9 was in orbit since January last year, when it blasted off from Florida.
The same booster section from the January 2025 mission is due to set off on its 18th flight on 10 August. SpaceX says the mission hopes to launch 29 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit.
The rocket that blasted from Florida last January was carrying two lunar landers into space.
Its job was to fire the upper stage hard enough to send both of the landers out of Earth's orbit and onto a path towards the Moon.
The spent stage was left drifting in a long, looping orbit that swung out towards the Moon and back again.
Over the next 18 months, the gentle gravitational tug of the Earth, Moon and Sun, along with light from the Sun, gave it a faint push.
Astronomers tracking the rocket part eventually worked out that those small nudges had put it on a course towards the Moon, and it was picking up speed every day.
The impact on Wednesday happened in broad daylight for many parts of the world, but the tiny flash it produced would have been far too faint to see, even through a telescope.

title: Artificial Intelligence used to design brand new viruses
summary: Scientists made 16 successful viruses that had their genetic code designed by artificial intelligence.
full_text:
Artificial Intelligence used to design brand new viruses
- Published
Artificial Intelligence has been used to design brand new viruses that are fully functional and can replicate in the laboratory, say US researchers.
It is the first time whole genomes have been successfully designed by AI.
The resulting 16 novel viruses were created to infect bacteria and pose no threat to people.
The breakthrough has been labelled a "very significant turning point" in science that could unlock a new era for treating disease. But experts have also warned AI-designed viruses raise "urgent" safety and security concerns.
AI tools are rapidly advancing and have already been used to design new antibiotics.
But that is relatively simple compared with designing a new viable virus from scratch.
"This is a next step in the complexity that's designable by generative AI, this is the first time generative AI has been used to design a complete genome, it's something that can replicate and have other functions inside cells… this was new territory for us," Brian Hie, assistant professor at Stanford University, told the BBC.
- AI designs antibiotics for gonorrhoea and MRSA superbugs 
  - Published14 August 2025
- I found a bacteria-eating virus in my loo - could it save your life? 
  - Published28 June 2025
The technology works similarly to large language models, like ChatGPT, which predict sequences of text.
In this instance the AI models, known as Evo1 and Evo2, predict the language of life rather than words.
The AI models were trained on genetic codes from viruses, bacteria, plants and people.
They were then refined to produce a type of virus, known as a bacteriophage, which infect only specific species of bacteria.
The Stanford researchers picked the most promising 302 AI designs and synthesised them in the lab. Of these, 16 proved effective at killing E. coli bacteria.
Samuel King, a PhD student in the lab, said they realised the phage were working in the early hours of the morning.
The phage were placed on petri dishes growing a layer of bacteria on them and the scientists waited for signs their new viruses were enjoying the feast.
"We were starting to see these clear spots and it was just extremely exciting," says King. When the results were shared with the wider team "the room spontaneously burst into applause", Hie recalls.
Developing new phage could lead to new ways of treating infections that have become resistant to antibiotics.
But the breakthrough also points to the ability of AI to design new biology that goes beyond the natural world – what is known as synthetic biology.
Hie argues this has the potential to "massively improve human health" by developing new drugs and therapies.
But concerns have already been raised that the same technology could be used maliciously to create new diseases.
In a commentary accompanying the publication in the journal Science, Dr Thomas Inglesby and Dr Moritz Hanke from the Center for Health Security at Johns Hopkins University wrote that the findings raise "urgent biosafety and biosecurity questions".
They said it was no longer a question of "whether generative viral genome design will exist" but whether it can be used without "enabling serious harm".
For example, they said new viruses with the potential to cause disease "should not be pursued".
The researchers themselves took steps to maximise safety. They excluded viruses that could infect complex organisms from the training database, performed the research on phage rather than viruses that infect people and it all took place in a secure laboratory.
Hie argues even existing safeguards go a long way towards "ensuring that the technology is used for good".
From computers bits to atoms
Viruses are not alive and it would take another significant leap for AI to generate living organisms.
The genetic code of the phage is around 5,400 base pairs (letters) long. The smallest genome of a living cell is around 500,000 base pairs. The human genome is three billion base pairs.
Hie says "it would probably be a lot of work, but not impossible" to attempt some simple organisms and they were "definitely interested in working towards" that.
Prof Marc Güell, from the synthetic biology lab at Pompeu Fabra University in Spain, said the study was a "very significant turning point" because for the "first time in history, we are beginning to design biology on a computer".
He said it "allows us to dream of exciting possibilities for tackling humanity's greatest challenges" such as developing phages to tackle disease, enzymes to treat genetic disorders and antibodies that could be used in immunotherapy.
Prof Patrick Cai, chair of synthetic genomics at the Manchester Institute of Biotechnology, said the study was an "important milestone".
"The significance extends far beyond phages – it suggests that genome language models are beginning to learn the design principles encoded by evolution, opening the door to AI-assisted genome writing."

title: Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
summary: The executive orders ban birth tourism and expand the existing definition of people whose children are not eligible for US birthright citizenship.
full_text:
Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
- Published
Donald Trump is trying again to scale back birthright citizenship in the US, weeks after the Supreme Court shot down his previous attempt to eliminate the right.
The president signed two executive orders on Thursday, including one that expands the existing definitions of non-citizens whose children are not eligible for birthright citizenship.
The second order bans so-called birth tourism, the practice of pregnant mothers coming to the US to give birth so that their babies will be citizens.
"This should have happened years ago, but we're taking care of it now," Trump said from the Oval Office, criticising the Supreme Court's rejection of his previous bid to end the 150-year-old policy.
"My Administration has guarded against the risks posed by malign foreign actors who attempt to swindle American citizens by taking advantage of the generosity of our Nation," the first executive order says.
That order prohibits the automatic citizenship of babies born in the United States to two non-citizen parents where one of the parents is: a member of a foreign terrorist group, a foreign government employee, has attempted to gain citizenship through fraudulent means, or is living in US territories where citizenship is not conferred by federal statute.
Birthright citizenship for people born in US territories such as Puerto Rico is codified by federal statute.
Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly railed against birth tourism, including accusing Russian and Chinese adversaries of taking advantage of birthright citizenship to infiltrate the US.
While announcing the executive orders from the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said that hundreds of thousands of babies have been born through birth tourism in the US.
The Migration Policy Institute, a nonpartisan research group, has said that the most expansive census-based estimate accounts for about 22,000 to 26,000 babies born in the US from birth tourism every year. Government data, according to the institute, showed that there were 9,600 births to mothers with foreign addresses in 2024.
"The idea (is) that people come here pretending to be a tourist, pretending to be a visitor," Stephen Miller, homeland security advisor and White House deputy chief of staff for policy, said while standing beside the president on Thursday.
"But the real reason they're here is to have a child, to make that child an automatic citizen, (to) leave our country and then have a US citizen child," he said, adding that thoe children then gain access to welfare benefits, the voting booth, and "all the other rights and privileges that belong solely to Americans".
Miller said the president has the authority to ban birth tourism under a section of the Immigration and Nationality Act, which grants the president the power to set exceptions and limitations on who can enter into the country.
On one of his first back days in office in 2025, Trump signed an executive order that tried to end birthright citizenship as guaranteed in the 14th Amendment to the US Constitution.
A legal battle brought the case to the Supreme Court, which in June ruled that Trump's 2025 policies could not stand and birthright citizenship remained the law.
The decision was a major blow to Trump's ongoing efforts to limit who can live, work, and become citizens in the US.
The high court made "a bad decision, very unfair decision", Trump said from the Oval Office on Thursday while announcing the executive orders. "Our country suffers because of it, and we're ending in a different way."
Gabriel Chin, a professor at the University of California Davis' School of Law, told the BBC that while parts of the order might hold up, other aspects "raise some serious constitutional questions".
Chin said the president does have some power to restrict people coming into the US specifically for the purposes of having a child.
"But once it does happen, once a child is born in the United States, I don't think the president has any power to decide that that child is not a citizen," he said, adding that the issue was settled in the Trump administration's recent loss in the Supreme Court.
He called birth tourism a "drop in the bucket" against the millions of births in the US.
"It's an unusual phenomenon," he said.

title: Met Police boss admits mistake over Cambridge professor plagiarism row
summary: Sir Mark Rowley says his force "dropped the ball" after it investigated a reporter looking into claims about Jason Arday.
full_text:
Met Police boss admits mistake over plagiarism row
- Published
The head of the Metropolitan Police has said his force should not have investigated a journalist who was looking into plagiarism claims about a University of Cambridge professor.
Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said officers "dropped the ball" when they looked into a complaint made against journalist Jack Grove over his attempts to contact Prof Jason Arday.
Sir Mark told broadcaster LBC the complaint should have been "screened out earlier on as not requiring investigation".
Arday, who resigned from Cambridge on Wednesday, has has admitted errors in his work, but denied plagiarism.
Times Higher Education (THE) reporter Grove said he had been investigating allegations Arday had plagiarised parts of his PhD, and contacted him in 2025 to offer him the right of reply.
"In early February I received a call from a Met police officer saying that a complaint had been raised against me by someone and Professor Arday was very distressed and I shouldn't contact him again," Grove told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
"It was a complete shock. Apparently it was for harassment but I hadn't contacted him for four months and then maybe I think I've only sent three or four emails to him in total."
The Met closed its inquiries into the case.
Sir Mark told LBC: "We dropped the ball on that one, let's not beat around the bush.
"A report came in of harassment or some crime like that, it should have been screened out as not requiring investigation...
"We shouldn't have made that call to him [Grove] and said that."
The University of Cambridge said on Tuesday it had begun an investigation into Arday, who became the institution's youngest black professor in 2023, following "new information" about his "academic qualifications and honorary appointments".
In a statement published by campaign group Good Law Project on Wednesday, Arday said the "relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love".
"I no longer wish to feel as though I am living under a constant spotlight, where every aspect of my life is subject to public examination and judgement," he said.
Speaking of his decision to step down he added it should not "be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me".
His resignation followed a series of media reports alleging he plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis completed at Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) and other research.
LJMU - which awarded his PhD in 2015 - had investigated the allegations that were made last year, but did not uphold the charges.
The Times reported Arday defended himself by arguing that he had not received adequate supervision during his PhD given his autism and "learning disabilities".
In an interview with the Times, Arday said that he could not afford a proofreader to catch mistakes when he started out in academia.
Further questions were raised in the press about the truth of other claims, including Arday saying he ran 600 miles in six days and that he raised £5.5m for charity.
The controversy has attracted a range of opinions, including within the academic community.
Kathleen Stock, a philosopher and former professor at Sussex University, said universities were "desperate for good press".
"The elite universities like Cambridge and Oxford had a particular problem because they are perceived to be quite harsh places, quite unkind places and very white places. And they wanted to change that impression," she told the Today programme.
Stock, who resigned her post in 2021 after a row over freedom of speech and her views on gender identity, said this was a "watershed" moment.
But Kehinde Andrews, who was previously professor of black studies at Birmingham City University, said the idea that black academics had an advantage because of their racial background was not true.
He told the BBC's Today programme: "What happens to black academics is we're not in an area where it's great and the left wing universities love us and they're trying to promote us.
"What happens is you work at a place for 12 years, you're very, very successful, and then you get made redundant. That's the experience of black academics."

title: Amanda Knox defends Fringe comedy show after claims it will 'trivialise violence'
summary: Knox, who was convicted and later acquitted of the murder of a British student, said she does not downplay the seriousness of Meredith Kercher's death.
full_text:
Amanda Knox defends Fringe comedy show after claims it will 'trivialise violence'
- Published
Amanda Knox, who was convicted and later acquitted of murdering British student Meredith Kercher in Italy in 2007, has defended her solo comedy show following calls for it to be cancelled.
The sold-out show called Cartwheel, which Knox will perform at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, discusses motherhood and how she will explain the case to her daughter.
Knox told the BBC she is not the first person to use comedy to talk about traumatic events and said her material focuses on "how the world is unsafe and unfair towards women".
But Stephanie Kercher, the victim's sister, said she is concerned it will "normalise and trivialise" violence against women, and Meredith, in particular.
Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Stephanie Kercher, said: "What I would say [to Knox] is to think about the family here, think about her friends and to turn the tables if it was your sister that this had happened to, because I know you have a sister as well."
Responding to the comments, Knox said: "The interesting irony of that is that my daughter is a huge motivation for me doing this show.
"It's about how the world is unsafe and unfair towards women and what it means to raise a daughter in that world, knowing how bad it can be.
"If they [Kercher's family] saw my show, they would recognise that."
A petition against the show, set up by a friend of Meredith, has been signed by nearly 5,000 people.
It states the show disrespects her memory and risks making light of such a harrowing event.
Stephanie Kercher added she did not believe Meredith would find these topics of any comedic value.
She said: "Our family's pain is immense. I can't explain to you how much pain our family have been through, and also we're talking two decades later now, this pain.
"I think that if it was a generic theme, as many comedy shows are, even when they're pushing the boundaries, it would be different.
"Because this is associated with an individual case and individual person, I think that's where the worry lies here for me, because who else is this going to then open up this opportunity for?"
But Knox told BBC Scotland News she does not downplay the seriousness of the case and is respectful in her approach.
"I hope people will honestly engage in my work and recognise the deep heart and sensitivity that I bring to it as I tell a very personal story," she said.
The comedy show is set to run over 11 days in the Gilded Balloon Teviot.
Its title Cartwheel references a story that once claimed Knox did cartwheels in the police station after her British roommate's death.
She said the cartwheel becomes a metaphor throughout the show.
"It is about acknowledging that bad things happen in life which will turn you upside down," Knox said.
"But it's also about not letting that arrest your momentum because the only way you can land on your feet is through those difficult experiences."
Knox added she would love to have an open and honest conversation with Kercher's family but claimed she has never had the opportunity.
"It would be incredible for them to see me for who I really am instead of the idea that was delivered to them by people in bad hands," she said.
Since Meredith Kercher's death, Knox has written two books about her imprisonment and served as an executive producer on the biographical drama The Twisted Tale of Amanda Knox.
Now 39, she is married with two children and lives in Washington state.
Knox, from Seattle, and Kercher, from Surrey, were both exchange students sharing a house in the university town of Perugia.
Alongside her then-boyfriend, Raffaele Sollecito, Knox was arrested on suspicion of murdering Kercher, 21, who was found dead in their house.
Her throat had been cut and she had been sexually assaulted.
Knox was found guilty and spent four years in an Italian prison before she and Sollecito were acquitted through an appeal.
She returned home to the US in 2011.
A retrial in 2014 reinstated Knox and Sollecito's convictions but Italy's top appeals court finally overturned them in 2015.
Ivory Coast-born Rudy Guede served 13 years of a 16-year sentence for Kercher's murder after his fingerprints were found at the scene.
The court ruled he did not act alone but after Knox and Sollecito were acquitted, no other accomplices were convicted.

title: Village sees 50 days without rain during summer heatwave
summary: Wisley in Surrey has recorded no rain for 50 consecutive days - with little rain on the horizon as Matt Taylor from BBC Weather explains.
full_text:
Village sees 50 days without rain during summer heatwave
- Published
As the extremely dry spell continues across much of England and Wales, a small village in Surrey has notched up 50 consecutive days without rain this summer.
Wisley, most famous for being the site of the 240-acre garden owned by the Royal Horticultural Society, saw 36 continuous dry days back in the hot summer of 1976 - but has comfortably exceeded that number so far this year, with no rainfall since mid-June.
It comes after the driest July for England and Wales since Met Office records began 190 years ago, external.
Meanwhile, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued further yellow heat health alerts, external for most of England this weekend as the temperatures start to build again. The alerts cover the Humber, West and East Midlands, east of England, London, and the South East and South West from 09:00 BST on Saturday until 21:00 on Tuesday 11 August.
Why has there been no rain?
High pressure has dominated the weather since late-spring, caused by a large zone of air descending through the atmosphere. This largely acts to prevent rain clouds building up.
Only 6.5mm (0.25in) of rainfall was recorded in England and only 9.3mm in Wales - both less than half of the previous records for the nations.
As this has been centred across mainland Europe, southern areas of England and Wales have been impacted more by the dry weather.
Any rain that has fallen has been in the form of well scattered showers meaning many areas - like Wisley - have completely missed out.
Scotland and Northern Ireland, by contrast, have been on the edge of the high pressure systems where rain clouds are occasionally directed.
Is there another heatwave on the way?
The same high pressure systems that have kept rain away have also brought sunny skies and surges of prolonged heat.
Despite the current return to more normal August conditions, forecasts are suggesting further surges of heat over the coming week prompting the UKHSA yellow heat health alerts.
Daytime temperatures in the affected areas are expected to climb back into the high 20s if not low 30s Celsius. Some forecasts hint at the potential of a further heat spike later next week with highs into the mid-30s possible.
The UKHSA is warning that minor impacts are likely across health and social care services. Use of healthcare services by vulnerable people is expected to increase, with a greater risk to life of vulnerable people.
There will also be an increased potential for indoor environments to become very warm, and water related incidents may increase, including risks from cold water shock and drowning.
When will it rain?
With parts of eastern Scotland in significant water scarcity, the whole of Wales and more than half of England in drought, there has been relief that some areas have seen some rain this week, particularly parts of Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England.
However, not enough fell in the drought-hit south to provide any meaningful relief with another water company introducing a ban on hosepipe use for its customers in Essex and Suffolk on Monday.
There is no defined amount of rain that would see a drought end. It depends on a number of factors including how much rain falls, where it falls, and how regular or prolonged the downpours are.
The speed at which rivers, reservoirs and groundwater storage tops up is also important, but this needs to be balanced out against the demand we and industry put on water supply.
The drought in 2025, which lasted around six months for some, only ended in the autumn when the UK experienced "weather whiplash" - a sudden change in weather patterns that brought weeks of above-average rainfall.
Despite forecasts showing our weather becoming slightly more variable over the next few weeks, including further hotter spells again, dry conditions continue to dominate for many and there is still no sign of any drought-busting rainfall.

title: Conservatives pledge to ban foreign nationals from social housing
summary: They claim around 230,000 homes would become available under their plan to limit social housing entitlements.
full_text:
Conservatives pledge to ban foreign nationals from social housing
- Published
The Conservatives have said they would end the provision of social housing for foreign nationals in England if they win power at the next election.
The party said ending new tenancies for all foreign nationals, as well as current tenancies for couples where neither person is a UK, Irish or EU citizen, would free up an estimated 228,144 homes for British families.
The Conservatives said Labour had "lost control of immigration" and British families had been left sitting on housing waiting lists as a result.
But Labour said the policy was an "unserious, unworkable proposal, copied from Reform, that does nothing to tackle the housing crisis the Tories themselves created".
In June, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said he would make it a requirement for foreign national tenants to find private accommodation within three months or face possible deportation if his party won power.
Under the Tory proposals, ineligible tenants would be expected to move out of their homes within six months.
Any single person currently living in social housing who is not a UK, Irish or EU citizen would lose their social home. This includes those with or without children.
Couples, where neither of them are UK or EU citizens, and they do not have EU settled status, will also lose their entitlement.
Anyone with EU settled status would not be evicted.
For future tenancies, UK nationals and those with EU settled status would be eligible but any new EU citizens without settled status would not be.
Foreign nationals with settled status, refugee status, or specific humanitarian protections can currently qualify for social housing.
Asylum seekers are not eligible for social housing, unless in exceptional circumstances such as domestic abuse cases.
Social housing, usually provided by housing associations or local councils, is typically cheaper and more secure than privately rented homes.
When they were last in government in 2024, the Conservatives were considering plans to make it a requirement for foreign nationals to have to live in the UK for 10 years before qualifying for social housing.
There are 1.34 million households on social housing waiting lists, as of March 2025, the latest government figures.
The vast majority of social housing lettings are given to single people.
In 2024-25, most lead tenants of new social lettings, the person in whose name the social home is rented, were UK nationals - 89% or 233,000 tenants.
In the same period, 2.3% of new lettings were given to refugees - 800 refugees were UK nationals, while the remaining 3,900 were non-UK nationals.
The most common nationality of refugees in a new social letting was Afghanistan with the second most common being Ukraine.
'Homelessness risk'
Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said: "Making Britain your home should be earned by working, paying tax and integrating.
"It should not come with a free ride on the benefits system. Britain cannot be a cash machine for the world.
"Labour has lost control of immigration and lost control of the welfare bill, and it is British families picking up the bill and sitting on waiting lists."
Labour said the Conservative policy would primarily affect refugees and long-term UK residents who had contributed to the country, while also leaving more families at risk of homelessness.
"No amount of headline-chasing, or following Reform to the extremes, can hide the damage the Tories did to our housing system. The least they could do is acknowledge their failures and apologise," the spokesperson said.
Housing and homelessness charity Shelter said there were already strict rules on eligibility for social housing and accommodation was not handed out to people on arrival.
"These divisive plans would brutally kick people out of their homes, including thousands of families and pensioners who have lived in them for decades," chief executive Sarah Elliott said.
"The housing emergency is caused by successive governments failure to build enough genuinely affordable social homes - not by who accesses social housing."
Reform UK's home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said the Conservatives were trying to copy his party's policy but accused them of not going far enough as their proposed ban does not include those with EU settled status.
"Incredibly, Kemi Badenoch's new policy is to allow tens of thousands of foreign nationals from the EU to occupy British social housing funded by British taxpayers," he said.
"Reform UK will ensure British social housing is strictly for British citizens."
