title: 39 moves across five countries - football's ultimate journeyman
summary: As he prepares to manage in the FA Cup for the first time, Zeph Thomas tells BBC Sport about his extraordinary career path spanning 39 moves in 18 years.
full_text:
39 moves across five countries - the footballer forever in motion
- Published
"If I I didn't get the money I thought I deserved, I'd be off," says Zeph Thomas, as he attempts to explain a career path that has spanned an extraordinary 39 moves in 18 years.
The Bradford-born winger, 36, is one of football's ultimate journeymen.
Rossington Main (five spells), Mickleover Sports (four spells), Frickley Athletic (three spells), Garden City Broncbusters (United States), Montegnee (Belgium), Thunder Bay Chill (Canada).
Thomas' list of former clubs goes on and on.
Cowdenbeath, Boston United, Harrogate Town, Scarborough Athletic, Stafford Rangers, Leek Town.
There's more. Lots more.
Ilkeston Town, Matlock Town, Goole, Glossop North End, Stocksbridge Park Steels, Brighouse Town (two spells), Emley, Harrogate Railway Athletic, Sheffield, Shaw Lane, Belper Town, Parkgate, Campion, Eccleshill United, Selby Town and Ossett United.
But could Thomas' life on the move be over?
The former St Kitts & Nevis international has embraced his player-manager role at ninth-tier South Yorkshire club Dearne & District since being appointed in 2024.
After winning the Northern Counties East League First Division last season, the village club based in Goldthorpe, near Barnsley, play their first ever FA Cup match on Saturday when they visit Runcorn Town - one of 219 extra preliminary round ties scheduled to take place.
"We've gone from being in the Doncaster Saturday League in 2021 to playing in the FA Cup," adds Thomas.
"It's massive for the area because they have never seen this team play in the competition."
'I was petulant and naive'
Thomas' career started at Rotherham United when former Manchester United forward Mark Robins was youth team coach.
He was released in 2008 without making a senior appearance, a decision that did not come as a complete surprise to him.
"I was a bit petulant and naive back then," he says.
"I remember scoring in a reserve game and then the next day we had to come in for recovery runs. At the time, I didn't think I should have been doing any of that.
"If my attitude had been better I would probably have been fine to be honest."
With his dreams of making it big in the full-time game shattered, Thomas embarked on a remarkable journey across non-league football in England, while there were spells at clubs in Kansas, Ontario, Scotland and Belgium.
In 2013-14 alone, he was on the books of Sheffield, Mickleover Sports, Scarborough Athletic, Matlock Town and Goole, while he started 2016-17 back at Mickleover Sports and then went to Shaw Lane, Stafford Rangers, Frickley Athletic... before ending back at Mickleover.
The non-league club where he spent his longest spell was Brighouse Town (second stint) between 2020 and 2023.
While at Stocksbridge Park Steels, he played against Jamie Vardy, then at Halifax Town, before Vardy went on to play for England and win the Premier League with Leicester City in 2015-2016.
In 2013, Thomas almost quit playing after suffering a groin injury. He worked in a call centre in Rotherham and thought about joining the army before being given an opportunity to resume his career at Thunder Bay Chill in Ontario.
Has he kept a record of his numerous destinations?
"Not at all. There's definitely been too many to count," adds Thomas.
"It's been a good experience but it could have been better. I moved up or went sideways for more money.
"But playing in different countries was a great experience and I would encourage all young players to go and experience that if they get a chance.
"I worked under different coaches with different ideas and philosophies."
After a life spent seemingly on the road, Thomas does not have so far to travel to games these days.
He lives a five-minute walk from Dearne & District's ground, with wife Marie and their two children, Jerome, 11, and Lucia, seven.
Thomas combines his part-time job with Dearne & District, who attracted a crowd of 453 for the home league game with Penistone Church on 28 July, with his role as lead coach for Derby County's Under-12s.
He is still registered to play for the non-league club but these days prefers to coach from the dugout and pass on his experience to players.
"Sometimes I feel a bit of a hypocrite because I used to move clubs for extra money," he says.
"Now I say to my players, 'keep on doing what you're doing because the money will come'."

title: ‘Still searching for truth’: Daughter of Sikh activist killed 30 years ago
summary: Jaswant Singh Khalra's daughter Navkiran reflects on slain father's life and legacy, which also inspired a recent film.
full_text:
‘Still searching for truth’: Daughter of Sikh activist killed 30 years ago
Slain Indian activist Jaswant Singh Khalra’s daughter, Navkiran, reflects on his life and legacy, which also inspired a recent film on rights abuses by officials during crackdown on Punjab separatist movement.
On the morning of September 6, 1995, human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra was washing his car outside his home in Amritsar city, India’s Punjab state.
His wife, Paramjit Kaur Khalra, a librarian, was getting ready to leave for work; their son, Janmeet, and daughter, Navkiran, were getting ready for school.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Why is India blocking film on a man who counted Punjab insurgency killings?
- list 2 of 4Sikh group in Canada slams India over new report into 2023 activist killing
- list 3 of 4Indian national admits role in plot to assassinate US Sikh leader
- list 4 of 4Diljit Dosanjh’s new film is a global success. Why can’t Indians watch it?
Nothing about the morning suggested that, within hours, their lives would be changed forever.
Minutes after Paramjit and the children left home, Khalra was picked up by the police, secretly tortured for days in custody, and later murdered. His body was never found.
Khalra was killed because of his investigation into thousands of disappearances and extrajudicial killings by the Indian security forces during a separatist movement launched by Punjab’s Sikh community in the 1980s to establish a homeland, called Khalistan.
In June 1984, the government sent troops inside Amritsar’s Golden Temple, Sikhism’s holiest site, where hundreds of rebels were believed to be hiding. Hundreds of people, including Sikh religious leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, were killed in Operation Blue Star.
The military operation led to the assassination of the then-Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by two of her Sikh bodyguards in October that year. Gandhi’s assassination triggered anti-Sikh riots across the country, killing thousands.
In Punjab, a brutal crackdown on the Khalistan movement started, with security forces given special powers to torture, forcibly disappear and even kill thousands of rebels and suspects.
Among those forcibly disappeared were one of Khalra’s friends and the friend’s mother, pushing the 42-year-old bank manager on a pursuit that saw him investigate thousands of similar cases.
In 1995, Khalra filed a petition with the Supreme Court of India, claiming the police had cremated 25,000 such bodies, labelling them “unidentified” and “unclaimed”. Police said his claim was exaggerated.
As he mobilised families who had lost loved ones and continued to seek answers from the police, he was repeatedly threatened with consequences and eventually abducted from his home and killed.
Khalra’s abduction and murder became one of India’s most consequential human rights cases. His wife’s campaign for justice forced the government to order an investigation. Five police officials are currently serving life sentences for Khalra’s killing.
But for three decades now, thousands of other people across Punjab and beyond are still seeking justice and closure over the disappearance and presumed killing of their loved ones.
Last month, a feature film, titled Satluj – after a river in Punjab in which many bodies, including Khalra’s, are believed to have been thrown – attempted to answer some of their questions by revisiting his life and work.
The government blocked the film within 48 hours of its release on a streaming platform over “security concerns”. But Sikh groups and rights activists organised community screenings of the film across Punjab and other parts of India and abroad, reigniting a decades-old debate over Khalra’s legacy, state accountability, and freedom of expression.
Thirty years after her father’s disappearance and murder, Navkiran Kaur Khalra reflects on his life, legacy and the long fight for justice, in an exclusive conversation with Al Jazeera.
Al Jazeera: Take us back to September 6, 1995. What do you remember about the day your father disappeared?
Navkiran Kaur Khalra: It was an ordinary morning. My mother was getting ready for work, and my brother and I left for school. As she stepped outside around 9am, she noticed several police officers standing outside our house. She didn’t think much of it and went to work. When I returned from school later that day, my brother came running towards me in panic and said, ‘The police have taken Papa’. That was the beginning of a nightmare that changed our lives forever.
AJ: When did your family realise his was not a routine detention, and that your father had been forcibly disappeared?
Khalra: We immediately went to the police station in Tarn Taran [a place in Punjab], but the officers denied everything. They said it was impossible that anyone had picked him up from their jurisdiction and discouraged us from filing a complaint. Later, my mother started receiving phone calls from the then-deputy inspector general of police. He told her, ‘Withdraw the case against us and we’ll tell you where he is.’ He even said they could bring my father back alive and create a story that he had gone to Pakistan and had now returned. For years, we searched everywhere. We explored every possibility because we genuinely believed he might still be alive.
AJ: People around the world know Jaswant Singh Khalra as a human rights activist. Who was he to you as a father?
Khalra: Before he became known internationally, he was simply our father. He was a Sikh, a human rights activist and a concerned citizen, but at home, he loved spending time with us. He brought us gifts, took us on family vacations, and made time for us whenever he could. We were an ordinary middle-class family. No matter how busy he was, he always came home. He travelled to Chandigarh [Punjab’s capital] almost every day, spending five or six hours on the road, but however late it became, he returned home to us.
AJ: What kind of home did you grow up in during Punjab’s insurgency?
Khalra: As children, we didn’t fully understand what was happening around us. Our home was always full of lawyers, activists, journalists and visitors from India and abroad. The walls were covered with photographs of people who had been killed in alleged extrajudicial killings across Punjab. Those images became part of our childhood. Looking back, I realise how unusual that was.
AJ: At what point did your family realise your father’s work had put him in serious danger?
Khalra: By early 1995, the threats had become very serious. When the police claimed that missing people had simply gone abroad, my father would hold press conferences and ask, ‘If they have gone abroad, why are their names in the cremation records?’
Around February 1995, my grandfather received a message from a ruling party legislator, telling my father to stop his work before it was too late. We were also told that permission had been obtained from the government to eliminate him.
Friends and lawyers urged him to seek police protection, but he refused. He used to say, ‘I visit families whose loved ones have disappeared because of the police. How can I go to them with the same police standing beside me?’
AJ: Shortly before he disappeared, your father asked your mother if she could take care of the children. Looking back, what does that moment mean to you?
Khalra: A day before he was abducted, he turned to my mother and asked, ‘Will you be able to take care of the children?’ At the time, she didn’t think much about it. It sounded like an ordinary question. Only afterwards did we realise he may have known something was going to happen.
AJ: Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh was assassinated in a suicide bombing on August 31, 1995, only days before your father was abducted. Singh’s government had led the state’s crackdown on the Sikh rebellion, and the killing triggered fears of a renewed security response. Your father had been documenting alleged police abuses during that period.

title: Despite South China Sea clashes, Chinese and Filipino police boost cooperation
summary:

Chief Jose Melencio Nartatez Jnr hosted Wang Xizhang, the executive director general of Fujian’s Public Security Department, on Tuesday, according to the official Philippine News Agency.

full_text:
1,230 times the size of Hong Kong: China deploys drones, AI as Typhoon Dolphin nears coast
Coastal provinces halt shipping and activities and evacuate fishermen as storm targets Zhejiang and Fujian
By Friday morning, the typhoon was about 820km from China’s east coast and was expected to land from Sunday afternoon to Monday morning somewhere between Zhejiang province in eastern China and northern Fujian, the National Meteorological Centre said.
The centre maintained a yellow alert, the third-strongest on a four-tier scale, warning of strong wind and rain in Zhejiang, Fujian and Taiwan.
The centre’s meteorologist Shen Yuyang said that by Friday morning, the typhoon had grown to nearly 13 times the size of Zhejiang, which is equivalent to 1,230 times the size of Hong Kong. It was not clear where it might travel after landing, said the centre, which estimated it could go west or northwest.
As the typhoon entered the 48-hour alert zone, Chinese authorities were busy preparing with new technology, state broadcaster CCTV said on Thursday. An artificial intelligence forecasting system at the National Marine Environmental Forecasting Centre could allow prediction of the typhoon’s route, strength and landfall factors for the next 240 hours, the report said.
The centre said the typhoon’s large wind radius meant inland residents should also pay attention to it, not just those living on the coast. Multiple regions could see heavy rain, including in Zhejiang, Fujian, Jiangxi, Hunan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Henan and Shandong provinces, CCTV said while issuing a caution for residents to check for flash flood alerts.
In Zhejiang, a level 2 emergency response – the second highest in a four-tier system – was launched on Friday morning, with authorities halting 162 ferry routes and 193 construction projects on the water, and docking 474 ships, while 15 tow boats were standing by in case of emergency, according to CCTV.

title: Colombia on the brink: ELN guerrilla group prepares for return to war
summary:
As Abelardo de la Espriella takes office as president vowing a new military offensive, the country’s last leftwing rebels are getting ready to fight back

As the boat approached the riverbank, camouflaged figures watched from the tree line.

Behind them, in the dim understory of the jungle, a commander of the National Liberation Army (ELN) sat with his rifle on his lap, amid the buzz and whine of insects and the thwacks of machetes on bamboo as his troops set up camp, hidden from enemy drones.

Continue reading...
full_text:
As the boat approached the riverbank, camouflaged figures watched from the tree line.
Behind them, in the dim understory of the jungle, a commander of the National Liberation Army (ELN) sat with his rifle on his lap, amid the buzz and whine of insects and the thwacks of machetes on bamboo as his troops set up camp, hidden from enemy drones.
Colombia’s 62-year old armed conflict is on the brink of a new chapter, with the country’s new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, who takes office on Friday, vowing an end to peace talks and launch a new military offensive. Colombia’s last guerrilla group says it is ready for whatever might come.
“Where we can go on the offensive, we will,” said the commander of the group’s Western War Front, who goes by the moniker Yerson. “And if the ELN leadership says we have to carry out a military offensive at the national level, we will. Attacks in cities, in the countryside, wherever.”
Yerson and his troops were deep in the Pacific department of Chocó, in an ELN stronghold accessible only after hours of river travel, where humid heat soaks through the cloud cover.
Occasional communities, each a line of wooden shacks on stilts, broke the dense forest on the banks. Giant mining barges were moored on the river, with diggers clawing up the riverbed to extract the particles of gold it contains.
The ELN and rival armed groups fight to control the San Juan River, its resources and its population. At one point in the journey, armed men from the Gulf Clan, a violent paramilitary group, stopped the Guardian’s boat to question the passengers, before promising to liberate the area from the ELN.
Yerson was unfazed. “All of the ELN territories are being invaded by bands of mercenaries,” he said. “They are very violent, but they are not disputing political power.”
Colombia’s conflict began in the 1960s, rooted in extreme land inequality and exclusionary politics. Leftwing guerrillas emerged to challenge the state, battling government forces later allied with rightwing paramilitaries, forerunners of the Gulf Clan. Money from cocaine trafficking fuelled all sides. The conflict has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
Along with the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), the ELN was the most important of the guerrilla groups. Founded in 1964, it fused Marxism-Leninism with Che Guevara’s foco theory — the idea that a small armed band in a remote rural area can eventually topple the state — and Liberation theology, which framed the struggle against poverty and oppression as an expression of Christian faith.
In their pursuit of revolution, the two groups have carried out killings and kidnappings, and forced the confinement and displacement of civilian populations.
The Farc demobilised in 2016 after striking a peace deal with the Colombian state, but the ELN says its members will only lay down arms after the country’s political and economic system has been transformed.
“The Farc surrendered in exchange for nothing,” said Yerson, adding that subsequent presidents have failed to fully implement the peace deal, while former Farc combatants have been killed.
Gustavo Petro, a leftist who was a guerrilla with the defunct M-19 in the 1980s, was elected president in 2022 on a promise of “total peace”, vowing to make good on the Farcdeal and negotiate with all of Colombia’s remaining armed groups on the left and right.
But after a few years, almost all the talks – including those with the largest groups — the ELN, the Gulf Clan and Farc dissidents who refused to demobilise in 2016 — either stalled or collapsed.
Yerson rejected the idea that the election of Colombia’s first leftist president meant that the ELN’s goals could be achieved through the current political system.
“They handed out lands [to the poor]. They did a kind of pension reform. They were looking for ways to improve healthcare,” he said. “But in the end these are small things. They don’t help with the popular awakening.”
In Yerson’s telling, Petro was allowed to take power by the “Colombian oligarchy”, which needed to pacify the people after an explosion of inequality protests in 2019 and 2021, but knew he “was never going to undertake fundamental reforms, that he could be controlled”.
Colombia’s political system “is not the democracy it claims to be”, he said. “That is where the trap is.”
Now the ELN faces a very different proposition in the form of De la Espriella, a Trump-admiring millionaire who rose to prominence as a criminal lawyer representing accused leaders of the AUC, a rightwing paramilitary group that fought the guerrillas and killed civilians accused of collaborating with them..
De la Espriella has given Colombia’s armed groups a month to submit to him or face the consequences, while promising to deepen security cooperation with the US and build mega-prisons inspired by the Salvadoran president, Nayib Bukele.
Security analysts, however, say armed groups have gathered strength and resources in recent years. The ELN has about 6,300 members between armed fighters and unarmed support, spread across Colombia and Venezuela.
The 60 or so fighters in the camp were evenly split between men and women, indigenous and Afro-Colombian members. “The majority [of the ELN] has always been the poor, the lowest down,” said Yerson. “Here, as Chocó is more Afro-Indigenous, that’s what we are.”
Each of them had a modern assault rifle, either an AK-47 or an AR-15, some with “Made in USA” stamped on the body. One also had a .50 calibre sniper rifle, the bullets of which can punch through vehicles, while another flew a drone.
The camp was deep in ELN territory, and they were relaxed. When someone took out a portable speaker and began to play vallenatos – popular Colombian folksongs – they left their rifles resting against trees or slung them over their backs and paired up to dance, suddenly looking like the young Colombians they are.
Various groups, including the UN and Human Rights Watch, have accused the ELN of recruiting minors — but Yerson said their rules only allow people over 16 to join.
It was impossible to verify details of his troops’ backgrounds, as they had been told not to talk. Yerson presented two women to be interviewed in his presence, but they struggled to speak, apparently afraid of saying the wrong thing.
Yerson himself described the ELN as “a life choice” for Colombia’s poor, who have few options. “Maybe that’s why they join, but once they are here they come to understand why we are fighting,” he said.
The ELN functions by taxing “every commercial entity” in the territory it controls, and in Chocó that means illegal gold mining and logging are their key sources of income, said Yerson. It also carries out kidnappings for ransom.
“We are an embryonic state, and every state takes taxes,” he said. “If they can strangle us economically, we will cease to exist as a rebel organisation.”
Yerson claimed coca cultivation has disappeared in ELN territory in Chocó. He denied the group was involved in the drug trafficking, but acknowledged it taxes the business like any other.
The US, which has given its military a new role to take on “narcoterrorism” across the Americas, might not think much of that distinction.
“The question of guilt doesn’t matter to the US. What matters to them are interests,” said Yerson. “We are the only guerrilla group with political principles left standing in Colombia and the world. We will always be something they want to destroy.”
He says the ELN will not simply be on the defensive, but will strike back where it can. A car bomb attributed to the group exploded outside a police station near the border with Venezuela last week, injuring 12 police officers and three civilians, and drone attacks have become common.

title: Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
full_text:
Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
The crypto market maker can now trade US stocks and options and support ETFs as crypto moves closer to traditional markets.
- Wintermute’s U.S. arm has officially registered with the SEC and joined FINRA, securing broker-dealer status for its institutional operations.
- The firm is now authorized to trade U.S. stocks and options, provide liquidity for ETFs, and self-clear digital asset securities for proprietary accounts.
- Wintermute plans to focus initially on crypto-linked markets, with intentions to scale into tokenized stocks pending necessary regulatory approvals.
Crypto market maker Wintermute has secured broker-dealer status in the U.S., giving the firm a regulated route into Wall Street as crypto trading and traditional securities markets draw closer together.
New York-based Wintermute USA LLC registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). The unit will operate as a proprietary trading firm rather than a retail broker.
The registration lets Wintermute trade stocks and equity options, provide liquidity to exchanges and over-the-counter counterparties, and act as an authorized participant for exchange-traded funds (ETFs), including crypto-linked funds.
Authorized participants create and redeem large blocks of ETF shares, a process that helps keep an ETF's market price close to the value of its holdings.
Wintermute described the unit as proprietary-only and did not announce retail brokerage services.
Authorized participants create and redeem blocks of ETF shares directly with fund issuers, helping keep fund prices aligned with their underlying assets.
The registration also lets Wintermute seek market-making roles on exchanges including the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. The firm has already lined up ETF issuers to work with, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Wintermute handles more than $10 billion in average daily trading volume across over 60 centralized and decentralized venues, according to the company.
The approval follows a longer U.S. buildout. Wintermute opened its New York headquarters last year and later asked the SEC to confirm that broker-dealers could trade tokenized securities for their own accounts, self-clear transactions and hold proprietary positions through wallet software.
Wintermute joins crypto firms including Ripple, GSR and Crypto.com that have acquired or built regulated US securities businesses as the line between crypto markets and traditional finance narrows.
Ripple completed its $1.25 billion purchase of prime broker Hidden Road in 2025, while GSR acquired broker-dealer Equilibrium Capital Services. Crypto.com bought Watchdog Capital in 2024.

title: Ethereum staking token weETH splits from restaking as rewards debate heats up
full_text:
Ethereum staking token weETH splits from restaking as rewards debate heats up
The move separates ordinary Ethereum staking from higher-risk restaking exposure as a new proposal to cap validator rewards divides the staking sector.
- Ether.fi has removed restaking from its main token, weETH, turning it into a plain Ethereum staking token and shifting restaking to a new token, weETHs.
- The change lets users choose between standard staking rewards with weETH or higher-yield, higher-risk restaking exposure with weETHs.
- Ether.fi’s move comes as Ethereum researchers propose cutting staking rewards to zero once staking participation crosses a threshold, a plan Ether.fi’s founder argues would hurt smaller stakers and staking-based products.
Ether.fi, which holds about $3.55 billion of customer deposits and is one of the largest staking businesses in crypto, has stripped restaking out of weETH, its main product, leaving it as a plain token that earns ordinary Ethereum staking rewards.
Anyone wanting the extra yield now has to hold a second token, weETHs.
Staking means locking up ether to help run Ethereum and getting paid for it — whereas restaking puts that same ether to work a second time, securing other services for extra rewards on top.
The tradeoff is that it doubles the ways a holder can be penalised, since a failure on either system can cost them part of their deposit.
For current holders:
You now have a clearer choice between basic staking exposure and additional restaking exposure depending on your goals
For new users:
This simply makes the EtherFi stack easier to understand
Until this week, anyone holding weETH was taking on both risks whether they wanted the extra rewards or not. Now the choice is theirs: Hold weETH for plain staking, or weETHs to take the restaking rewards and the extra risk that comes with them.
Ether.fi has captured roughly $223 million in annualized fees and about $51 million in annualized revenue. In the second quarter, it earned $41 million in gross revenue and nearly $10 million in earnings after rewards and other costs, with only $30,000 of value distributed to ETHFI holders through buybacks.
The split lands as Ethereum's staking economics are under debate.
A group of Ethereum researchers, one from the Ethereum Foundation, proposed this week that the network stop paying people to stake once half of all ether is locked up. Under the current setup the payment never falls to zero no matter how much gets staked, so there is always a reason to stake more, and they argue that concentrates ether with a handful of large custodians.
Their proposed fix destroys a growing share of the rewards until the payment disappears entirely at around 60 million ether. About a third is staked today.
Ether.fi founder Mike Silagadze was among the proposal’s critics, arguing it would push out smaller stakers and weaken the products built on staking rewards, his own among them.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin flat at $64,300 before US jobs report, with oil back as a headwind
full_text:
Live updates: Bitcoin flat at $64,300 before US jobs report, with oil back as a headwind
Brent climbed on stalled Hormuz talks, reviving the inflation worry that has capped bitcoin all summer. Today's US payrolls print is the next catalyst.
Bitcoin miners transfer $37 million in BTC to NYDIG
Bitcoin miners’ transfers to exchanges often signal preparations to sell. However, NYDIG also offers custody and financing, meaning the coins may remain in custody or serve another purpose. Ten hours ago, according to Lookonchain, MARA Holdings (MARA) deposited 200 BTC ($12.86M), while Riot Platforms (RIOT) transferred another 381 BTC ($24.51M) to NYDIG.
MetaMask launches AI-powered Agent Wallet for hands-free crypto trading
MetaMask announced the deployment of its Agent Wallet, which allows users to put AI agents to work on their behalf to monitor markets and execute crypto trades, swaps and other onchain transactions. Users can connect tools such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, set how much an agent can spend and which protocols it can use and then choose a more cautious Guard Mode or a less restrictive Beast Mode.
The wallet supports HyperLiquid and selected Ethereum-compatible networks or blockchains, and MetaMask says it adds transaction simulations, threat checks and Miner Extractable Value (MEV)-protection tools before an agent completes a trade.
Metals momentum continues on Friday. Gold is up a further 1%, trading near $4,300 an ounce, while silver has surged above $64 an ounce, gaining more than 4% over the past 24 hours. The metals appear to be the biggest beneficiaries of the AI slowdown, which has prompted a rotation out of AI stocks and into precious metals.
Nothing good happens when the 10-year yield is above 4.5%, Fidelity's Timmer says
Nothing good happens when the yield on the U.S. 10-year Treasury note trades above 4.5%, Fidelity’s Director of Global Macro Jurrien Timmer said Friday.
“Long-term bond yields are on the move again, with the 10-year yield well into the danger zone at 4.73%. As I have written many times, recent history suggests that nothing good happens above 4.5%,” he noted.
The rise in yields could be driven by several factors, Timmer explained.
One possibility is a reverse “crowding out” effect: rather than heavy government borrowing squeezing out private-sector investment, insatiable demand for financing from AI companies may be diverting investor appetite away from Treasuries.
Another explanation is growing skepticism that a hawkish Federal Reserve will back its rhetoric with meaningful action. Alternatively, the move may reflect the consequences of a less transparent Fed, as reduced clarity tends to increase uncertainty and push up risk premia.
“Less transparency means more uncertainty, and more uncertainty usually means high risk premia. Either way, we have a bear steepening on our hands,” he noted.
Hardening bond yields often create a headwind for stocks and emerging technologies such as cryptocurrencies.
SK Hynix will invest 54 trillion won, about $38 billion, to expand its chipmaking facilities in South Korea, the company said Friday. It is building new fabs in Yongin and Cheongju to meet what it called the continuously growing demand for memory in the AI era.
The spend is one of the largest single commitments yet from the memory maker, whose stock has been among the most volatile of the AI trade this year, swinging the Kospi through sharp selloffs and a record US listing.
For crypto, it reads as another sign the AI infrastructure spending that bitcoin has loosely tracked is still climbing.
Bitcoin flat at $64,350 before the jobs report, with oil back as a headwind
Bitcoin traded near $64,350 on Friday, unchanged on the week, as the whole market drifted ahead of the US payrolls report, per CoinDesk data. Ether held at $1,903 and the rest of the majors sat within a point or two, a market waiting on the data rather than moving on anything of its own.
The setup turned slightly less friendly overnight. Brent rose 1.4% to $83.61 after reports Iran will try to restrict US and Israeli ships through the Strait of Hormuz and demand compensation from countries it deems hostile before letting them pass, stalling the deal that had been pulling oil lower. Higher crude revives the inflation worry that keeps the Fed leaning tight, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed seven basis points on it during the US session.
That macro chain is the one bitcoin has been stuck inside all summer. Oil up feeds inflation, inflation keeps yields and the dollar firm, and firmer financial conditions cap risk assets. The dollar just posted its best day in two weeks, which is the opposite of the easing setup bulls want.
Today's jobs number is the release that matters. A soft print revives the case for the Fed to loosen and gives bitcoin room above its range. A strong one, stacked on climbing oil, hands the hawks another reason to hold, and the range that has held since May holds again. Watch the reaction in yields, not just the headline number.

title: Coldcard exploit pushes July losses to $247M as second-worst month of 2026
summary: The Coldcard exploit, which caused more than $100 million in losses, helped push July crypto thefts to $247 million, making it the second-worst month of 2026.
full_text:
Coldcard exploit pushes July losses to $247M as second-worst month of 2026
The Coldcard exploit, which caused more than $100 million in losses, helped push July crypto thefts to $247 million, making it the second-worst month of 2026.
July emerged as the second-worst month of 2026 for cryptocurrency thefts, largely due to the recent Coldcard exploit.
Hackers stole $247.4 million in crypto in July, the most this year after the $644 million stolen in April, according to DefiLlama data. The total was more than triple the $75 million stolen in June and the $60 million stolen in May.
The Coldcard exploit was the month’s biggest exploit, with at least $100 million in Bitcoin (BTC) stolen from 7,300 wallets across three confirmed attack waves, according to Galaxy Digital. The company also identified a suspected fourth wave that could bring total losses to about $130 million. DefiLlama’s hack tracker estimates losses tied to the Coldcard exploit at $115 million.
“July showed that even cold storage does not eliminate technological risks, which can put thousands of wallets at risk simultaneously,” research platform CryptoRank said in a Thursday X post.
Other notable July exploits included a $9 million hack against decentralized finance protocol Bonzo Lend, $2.6 million stolen from Cardano-based wallet SecondFi, $24 million stolen from Arbitrum-based perpetual exchange AFX and $7.5 million stolen through the Verus Ethereum Bridge.

full_text:
英國《金融時報》8 月 7 日引述知情人士報導，字節跳動正在訓練一個參數量上看 10 兆的 AI 模型，規模逼近 Anthropic 最前沿的 Mythos 系統。這個數字是月之暗面 Kimi K3（2.8 兆參數）的三倍多，產業估算 Mythos 5 約 8 兆、Fable 5 約 5 兆。該模型目前還在預訓練階段，這道工序通常要跑三到六個月才會進入微調與發布。
（前情提要：中國傳放行阿里、字節、DeepSeek 購買輝達 H200 晶片，川普鬆綁半年終核准）
（背景補充：加密貨幣進入 AI 軍備競賽：最強模型 Mythos 被閹割，幣安喊「我們還沒拿到」）
重點摘要
- FT 報導字節跳動正訓練參數量上看 10 兆的 AI 模型，目前仍在預訓練階段
- 10 兆參數是 Kimi K3（2.8 兆）的三倍多，產業估算 Mythos 5 約 8 兆參數
- 字節跳動 2026 年計畫採購約 140 億美元的輝達 AI GPU，訓練算力多在境外
字節跳動要把模型堆到 10 兆參數。英國《金融時報》週五引述知情人士報導，這家 TikTok 母公司正在訓練一個參數量最高上看 10 兆的 AI 模型，規模已經逼近 Anthropic 最前沿的 Mythos 系統。路透轉述時特別註明，無法立即證實這則報導。
把數字擺在一起比較有感。月之暗面 7 月開源的 Kimi K3 是 2.8 兆參數，已經是全球最大的開源權重模型，字節跳動這個是它的三倍多。至於對標的另一邊，產業估算 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 約 8 兆參數、公開版的 Fable 5 約 5 兆，不過 Anthropic 從來沒有公布過自家模型的參數量，這些都是外界推估。
進度上還早。該模型目前處在預訓練階段，這道工序一般要跑三到六個月，跑完才輪到微調，然後才談得上發布。換句話說，就算一切順利，這個模型最快也要到今年底或明年初才會露面。
追的是一個大眾用不到的模型
字節跳動選的對標對象很特別。Mythos 是 Anthropic 手上最強的模型，但它沒有對一般大眾開放，只透過 Project Glasswing 這個篩選過的計畫，提供給特定的資安夥伴使用。
目前拿到門票的包括 Coinbase、銀行科技商 FIS、漏洞回報平台 HackerOne，以及 Zcash 基金會旗下的 Shielded Labs。幣安、Fireblocks、以太坊基金會這些名字，到本週為止都還在排隊。
所以字節跳動要造的，是一個連幣安都還沒拿到使用權的模型的同級品。這件事的另一層意思是，前沿模型的「最強版本」已經不再是誰都能買到的商品，能不能用到取決於供應商願不願意給，而不是付不付得起錢。想繞開這個限制，就只剩自己造一個。
算力才是真正的門檻
參數堆到 10 兆，卡的從來不是想不想，而是有沒有卡。
字節跳動的解法分兩路走，境內這邊，中國 7 月傳出放行阿里巴巴、字節跳動、DeepSeek 採購輝達 H200 晶片，是川普政府鬆綁出口管制半年後首次核准；公司同時也找上高通下了數百萬顆客製 ASIC 的大單，把推理需求分流出去。
走境外這條路更直接，多家報導指出，字節跳動與其他中國科技巨頭把先進模型的訓練搬到東南亞，透過新加坡、馬來西亞的非中國業者租用機房，藉此接觸到輝達的 Blackwell 晶片。有報導估計，字節跳動 2026 年計畫採購約 140 億美元的輝達 AI GPU，中國廠商今年對 H200 的下單量更超過 200 萬顆，將近輝達現有庫存的三倍。
缺口還是很大。分析師估算，即使 H200 對中國的出口完全放行，美國 2026 年產出的 AI 算力仍是中國的 21 到 49 倍。10 兆參數這個目標要不要打折，最後多半不是由模型團隊決定的。
字節跳動現有的旗艦是 6 月底發布的 Doubao-Seed-2.1 Pro，官方說法是多項基準測試表現接近 GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 4.7 與 Gemini 3.1 Pro，豆包日均 token 調用量約 180 兆。從這個位置直接跳到 10 兆參數，是把整個量級往上拉了一整個量級。
常見問題
字節跳動的新 AI 模型有多大？
據《金融時報》報導，參數量上看 10 兆，是月之暗面 Kimi K3（2.8 兆參數）的三倍多。產業估算 Anthropic 最強的 Mythos 5 約 8 兆參數，字節跳動這個模型的規模已經接近。目前仍在預訓練階段。
Anthropic 的 Mythos 是什麼模型，一般人可以用嗎？
Mythos 是 Anthropic 手上最前沿的模型，沒有對一般大眾開放，只透過 Project Glasswing 提供給經篩選的資安夥伴。Coinbase、FIS、HackerOne 已取得存取權，幣安、Fireblocks、以太坊基金會仍在排隊等候。
還有一個變數在模型之外。北京 7 月傳出擬對自家 AI 模型祭出出口管制，豆包、阿里千問、Z.ai 全被點名。模型還沒練完，出不出得了國門這件事，已經先有了問號。

title: 那斯達克拍板年底開跑 23 小時交易：美股一天只休 1 小時，向全日無休交易邁進
summary:
那斯達克（Nasdaq）宣布 23 小時交易制度「Global Trading Hours」目標於 2026 […]

〈那斯達克拍板年底開跑 23 小時交易：美股一天只休 1 小時，向全日無休交易邁進〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
那斯達克（Nasdaq）宣布 23 小時交易制度「Global Trading Hours」目標於 2026 年 12 月 6 日上線，屆時美股一週五天、每天只休市 1 小時，交易時間從現行的 16 小時拉長到 23 小時。美國證券交易委員會（SEC）已在 4 月 10 日批准該提案，剩下的前提是 DTCC 清算與證券資訊處理器（SIP）完成夜間升級。加密市場 24/7 不打烊跑了十幾年，現在傳統股市正追上來。
（前情提要：美股也要 24 小時交易了！SEC 宣布 9 月圓桌會議，那斯達克最快下半年上線）
（背景補充：那斯達克攜手 Kraken 打造股票代幣化閘道！xStocks 串接鏈上鏈下市場，料 2027 上半年上線）
重點摘要
- 那斯達克 23 小時交易目標 2026/12/6 上線，日盤 4am-8pm、夜盤 9pm-4am（美東時間）
- SEC 已於 4 月 10 日批准，美股每日交易時間從 16 小時延長至 23 小時
- 夜盤設官方收盤價 ±20% 靜態價格區間，超出範圍的委託單直接拒單
那斯達克（Nasdaq）已經把日子訂下來了。這家全球第二大證券交易所宣布，23 小時交易制度「Global Trading Hours」目標在 2026 年 12 月 6 日正式上線，屆時美股一週跑五天，每天只在美東時間晚上 8 點到 9 點休市 1 小時，其餘 23 小時全部可以下單。
美國證券交易委員會（SEC）已於 4 月 10 日批准這項提案。那斯達克是在 2025 年 12 月 29 日遞件，從送審到拍板花了三個半月。
那斯達克董事長兼執行長 Adena Friedman 表態，「我們很樂於領導市場往 Always-On 轉變」，並說有信心為全球數位經濟中的受監管市場設下新標準。交易所講「Always-On」這個詞，用的是雲端服務的語彙，不是證券業的語彙。
休息 1 小時是技術極限
新制把一天切成兩段，日盤從美東時間凌晨 4 點跑到晚上 8 點，夜盤從晚上 9 點跑到隔天凌晨 4 點。中間那 1 小時不是留給交易員睡覺，是留給系統。
那斯達克要在這 60 分鐘內做維護測試，還要處理股利、股票分割這些隔天生效的公司行為。整週的節奏則是週日晚間 9 點開盤，一路跑到週五晚間 8 點收盤。
這也解釋了為什麼是 23 不是 24 無休交易。加密市場能做到 7×24 不打烊，是因為結算就在鏈上，傳統股市的清算還保持批次處理的架構，1 個小時就是現實的技術承載上限。
夜盤有 ±20% 護欄
那斯達克沒有把夜盤放生。夜間時段會套用靜態價格區間，一般以官方收盤價為基準上下各抓 20%，超出範圍的委託單直接拒單。
重大公司行為則整段避開夜盤。股票分割、合併、SPAC 出場、代號變更這類事件會在夜盤前掛上 M1 暫停代碼，等隔天上午 8 點才恢復交易。
白天仍然是主場。上午 9 點半到下午 4 點的正常時段依舊承擔主要的價格發現功能，夜盤的定位比較接近讓亞洲和歐洲投資人有地方反應消息，不是要取代開盤。
這個定位有數字撐著。目前美股現貨大約只有 2% 的成交量發生在標準時段之外，而那斯達克 100 期貨早就是 24×5 在跑了。
業界的疑慮集中在兩件事。一是夜盤流動性薄，買賣價差可能拉開，散戶在凌晨掛市價單會吃到什麼價格很難說，二是市場失去了「睡一覺再說」的緩衝，重大消息不用等開盤，可以在半夜直接變成賣單。
代幣化才是那斯達克的下一步
延長交易時間看起來像是在追加密市場的作息，但那斯達克真正在鋪的是另一條路。
SEC 已在 3 月 18 日批准那斯達克的代幣化證券交易提案，適用範圍涵蓋 Russell 1000 成分股，以及連結 S&P 500 和那斯達克 100 的 ETF。合格參與者可以選擇讓交易以區塊鏈代幣的形式結算，代幣與傳統股票共用同一組股票代號、同一個價格、同樣的股東權利。首批代幣化交易最快落在第三季底，前提是 DTC 完成系統更新。
那斯達克也和 Kraken 合作打造代幣化股票閘道，串接 xStocks 把鏈上鏈下的流動性接起來，目標 2027 上半年上線。
順序其實排得很清楚。先把結算從 T+2 壓到 T+1，再把交易時間拉到 23 小時，最後讓股票能以代幣形式結算。三步走完，「不打烊」就不只是延長營業時間，而是把底層整組換掉。
同一條賽道上不只那斯達克一家在跑：
- 紐約證交所 Arca: 同樣瞄準 12 月 6 日，週一至週四 1:30am 到 11:30pm、週五做到 8:00pm（美東時間）
- 24X National Exchange: 2024 年就拿到 SEC 批准做 23 小時交易，2026 下半年分階段上線
- Cboe: EDGX 推進 24×5，仍待批准
- 倫敦證券交易所: 計畫 2027 年初推出夜間交易
- SEC: 主席 Paul Atkins 將於 9 月 17 日在華盛頓辦 24 小時交易圓桌會議
台灣這邊也已經在動，主管機關 2026 年 1 月就通知券商提前因應複委託變革，目前全台有 37 家券商辦理複委託業務，現行下單模式多半配合美股開盤時段，或是開放特定的盤前預約，要承接夜盤等於整套系統重做。
常見問題
那斯達克 23 小時交易什麼時候上線？
那斯達克目標 2026 年 12 月 6 日上線，SEC 已於 4 月 10 日批准。日盤為美東時間凌晨 4 點至晚間 8 點，夜盤為晚間 9 點至隔日凌晨 4 點，中間留 1 小時做系統維護。
美股 23 小時交易對台灣投資人有什麼影響？
台灣投資人可在白天直接下單美股，不用熬夜盯盤。主管機關 2026 年 1 月已要求券商因應複委託變革，全台 37 家券商現行下單模式多配合美股開盤時段，需升級系統才能承接夜盤。

title: SK 海力士砸 384 億鎂新建兩廠！龍仁完工提前 12 年，但無塵室要等到 2029
summary:
SK 海力士董事會 8 月 7 日拍板兩座新廠，龍仁 Y2 投 35.2 兆韓元做 HBM 與次世代 DRAM […]

〈SK 海力士砸 384 億鎂新建兩廠！龍仁完工提前 12 年，但無塵室要等到 2029〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
SK 海力士董事會 8 月 7 日拍板兩座新廠，龍仁 Y2 投 35.2 兆韓元做 HBM 與次世代 DRAM、清州 M17 投 19.1 兆韓元做企業級 SSD 用的 NAND，合計約 54.3 兆韓元、384 億美元。這筆錢相當於它第二季末帳上現金的六成，也讓龍仁叢集第四座廠的完工時程從 2045 年一口氣拉到 2033 年。但兩座廠的第一間無塵室，要等到 2028 年底與 2029 年中才會開。
（前情提要：彭博：SK 海力士現金多到沒處放，狂掃韓國公司債成債市新莊家）
（背景補充：高盛上調三星電子目標價至 49 萬韓元，AI 記憶體供不應求至少延續到 2028 年）
重點摘要
- SK 海力士董事會核定 54.3 兆韓元（約 384 億美元）建兩座新廠，龍仁 Y2 佔 35.2 兆、清州 M17 佔 19.1 兆
- Y2 生產 HBM 與次世代 DRAM、M17 生產企業級 SSD 用的 NAND，龍仁叢集第四座廠完工時程從 2045 年提前到 2033 年
- M17 在 2027 年 2 月動工、Y2 在 2027 年 7 月動工，第一間無塵室分別要等到 2028 年 12 月與 2029 年 6 月才開
SK 海力士董事會週五（8/7）決議在韓國本土加蓋兩座記憶體廠，總投資約 54.3 兆韓元，換算約 384 億美元。其中 35.2 兆韓元砸在京畿道龍仁半導體叢集的 DRAM 廠「Y2」，19.1 兆韓元投入忠清北道清州的 NAND 廠「M17」。
官方的說法很直接：「這項投資是配合市場成長速度、為了抓住機會所做的決定。透過提前確保生產能力，我們的目標是成為 AI 基礎設施的關鍵夥伴。」
錢的去向給出答案
動區今天上午才報導，彭博披露 SK 海力士現金多到沒地方擺，今年掃進 10 兆到 40 兆韓元的韓國公司債，被當地信用市場分析師稱作「新莊家」，甚至為了管這筆錢專門開了職缺。當時留下的問題是，這家公司到底要拿這些錢做什麼。
幾個小時後，答案來了一半。截至第二季末，SK 海力士的現金與約當現金為 88 兆韓元，這次一口氣核定的 54.3 兆韓元，等於把帳上現金的六成押在兩座還沒動工的廠房上。
錢的來源也不難追。上個月它才靠美國存託憑證在美股掛牌，一次募得 265 億美元。今天宣布的投資規模是 384 億美元，比那次募到的還多出 119 億美元，等於掛牌拿到的錢全部投進去還不夠，其餘得靠自己賺的現金流補上。
龍仁完工提前 12 年
Y2 是龍仁半導體叢集規劃的四座廠中的第二座。這個位在龍仁市處仁區元三面、佔地 415 萬平方公尺的園區，分階段投入廠房與生產設備後，總投資預計會來到 600 兆韓元。第一座廠 2025 年 3 月動工，Y2 則排在 2027 年 7 月開工，2029 年 6 月開出第一間無塵室，生產 HBM 與次世代 DRAM。
真正的變化在時間表。加進 Y2 之後，龍仁叢集第四座廠的完工目標從原本的 2045 年拉到 2033 年，整整提前 12 年。一個二十年尺度的園區計畫直接砍掉一半工期，比起投資金額，這個數字更能說明 SK 海力士對 AI 記憶體需求的判斷有多急。
清州那邊也不小。M17 是 7 月初宣布的清州 100 兆韓元計畫的主角，當時規劃 80 兆投入 M17、20 兆投入先進封裝廠 P&T7，這次董事會先核定其中的 19.1 兆韓元，2027 年 2 月動工、2028 年 12 月開出第一間無塵室，投資期拉到 2031 年 4 月，Y2 則到 2031 年 10 月。
兩座廠的樓地板面積分別是 34.1 萬坪與 20.6 萬坪，加起來約 181 萬平方公尺，大約是 7 個大安森林公園的大小。
無塵室要等到 2029
值得注意的是產品分工。Y2 押在 HBM 與次世代 DRAM，M17 押在企業級 SSD 用的 NAND，兩邊都是這波 AI 伺服器最缺的東西。SK 海力士第二季財報裡，企業級 SSD 營收較上季翻倍，30TB 以上的大容量產品營收更成長超過兩倍，這次的產能配置基本上是照著財報數字下注。
但時間對不上。高盛本週稍早才說 AI 記憶體供不應求至少延續到 2028 年，而這兩座新廠的第一間無塵室要到 2028 年 12 月和 2029 年 6 月才開，開了之後還得裝機、試產、爬坡。換句話說，今天這筆 384 億美元解決的是 2029 年以後的產能，不是眼前的缺貨。
常見問題
這次的 54.3 兆韓元跟先前宣布的百兆級計畫是什麼關係？
這次是董事會針對兩座具體廠房核定的投資，屬於既有大計畫的執行部分。龍仁半導體叢集總投資預計 600 兆韓元、規劃四座廠，Y2 是第二座；清州計畫規模 100 兆韓元，其中 M17 分到 80 兆、先進封裝廠 P&T7 分到 20 兆，這次先核定 M17 的 19.1 兆韓元。
這兩座廠什麼時候會開始供貨？
M17 在 2027 年 2 月動工、2028 年 12 月開出第一間無塵室；Y2 在 2027 年 7 月動工、2029 年 6 月開出第一間無塵室。無塵室啟用之後還需要裝機與試產，實際量產貢獻會再往後。

title: Bitget Wallet 研究》過去 10 年，你為何沒變成有錢人？
summary:
過去十年你可能升了職、加了薪，購買力卻在原地踏步。本文把「2% 通膨目標」還原成一份沒人讀過、沒人簽字的合約： […]

〈Bitget Wallet 研究》過去 10 年，你為何沒變成有錢人？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
過去十年你可能升了職、加了薪，購買力卻在原地踏步。本文把「2% 通膨目標」還原成一份沒人讀過、沒人簽字的合約：從 1990 年紐西蘭的制度創新，到聯準會遲至 2012 年才首度書面承諾，再到 2022 年美國 CPI 衝上 9.1% 的失約現場，最後算出同一筆 10 萬元本金放在銀行、黃金與比特幣裡的十年落差。本文由 Bitget Wallet 研究院 Emily 撰文。
（前情提要：Bitget Wallet 研究》戰爭在美元帳戶發生，誕生在銀行之外）
（背景補充：現金回饋縮水別怕《 Bitget Wallet Card 推出「資產回饋」，消費最高返 3%）
重點摘要
- 2% 通膨目標源自 1990 年的紐西蘭，聯準會遲至 2012 年才首度以書面形式確立，是一項相當年輕的制度發明
- 複利下的 2%，十年累計物價上漲約 21.9%、購買力約 35 年腰斬，而 2022 年美國 CPI 峰值 9.1%、歐元區 HICP 峰值 10.6%，是目標的三到四倍
- 同一筆 10 萬元本金從 2015 年放到 2025 年，銀行存款變 12.19 萬元、黃金約 26 萬元、比特幣約 960 萬元
撰文：Emily，Bitget Wallet 研究員
貨幣每年貶值 2%，不是意外，也不是失誤，而是一項寫進政策目標的承諾。
序：一份無人知曉、無人簽字的合約
過去十年，你可能升了職，加了薪，學會更聰明地花錢，用信用卡的回饋規則，用各種「省錢」技巧把每一筆消費的邊際成本壓到最低。你做了所有「正確」的事。
但如果你把薪資單上的數字換算成十年前的購買力，你會發現一件很不舒服的事情：薪水在漲，帳戶餘額在漲，但你能買到的東西，像是同樣的房子頭期款、同樣一次家庭旅行、同樣一頓曾經覺得「貴一點但還能負擔」的晚餐，門檻卻在悄悄升高。
這不是錯覺，也不是你理財能力不足。這是一份合約的執行結果，一份你從未讀過、從未簽字、但每天都在履行義務的合約。合約的另一方是全球主要央行，條款很簡單：每年，你手裡的貨幣會貶值 2% 左右。這不是意外，也不是失誤，而是過去三十多年裡，全世界幾乎所有主要經濟體共同確立的政策目標。
問題是：如果我們從十年前就知道這份合約條款，並且選擇不用現金，而是用價值資產來履行「儲蓄」這個職能，今天的處境會有多大不同？這篇文章想認真算一次這筆帳。
2%，一份公開的「貶值承諾」
通膨不是故障，是設計
在大多數人的意識裡，通膨像是經濟這台機器偶爾犯的毛病，一種需要被「治癒」的失衡狀態。但過去三十年貨幣政策的實際演變，卻完全相反：全球主要央行逐漸把穩定的正通膨（約 2%）視為貨幣政策的重要目標。
這個轉折點要追溯到 1990 年的紐西蘭。當時的紐西蘭剛從 1970-80 年代的高通膨泥沼裡掙扎出來，《紐西蘭儲備銀行法》（Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989）確立了央行獨立性和通膨目標框架，紐西蘭 1990 年簽署的第一份《政策目標協議》（PTA，Policy Targets Agreement）將 CPI 通膨目標設定為 0–2%，紐西蘭因此常被視為「通膨目標制」的發源地。
這套框架此後被證明極具「傳染性」。加拿大、英國、瑞典等國在 1990 年代初相繼跟進。但真正讓「2%」這個數字成為全球貨幣政策預設語言的，是幾個更大經濟體後知後覺卻影響深遠的表態：
通膨目標制歷史時間線：從紐西蘭到全球共識「2%」 | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
- 聯準會在 2012 年 1 月首次以書面形式發布《長期目標與貨幣政策戰略聲明》（Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy），正式將 2%（以 PCE 價格指數衡量）確立為「長期」通膨目標，這是聯準會歷史上首次正式公布明確的長期通膨目標。值得注意的是，聯準會成立於 1913 年，卻在近百年之後才第一次把這個數字寫成正式聲明，足見「通膨目標」本身是一項相對年輕的制度發明，而不是貨幣政策與生俱來的屬性。
- 日本央行在 2013 年 1 月與政府發布聯合聲明，設定 2% 的「物價穩定目標」，作為「安倍經濟學」三支箭中貨幣政策這一支的核心錨點，目的是終結持續近二十年的通縮與低速成長。
- 歐洲央行在 2021 年 7 月完成貨幣政策戰略評估，將此前「低於但接近 2%」的模糊表述，修訂為更明確的「對稱的 2% 中期目標」，意味著通膨高於或低於 2% 同樣被視為偏離，而不是「越低越好」。
央行為什麼「不得不」這樣選擇
如果只看結果，「主動選擇讓貨幣每年貶值」聽起來像是一種失職。但從央行自身的政策邏輯看，這幾乎是一種無奈卻理性的選擇，背後有三層現實約束：
第一，規避通縮螺旋。通縮比溫和通膨更可怕的原因在於心理機制：如果人們預期明天的價格更低，最理性的選擇就是延後消費和投資，這會進一步壓低需求，導致價格繼續下跌，形成自我強化的螺旋。日本在 1990 年代到 2010 年代初的「失落的二十年」，常被作為這一邏輯最慘痛的案例研究對象。
第二，適應名目工資的僵固性。經濟學中一個反覆被驗證的現象是：企業極難直接下調員工的名目工資（哪怕是經營困難時期），因為這會帶來強烈的士氣打擊和法律、合約摩擦。但溫和通膨提供了一條「隱形」的調整通道，名目工資不變，實際購買力卻可以隨著通膨被悄悄下調，讓企業在不引發員工反彈的情況下完成實際薪酬的彈性調整。
第三，為降息保留政策空間。名目利率很難降到顯著低於零（即所謂的「零利率下限」問題）。如果目標通膨是 2%，那麼名目利率通常也會維持在一個正的水準上，這樣一旦經濟衰退來襲，央行還有「降息」這張牌可以打。如果長期目標通膨是 0%，名目利率可能常年徘徊在零附近，一旦危機發生，央行就沒有傳統的降息空間了。
複利的殘酷：2% 不是小數字
「每年 2%」聽起來溫和無害，但複利從不溫和。按照複利公式計算，2% 的年通膨率意味著：
- 10 年，累計物價上漲約 21.9%（即 1.02^10 ≈ 1.219），對應購買力下降約 18%。
- 35 年，按照「72 法則」的近似估算（72÷2=36），購買力大約每 35 年左右被攔腰砍去一半。也就是說，一個剛出社會的年輕人，在退休時會發現，同樣一筆數量的存款，購買力只剩下當年的一半左右。
複利的力量：2% 年通膨下的購買力侵蝕 | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
這就是「2%」這份合約真正的份量：它不是一次性的損失，而是一台持續運轉、永不停機的貶值機器。你今天存下的 1 萬元，在這台機器面前，不是「放在那裡不動」，而是「每天都在緩慢燃燒」。
未完成的履約：承諾與現實的巨大裂縫
如果央行真的能夠精確地把通膨控制在 2%，那麼「2%」至少是一份誠實的合約，你知道規則，可以據此規劃。但過去十年真正發生的事情，遠比「溫和的 2%」複雜和殘酷得多。
2020 年之後的全球通膨衝擊，是這個裂縫最直觀的體現。供應鏈紊亂、能源價格飆升、財政與貨幣政策的雙重寬鬆疊加，讓美國、歐元區等主要經濟體的實際通膨率在 2021-2023 年間大幅超越 2% 目標，美國 CPI 2022 年 6 月峰值通膨達到 9.1%，歐元區 HICP 2022 年 10 月峰值通膨達到 10.6%，達到目標水準的三到四倍。
即便到 2024-2025 年通膨有所回落，過去十年的累計通膨路徑，很可能也顯著偏離了「每年精確 2%」的理想曲線。這意味著，如果你完全按照「官方承諾的 2%」來規劃自己的儲蓄貶值速度，你幾乎肯定低估了實際的購買力損失。
而這還只是「溫和偏離」的例子。更極端的樣本，發生在那些貨幣信用本身出現結構性問題的經濟體：
- 日圓在過去十年經歷了歷史性的匯率潰敗。受日本央行長期維持超寬鬆貨幣政策、與聯準會升息循環形成巨大利差的影響，日圓兌美元匯率在 2022 年之後跌至數十年未見的低位。
- 土耳其里拉在過去十年的貶值幅度堪稱貨幣史上的極端案例：持續的高通膨、非常規的低利率政策組合，使里拉對美元的購買力出現斷崖式下跌。
- 阿根廷比索的故事則是另一版本的「法幣信用崩潰」：反覆的債務違約歷史、惡性通膨週期，使比索成為全球貨幣貶值案例研究中被引用最頻繁的樣本之一。
過去十年：日圓、土耳其里拉、阿根廷比索兌美元匯率走勢對比（2015-2025） | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
這些極端樣本提醒我們一件容易被忽視的事：「2%」從來不是一個被物理法則保證的數字，它只是一份政策承諾，而政策承諾的可信度，取決於執行這份承諾的機構本身的獨立性、紀律性，以及它所處的財政與政治環境。
承諾，但沒有擔保
這正是整套邏輯中最容易被忽視、卻最致命的一點：央行承諾了 2%，但這份承諾沒有任何擔保。
如果你把錢借給一家公司，你通常能拿到抵押品、優先償付順序，或者至少一份寫明違約後果的合約條款。但當你把畢生積蓄以本國貨幣的形式「存放」起來時，你和「發行這份貨幣的機構」之間，沒有抵押品，沒有違約金條款，更沒有任何法律意義上的追索權。如果實際通膨顯著偏離目標，無論是因為外部衝擊、政策失誤，還是財政壓力反過來迫使貨幣政策讓步，當貨幣貶值時，你沒有任何合約工具可以要求賠償。你唯一能做的，是承受。
這種不對稱，根源在於貨幣本身承擔的三種經典職能：記帳單位（unit of account）、交換媒介（medium of exchange）、價值儲藏（store of value），在法律強制力上存在天壤之別。
前兩項職能，幾乎是被制度強制綁定的：你的薪水必須以法定貨幣計價和發放，你的稅款必須以法定貨幣繳納，你的房貸、車貸等長期債務合約，幾乎全部以法定貨幣結算。這是現代經濟運轉的基礎設施，你無法退出，也幾乎沒有議價空間。
但「價值儲藏」這一項，從來不是被強制的。在絕大多數國家，法律並不要求個人必須以本幣現金作為長期儲蓄形式持有資產。你完全可以合法地把儲蓄換成黃金、股票、房產，或者其他任何你認為能更好保值的資產形式。
誰在「打包交給貨幣」？
答案不是因為貨幣適合「價值儲藏」，過去十年的數據已經反覆證明恰恰相反。而是因為把儲蓄從「本幣現金」切換到「其他資產」這件事，門檻太高了：
- 開一個證券帳戶、一個境外資產帳戶，涉及繁瑣的身分驗證與合規流程；
- 很多優質資產的最低投資門檻，把一般上班族擋在門外；
- 什麼時候買、買多少、要不要擇時，需要普通人不具備的專業認知；
- 更重要的是一種心理門檻，「存錢」這個動作，幾十年來已經被預設等同於「把錢放進銀行」，切換成「買資產」在直覺上會被誤認為是一種「投機」而非「儲蓄」。
這套操作與認知的雙重門檻，才是真正把絕大多數人鎖死在「用貶值中的貨幣做儲蓄」這條軌道上的隱形的牆。但這堵牆的代價，在過去十年裡被無限放大了。
三類人的三種命運
理論說到這裡，該看真實的數字了。過去十年，不同的「儲蓄載體選擇」帶來的結果差異，已經不是「跑贏通膨」或「跑輸通膨」這種量級的差距，而是改變命運級別的分野。
十年鏡像：硬資產漲幅 vs 法幣購買力走勢 | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
假設時間回到 2015 年。你手裡有 10 萬元，不做任何交易，不做任何擇時，只做一個動作：買入一種資產，然後一直持有到 2025 年。十年後，這 10 萬元的大致結果會是什麼？
十年鏡像：10 萬元本金，七種儲蓄方式的真實結果 | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
很多人過去十年做的選擇，其實就是把錢留在銀行，獲得穩定的名目收益。問題在於，同一時期美國累計通膨約 30%，日本累計通膨也明顯高於長期平均水準。也就是說，10 萬元變成 12.19 萬元，看起來賺了 2.19 萬元，但真正增加的購買力可能非常有限。
這就是過去十年最容易被忽視的事實：財富成長，不僅取決於你賺了多少錢，更取決於你把錢放在了什麼地方。拉開差距的，往往不是交易能力，而是儲蓄載體。
把這兩組數據放在一起看，會得到一個遠比「通膨很討厭」更尖銳的結論：過去十年，聰明的資金早已經把「交換」和「儲藏」這兩項貨幣職能徹底脫鉤了。
三類人的十年命運
如果把這些數字翻譯成三種真實的人生選擇，大致可以描繪出這樣三條軌跡：
A 類人：法幣理財者。他們勤懇、謹慎、不冒險，把辛苦賺來的錢存進銀行定存，或者買入銀行管道推薦的「穩健型」貨幣型基金理財商品。十年下來，帳戶裡的數字確實在緩慢成長，名目報酬率看起來「跑贏」了活期存款。但如果按實際購買力折算，他們十年的辛苦積累，很大程度上只是勉強抵消了通膨侵蝕，甚至在通膨超預期的年份出現實際購買力的淨損失。他們沒有做錯任何「傳統意義上正確」的事，卻依然是這場十年遊戲裡過得最辛苦的一群人。
B 類人：資產玩家。他們做的事情，本質上極其簡單，把手裡閒置的法幣流動性，儘快轉化成黃金、優質股票、比特幣等硬資產，並長期持有，不做頻繁的擇時交易。這群人未必是專業投資者，很多只是恰好「懶得管」，買入後就沒有再動。但正是這種「懶惰」，讓他們充分享受了過去十年全球資產價格擴張週期帶來的巨大溢價。
C 類人：山寨幣投機者。這是最容易被忽視，卻同樣重要的一類樣本，他們同樣試圖「逃離法幣貶值」，但選擇的載體是缺乏基本價值支撐、純粹依賴敘事和流動性驅動的山寨幣。過去十年，絕大多數山寨幣的命運是歸零，或者接近歸零。這組樣本的意義在於提醒我們：「逃離法幣」這個方向本身是理性的，但「逃向哪裡」的選擇，同樣至關重要。不是所有的「非法幣資產」都天然具有保值屬性，資產本身的稀缺性、共識強度和真實需求，才是決定其能否穿越週期的核心。
最誠實的信號：央行自己在買什麼？
這裡有一個幾乎堪稱「降維打擊」的觀察角度：你不需要相信任何一位分析師、任何一份投研報告，你只需要看央行自己的資產負債表在過去幾年做了什麼。
全球央行的官方外匯存底管理機構，在過去幾年以歷史級別的規模持續增持黃金儲備。據世界黃金協會（World Gold Council）的報告，2025 年黃金價格多次刷新歷史最高紀錄，全球央行的黃金購買總量也達到了極為可觀的規模。
全球央行年度淨購金量（2015-2025），2022 年起連四年維持高位 | 圖表來源：Bitget Wallet 研究院
這個現象本身，比任何理論推演都更有說服力，央行不是不知道法幣在「儲藏」這項職能上的天然缺陷，它們比任何人都清楚。它們只是沒有，也不需要，把這份認知告訴每一個普通存戶。
從暴跌走向資產積累：加密如何承諾
在加密世界過去幾年的實踐中，其實也能看到這條演化路徑。以 U 卡回饋為例，大多數項目向用戶承諾高回饋比例，卻遮掩了代幣最終將暴跌的命運：
- 法幣、穩定幣回饋：消費 → 消耗法幣 → 剩餘的法幣躺在帳戶裡，不漲反貶。你的每一次消費，都在無形中讓你的儲蓄基數繼續被通膨侵蝕，你什麼都沒有「賺到」，只是完成了一次純粹的價值消耗。
- 代幣回饋：消費 → 消耗穩定幣 → 商家或平台返還山寨幣作為「獎勵」。這個模式表面上引入了「回饋」的激勵結構，但如果返還的資產本身缺乏真實的稀缺性與需求支撐，這份「回饋」極可能會在時間維度上被稀釋到歸零，本質上只是換了一種包裝的價值損耗。
但 RWA 與代幣化美股給了加密另一個選擇。以往，真正被全世界認可的加密資產只有 BTC，但美股、真實世界資產上鏈改變了一切。譬如，如果我們採用資產回饋（Assetback）方式，給用戶返還的是真正具有長期價值支撐的硬資產，則能讓用戶與價值資產的積累綁定起來。
這就是本文想要論證的最終結論，也是它唯一想要落地的應用場景：我們無法改變央行設定 2% 通膨目標的進程，也無法改變這份承諾沒有擔保這一事實。但我們完全可以改變的，是當法幣從我們手中流出的那一刻，由什麼資產來接住它。這或許是普通人在這場持續了三十多年、且沒有任何跡象會終止的「2% 遊戲」裡，能夠找到的最樸素，卻最有效的因應方式。
常見問題
央行為什麼要刻意讓貨幣每年貶值 2%？
三個現實理由：一是規避通縮螺旋，避免民眾預期價格下跌而延後消費；二是名目工資難以下調，溫和通膨提供了實際薪酬的隱形調整通道；三是保留降息空間，若目標通膨是 0%，名目利率會常年貼近零，衰退來襲時央行沒有牌可打。
2% 通膨目標是什麼時候變成全球共識的？
1990 年紐西蘭簽署第一份《政策目標協議》，把 CPI 目標設在 0-2%，是通膨目標制的起點。加拿大、英國、瑞典在 1990 年代初跟進，聯準會遲至 2012 年 1 月才首度書面確立 2%（PCE 口徑），日本央行 2013 年 1 月跟上，歐洲央行則在 2021 年 7 月改為「對稱的 2% 中期目標」。

title: 幣託揭加密詐騙陷阱，熟齡族「高資產、長沉睡」成詐團目標！
summary:
幣託集團（BitoGroup）連續第三年進駐「高齡健康產業博覽會」，是唯一參展的虛擬資產業者。幣託分析近半年受 […]

〈幣託揭加密詐騙陷阱，熟齡族「高資產、長沉睡」成詐團目標！〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
幣託集團（BitoGroup）連續第三年進駐「高齡健康產業博覽會」，是唯一參展的虛擬資產業者。幣託分析近半年受騙個案，歸納出鎖定熟齡族的假信貸、假交友與二次詐騙三大手法，並指出 55 歲以上族群呈現「高資產、長沉睡」特性，沉睡帳戶一旦突然活躍，高機率已落入詐騙陷阱。
（前情提要：破解虛擬資產「二次詐騙」！幣託攜手刑事局、水丰刀公私協力傳授防禦心法）
（背景補充：防詐》幣託攜手 Whoscall 啟動虛擬貨幣查證防護，建構雙層防護網）
重點摘要
- 幣託集團連續第三年進駐「高齡健康產業博覽會」，是唯一參展的虛擬資產業者，8 月 7 至 9 日於台北世貿一館攤位設有反詐互動關卡。
- 幣託分析近半年受騙個案，歸納出鎖定熟齡族的三大詐騙手法：假信貸與信用評估陷阱、假交友與假投資勒索、假冒專家的二次詐騙。
- 55 歲以上族群呈現「高資產、長沉睡」特徵，普遍持有比特幣等主流資產但鮮少交易，沉睡帳戶一旦突然異常活躍，高機率已落入詐騙陷阱。
＊本文為新聞稿，由 BitoGroup 撰寫並提供。
台灣知名虛擬資產業者幣託集團（BitoGroup）連續第三年進駐「高齡健康產業博覽會」，幣託身為唯一參展的虛擬資產業者，聚焦高齡防詐議題。據分析，55 歲以上的族群呈現「高資產、長沉睡」特性，極易成為詐騙集團的目標。為提升熟齡族群「識詐」能力，幣託舉辦線上活動「防詐大會考」抽萬元加密貨幣盲盒，8 月 7 至 9 日展期間攤位設有反詐互動關卡，抽千元黃金幣盲盒金磚、《Whoscall 進階版》兌換代碼，將防詐知識融入日常生活。
圖一：幣託集團（BitoGroup）連續第三年進駐「高齡健康產業博覽會」，身為唯一參展的虛擬資產業者，聚焦高齡防詐議題。｜圖片來源：幣託集團
幣託集團創辦人暨執行長鄭光泰表示：「積極防詐是幣託的首要任務與企業責任，我們透過科技防禦與跨域聯防已發揮顯著的阻斷效果；許多詐騙案件的根本原因在於，受害者落入非法平台與非託管錢包的陷阱。幣託將持續落實金融友善與防詐防線，陪伴熟齡族群安心邁入數位金融時代。」
拆解熟齡詐騙三大陷阱：假信貸、假交友與二次詐騙
針對熟齡詐騙型態，幣託大規模分析近半年受騙個案，歸納出鎖定熟齡族的三大典型詐騙手法。首先是假信貸與信用評估陷阱，詐騙集團利用受害人資金週轉或理財需求，冒用合法金融機構名義提供帳密引導開立加密貨幣帳戶，並要求購買 USDT 作為信用評估資產，實質騙取帳戶作為人頭戶。其次為假交友與假投資勒索，詐騙集團花費數月培養感情建立信任，誘使受害人將資金轉移至假交易所，當欲取回本金時，假客服即以帳戶風控、補繳稅金、滯納金或網路轉換費進行資金勒索。最後則是假冒專家之二次詐騙，已經歷詐騙的受害者在網路尋求救助時，宣稱能憑技術追回鏈上資產的假律師或假反詐組織便趁虛而入，利用受害者急於尋回本金的心態進行二次敲詐。
數據揭密高資產沉睡用戶，突發操作成防護重點
進一步分析詐騙個案與其行為，幣託發現 55 歲以上的熟齡族群呈現「高資產、長沉睡」的特徵，他們普遍持有比特幣等主流資產，但平時鮮少交易；一旦沉睡帳戶突然異常活躍，高機率已落入詐騙陷阱。由於高齡者對鏈上操作與錢包運作機制較不熟悉，一旦資金轉出至假平台，挽回難度極高，凸顯熟齡金融識詐以及主動防護的重要性。
為持續深化熟齡族群資產防護，幣託從兩大面向建構防護網，在「科技防禦」層面，平台提供通行密鑰（Passkey）、雙重驗證（2FA）與防釣魚碼等工具提升帳號強度，並導入嚴謹的身份驗證機制，部署可疑交易監控系統主動偵測異常行為，串連銀行與檢警調的跨域聯防機制，並由客服團隊主動關懷高風險用戶。
在金融識讀層面，除了定期舉辦防詐講座與案例宣導外，幣託推出線上活動「防詐大會考」，引導會員完成平台安全設定、抽「萬元加密貨幣盲盒」，更串連多位具影響力的幣圈專家分享防詐經驗。高齡展現場則有寓教於樂的互動體驗，包含「防詐答題開箱黃金幣盲盒」、「追蹤社群領 BTC 典藏金幣組」。為從源頭及早阻斷詐騙接觸路徑，幣託持續與 Gogolook 旗下數位防詐 App Whoscall 合作，於展期間舉辦「一分鐘測驗《Whoscall 進階版》兌換代碼」，期盼將防詐知識落實於日常生活中，升級大眾的防詐免疫力！
圖二：為提升熟齡族群「識詐」能力，幣託於高齡展期間攤位設有反詐互動關卡，抽千元黃金幣盲盒金磚、《Whoscall 進階版》兌換代碼等好禮。｜圖片來源：幣託集團

幣託反詐線上活動
防詐大會考，抽萬元加密貨幣盲盒，參加請點：https://bitogroup.info/BW3Bk
關於幣託
幣託集團（BitoGroup）成立於 2014 年，致力於用最簡單的方式讓區塊鏈進入每個人的日常生活，並協助企業與消費者進入 Web3 時代。幣託運用區塊鏈和高頻交易技術，積極打造創新的企業級虛擬資產核心品牌「Bito.Enterprise」，包括穩定幣結算、點數換加密貨幣及加密貨幣支付。BitoPro 加密貨幣交易所已完成金管會「提供虛擬資產服務之事業或人員洗錢防制登記」，提供加密貨幣錢包和交易服務，亦支援法幣出入金、超商購買或點數換加密貨幣。官方網站：https://www.bitopro.com
常見問題
幣託歸納出鎖定熟齡族的加密詐騙有哪三種手法？
第一是假信貸與信用評估陷阱，冒用合法金融機構名義引導開戶並要求買 USDT 作為信用評估資產，實際上是騙取人頭戶；第二是假交友與假投資勒索，培養感情後誘導資金轉入假交易所，提領時再以風控、補稅、滯納金名義勒索；第三是假冒律師或反詐組織的二次詐騙，鎖定已受害且急於追回資產的人再敲詐一次。
為什麼 55 歲以上族群容易成為加密詐騙目標？
幣託分析指出，這個族群呈現「高資產、長沉睡」特徵，普遍持有比特幣等主流資產但平時鮮少交易，且對鏈上操作與錢包機制較不熟悉。一旦沉睡帳戶突然異常活躍，高機率已落入詐騙陷阱，而資金轉出至假平台後挽回難度極高。

title: 買盤狂湧 20 億美元卻漲不動？分析師：比特幣衝破 6.5 萬美元才能翻盤
summary:
巨鯨、大型持幣者近期持續加碼，短短數日累計買進超過 2 萬枚比特幣，價值約 12 億美元；與此同時，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 本周也吸引超過 7.5 億美元資金流入，顯示機構需求正逐步回溫，在一定程度上抵銷了《 CLARITY 法案 》延宕所帶來的失望賣壓。

〈買盤狂湧 20 億美元卻漲不動？分析師：比特幣衝破 6.5 萬美元才能翻盤〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
比特幣市場正出現新買盤訊號。鏈上數據顯示，巨鯨、大型持幣者近期持續加碼，短短數日累計買進超過 2 萬枚比特幣，價值約 12 億美元；與此同時，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 本周也吸引超過 7.5 億美元資金流入，顯示機構需求正逐步回溫，在一定程度上抵銷了 《CLARITY 法案》延宕所帶來的失望賣壓。
根據區塊鏈分析平台 Santiment 追蹤數據，持有 10 至 1 萬比特幣的「巨鯨與鯊魚級地址」，自 7 月 29 日以來已吸收超過 2 萬枚比特幣，以目前價格計算約值 12 億美元。
值得注意的是，這些大額買盤高度集中在比特幣跌破 6.5 萬美元後的震盪盤整區間。 Santiment 在社群平台 X 發文指出：
隨著大戶持續吸籌、散戶在恐慌中拋售，在這種籌碼換手的格局下，比特幣未來突破 7 萬美元的機率，已遠高於跌破 6 萬美元的可能性。
小額持幣者信心降溫，巨鯨逆勢布局
究其原因，Santiment 解釋，近期散戶之所以心灰意冷、紛紛下車，主要受到 3 大負面因素夾擊：首先是 7 月 30 日爆發的冷錢包 Coldcard 駭客事件，導致多達 1.2 億美元的比特幣遭竊；其次是《CLARITY 法案》闖關失敗帶來的不確定性；最後則是近期沉悶的幣價走勢，徹底消磨了小額投資人的耐心。
不過，從鏈上數據來看，市場籌碼正在逐漸向長期持有者集中。
比特幣 ETF 單周吸金 7.5 億美元，機構買盤重新回流
除了鏈上活動升溫，美國現貨比特幣 ETF 的資金流向也顯示機構需求正在復甦。
根據 SoSoValue 數據，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 本周累計流入 7.5469 億美元，有望創下自今年 4 月以來最佳單周表現。
加密貨幣平台 Nexo 分析師 Liya Kalchev 表示，市場最明顯的變化來自「機構資金的動向」。她指出，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 8 月至今已吸引超過 5 億美元資金流入，且資金流入速度在本周持續升溫。其中，僅周三單日就吸金超過 2.4 億美元，與 6 月 ETF 創下史上最差單月表現形成鮮明對比。
買盤回歸但價格未突破，市場等待 6.5 萬美元關鍵壓力
然而，令市場困惑的現象在於，儘管巨鯨大戶、 ETF 聯手掃貨，比特幣價格卻遲遲未見明顯突破行情。
Liya Kalchev 認為，這反而透露出目前進場買家的特徵。她表示：
資金回流卻未能有效推升幣價，這件事本身就極具參考價值，部分交易機構認為，目前新增買盤較偏向短線策略性布局，而非基於長期信念的大規模進場。
她指出，比特幣若要重新建立多頭趨勢，仍需要有效突破並站穩 6.5 萬美元大關，才能真正穩住陣腳。
技術面存在反彈空間，《CLARITY 法案》成市場最大變數
從技術分析來看，比特幣價格型態仍顯示進一步反彈的可能性。不過，美國參議院本月無法完成《CLARITY 法案》表決，成為市場短期最大阻力。
《CLARITY 法案》被視為美國建立加密貨幣市場監管框架的重要立法之一，市場期待法案通過後，能進一步降低監管不確定性，吸引更多機構資金進入數位資產市場。

title: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
summary: The BBC has seen evidence from previous cases that Russian-linked proxies not only handled drones and explosives, but also delivered them to Germany.
full_text:
German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
- Published
As Germany investigates how a drone loaded with explosives reached a runway at Leipzig airport, there is renewed talk in Europe of hybrid war.
The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers".
There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form.
The BBC has seen details of the investigation into a plot in 2024 in which Russian-linked proxies in Poland and Lithuania not only handled drones and explosives but also delivered them to Germany.
The flying bomb
The quadcopter was discovered at Leipzig airport late on Tuesday night, forcing one runway into lockdown as a bomb disposal robot rolled into action.
On the tarmac close by were several Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes, stripes along their enormous bodies in the blue and yellow of the country's flag. One reads, "Be Brave Like Kherson", the southern city now on the frontline of Russia's invasion.
Pictures published by German media suggest the drone was a relatively small device which airport staff spotted "floating" between the Ukrainian planes.
Around the same time, a DHL cargo plane collided with an "unidentified object" as it pulled up into the sky, unable to land in Leipzig.
Teams are still working to establish whether that was a second drone.
They are also trying to trace who launched the devices and why.
A previous plot
A previous Russian-backed plot involving Leipzig airport could provide clues.
In 2024, a parcel containing a sophisticated incendiary device caught fire at the airport's DHL hub shortly before it was loaded onto a plane. Similar packages then ignited in the UK and Poland, causing extensive damage.
A group of men are currently on trial in both Lithuania and Poland, where prosecutors believe they were part of a substantial network of proxies recruited by Russian military intelligence.
But there was a subplot that has been little discussed before.
Last September, Lithuanian prosecutors said that investigators had also seized RDX explosives meant for "other terrorist attacks". The amount was significant: equivalent to 6kg of TNT.
"Some of the devices were manufactured to intensify the blast," the prosecutor added.
The BBC has since had access to case documents that describe how several of the men on trial were paid to transport those explosives around Europe, concealed in cans of sweetcorn and chopped tomatoes. The detonators were hidden inside headphone sets.
The suspects also handled drone parts and the case talks specifically of attachments, suitable for holding a bomb.
Prosecutors allege that some of the items were brought into the EU from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.
Almost two dozen suspects have been charged with terror offences, but with the men's handlers still at large, believed to be in Russia, it is not clear whether the entire network was disbanded or all the hidden material found.
While there is no evidence of a link to the Leipzig drone bomb, the 2024 plot certainly highlights the potential.
Vladyslav's story
One of the suspects charged in Poland, a Ukrainian called Vladyslav D., described in detail to investigators how he made multiple long car trips in July 2024 following instructions from someone he knew as "Warrior".
He has since pleaded not guilty in court.
One message sent him to the edge of a Lithuanian forest where he found a carrier bag containing "three or four packs of headphones", soggy with rain.
He had already collected two cans of corn "lightly covered with soil" from another location, telling investigators he had no idea what was inside.
He was ordered to leave the headphones many hours' drive away in Poland where he noticed "a guy on a bicycle" collect them from beside the road.
For another assignment he received a pin for a location inside a Lithuanian cemetery and was told to dig beneath some plastic flowers. He quickly uncovered a bin bag wrapped in brown tape.
"Inside were drone components: small plastic propellers, I think four pieces," Vladyslav told investigators.
These items were to be left by a road in central Poland for pick-up.
Finally there was a trip to Germany where he was given the code to access a hostel room in Dusseldorf. He was instructed to leave the drones and other items inside.
The intended targets were never revealed.
Moscow's motive?
In statements to investigators, Vladyslav D. said he was paid more than $2,000 (£1,487) in cryptocurrency for his efforts. His motive was clear.
And what about the Leipzig case?
Few details about the drone bomb are yet public.
Some German sources report that the explosive was Semtex, which contains RDX - the explosive found in the food cans in a Lithuanian cemetery.
We do not know how much the drone found at the airport was carrying and the physical damage may have been limited.
"The drone casing, if it was metal, might have put a hole in the plane but just a blast wave probably would just have dented it unless they put some fragmentation inside," explosives expert Professor Jackie Akhavan of Cranfield University explained.
But if Russia was behind this, its aim was more likely to sow fear.
Andrei Soldatov, an expert on Russia's intelligence agencies, said it "makes sense" to suspect Moscow, pointing to a clear pattern of sabotage and hostile activity, from arson attacks on facilities supporting Ukraine to drones over sensitive sites in Europe.
Germany is one of Kyiv's biggest suppliers of military aid.
"It's a message. You get something like that [bomb] into one of the biggest European airports and you send the message that, 'Guys, we can do that. Remember'," Soldatov explained.
"You hint to the adversary that you might cause a really big problem: that tomorrow might be more serious."
And the potential motive? Moscow is under intense pressure from Ukraine's long-scale drone attacks, he said, and the fact that Russian President Vladimir Putin "has been humiliated, repeatedly".
International response
"We are aware of the incident, which the German authorities continue to investigate," a Nato official told the BBC.
Antonov Airlines has also been cautious so far in its response.
The firm supplies planes for certain Nato operations but declined to say whether that includes military support for Ukraine.
Asked whether the Ukrainian planes might have been targeted, a spokeswoman in Kyiv told the BBC: "We are not making any such assumptions…We don't know what this drone was or why it was there."
But Russia watchers are clear.
"This is Russian interference," said John Lough of the New Eurasian Strategies (NEST) Centre. "It's all part of undermining support for Ukraine by pointing to the dangers of escalation and, frankly, scaring the German authorities."
He sees high potential for a surge in such hybrid attacks now because Ukraine has "changed the balance" of the war.
"My expectation is that such activity will increase quite sharply over the coming months. I think it's a dangerous moment."

title: Divers find 162-year-old Guinness in shipwreck off the English coast
summary: Samples from the bottle have been sent for analysis, with researchers hoping to learn more about what the stout would have tasted like.
full_text:
Divers find 162-year-old Guinness in shipwreck off the English coast
- Published
How far would you travel for a pint of Guinness? If the answer is to the bottom of the sea, you might be in luck.
There's just one catch - the pint in question is 162 years old.
When Belgian underwater photographer Stefan Panis discovered a bottle buried in a shipwreck off the coast of Dover in 2025, he had no idea what he had found. He just knew something about it had caught his eye.
When Panis and his friend, Eddie Huzzey, surfaced, a quick rinse revealed the familiar Guinness branding. The bottle dates back to 1864.
"We lifted the artefact, and then on the surface a quick rinse revealed 'Guinness'," he said.
Panis, who has been diving for more than 40 years, contacted Guinness to share the discovery.
So far, he has recovered just one bottle, but believes many more remain buried beneath the sand surrounding the wreck and he already has plans to recover more when conditions allow.
"Seeing the size of the case, I think it is definitely a case of 24 bottles.
"But there might be more cases."
After the discovery, Panis' colleague Pawel Truszynski contacted a microbiologist specialising in beer at KU Leuven University in Belgium.
Samples from the bottle have been sent for analysis, with researchers hoping to learn more about what the stout would have tasted like.
"There is always a chance that we can recover the complete DNA, and then we can do a small re-brew of the exact beer that was found in the 1860s," Panis said.
If successful, researchers could recreate the taste of Guinness as it was brewed in 1864 using samples of the recovered stout.
But there may be an even more intriguing possibility.
"There is a possibility that it's still drinkable. The question is if the sea water has come into the bottles through the corks.
"If not, most likely the beer would still be drinkable."
And although Panis admitted he is "not that big" of a Guinness fan, he didn't hesitate when asked whether he would try the 162-year-old stout if experts declared it safe.
"Of course."
'I would try it even though I don't like Guinness'
For some people in Belfast, the novelty of drinking a pint that's spent more than 160 years at the bottom of the sea was reason enough to give it a go.
Fraser Hill, Katie Wilkinson and Katie White all said curiosity would outweigh any hesitation if they were offered a taste of the recovered Guinness.
"I would try it even though I don't even like Guinness," Katie White said.
Others also needed very little convincing.
Matt McCoppin said he would try the stout "in a heartbeat", while Natalia Nowacka admitted she would be nervous, but still couldn't resist the opportunity.
"I wouldn't know what to expect, I'd be quite scared," Natalia said.
Noë Vernet also said the chance to taste such a historic drink was too good to miss.
"For the sheer experience, I would try it," he said.
Not everyone was tempted, however.
Margaret Barr said she would much rather enjoy a pint of Guinness fresh from the tap than one recovered from the seabed.
"Absolutely not," she said. "I'm a big Guinness drinker, I'm just not a risk taker."
Andrew Clarke, meanwhile, said safety advice would not keep him waiting.
He joked the Guinness would be "halfway down me" before experts had the chance to declare whether it was safe to drink.
"I don't think it would age like a fine wine, but for the sake of mankind someone needs to drink it," he said.
"Maybe put a few more down there and see what happens 200 years from now."
A spokesperson for Diageo said: "Discoveries like this provide a fascinating window into our past and help build a deeper understanding of our heritage.
"Currently, our Guinness Archive team is liaising with the divers to gather more information and evaluate the find."

title: Mexico break ranks to join Argentina in backing Infantino
summary: Mexico goes against its regional governing body Concacaf to publicly support under-fire Fifa president Gianni Infantino.
full_text:
Mexico break ranks to join Argentina in backing Infantino
- Published
The Mexican Football Federation has broken ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to come out in support of under-fire Fifa president Gianni Infantino.
Concacaf, which runs football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency after he aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
However, 2026 World Cup co-hosts Mexico have backed Infantino's leadership amid widespread calls for him to resign.
"The FMF [Mexican FA] supports president Infantino's leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening," a statement read.
It echoed a statement from Conmebol - South America's governing body - in saying it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 Fifa members.
"The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made by president Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations," it added.
- Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support 
  - Published7 hours ago
- Infantino sorry for errors but stays Fifa president 
  - Published1 day ago
- If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president? 
  - Published3 days ago
However, Conmebol did "express its concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or the institutional mechanisms provided for dealing with this type of situation".
Meanwhile, the football association of 2026 World Cup runners-up Argentina praised Infantino for recognising and apologising for his "errors".
It described his decade-long tenure as Fifa president as "centred on the development of soccer worldwide and institutional strength based on a clear, stable, and transparent governance model".
Infantino is unanimously backed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), but faces opposition from European football's governing Uefa and Concacaf.
European teams could still boycott the World Cup as Uefa said its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino's plan being aborted.
"Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again," a Uefa statement read.
"These conditions have not been met."
Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a "shabby, back room, opaque deal".
The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino, while Wales, Albania and Croatia are among other individual associations to have turned their back on the 56-year-old.
Concacaf described Infantino's proposal as "a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first", and that "this recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour".
However, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president.
Before Infantino withdrew his proposal, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood "in solidarity" with Uefa and Concacaf in opposition to the plans.
Infantino had offered all associations $40m (£30m) if they backed a proposal for private investment in its tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups, through the FFE subsidiary.
During a meeting of Fifa executives in Morocco on Wednesday, the world governing body said "mistakes" regarding FFE were "acknowledged", saying it was "not the intention" for the Fifa Council and members association to "feel excluded from the process and that the process should have been handled differently".
Uefa's statement in response added: "Uefa made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.
"Yesterday's announcement that some people employed by the Fifa president (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."
Fifa has been approached for comment.

title: Norrie saves match point in superb Montreal fightback
summary: Britain's Cameron Norrie saves a match point as he produces a superb fightback to beat world number seven Alex de Minaur at the Canadian Open.
full_text:
Norrie saves match point in superb Montreal fightback
- Published
Britain's Cameron Norrie saved a match point as he produced a superb fightback to beat world number seven Alex de Minaur at the Canadian Open.
Norrie was a set and 5-2 down against the Australian third seed before coming through 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1 to reach the fourth round.
De Minaur, leading by a double-break, had a match point on his own serve in the second set but double-faulted.
He twice served for the match but, at 5-4 up, double-faulted again to put the set back on level terms.
World number 37 Norrie edged the tie-break and then ran away with the deciding set to complete victory in two hours and 52 minutes.
"It was a great match to win and to test my level, and I can take so much confidence from this one," the 30-year-old said.
"The level was so high the first two sets.
"From the beginning, [de Minaur] came out firing and I had to match it."
Norrie - who reached the Los Cabos semi-finals last week - will face France's Arthur Fils for a place in the quarter-finals.
De Minaur's exit means that fifth seed Ben Shelton is the only top-10 men's player remaining in Montreal.
World number one Jannik Sinner and third-ranked Novak Djokovic withdrew before the tournament began, while top seed Alexander Zverev lost his first match.
Sixth-ranked Daniil Medvedev, seventh seed Taylor Fritz and world number nine Flavio Cobolli also all lost in the second round.

title: Caldentey embraces 'cool' pressure as Arsenal target Treble
summary: Midfielder Mariona Caldentey explains why Arsenal, strengthened by seven new players, are talking up their chances of winning the Treble this season.
full_text:
Caldentey embraces 'cool' pressure as Arsenal target Treble
- Published
Mariona Caldentey has won four Champions Leagues, six Spanish titles, six Spanish Cups, a European Championship and a World Cup - but her eyes light up when discussing Arsenal's hopes of silverware in the upcoming 2026-27 season.
With the Gunners chasing a first Women's Super League title since 2019, along with two domestic cups and another Champions League, she is explicit about what she expects.
"We have to do it - now it has to be our time."
The last time Caldentey, 30, was spotted in an Arsenal shirt was in May, standing on an open-top bus as part of the men's and women's victory parade around north London.
Hundreds of thousands of supporters lined the streets to celebrate a first Premier League title in 22 years for the men, with Caldentey and her team-mates also showing off the inaugural Women's Champions Cup they won against Brazilian side Corinthians in February.
It was a prize to cherish last season but, having finished second in the WSL and had their Champions League defence ended by an 87th-minute Lyon winner in their semi-final second leg, the Spain midfielder wants to put things right this season.
"We need to take the next step and are ready for it," she said. "We need to be ambitious, have no fear and believe in ourselves.
"That does not mean we are going to win it - there are other things that we cannot control, but that's the message.
"We are professional athletes at a big club and we have to deal with pressure. We accept it and I think it's a cool part of the job."
Why fast start crucial to Arsenal's title chances
Boss Renee Slegers is equally bullish about Arsenal's targets for this season and is expecting her players to deliver.
"We are in a really good place," she told the Women's Football Weekly podcast. "We need to be bold and explicit - we want to win the Women's Super League, and, of course, the Treble."
Last season, Arsenal won only four of their first nine games. By contrast, eventual champions Manchester City recovered from losing their opening match at Chelsea to rattle off 13 straight wins and seize control of the title race.
Replicating such a start will leave Arsenal's dreams of a first WSL title in eight seasons in tatters - and it could not be much tougher, with early trips to Stamford Bridge and Etihad Stadium.
They also travel to Brighton where they lost in the FA Cup quarter-finals in April and who, a month later, held them 1-1 to guarantee City the title.
However, after the novelty of a full pre-season, Slegers is confident of a faster start this time.
"Some players haven't had that since 2017, 2018, and you can see that," she said. "They come back with so much energy, so much excitement.
"I think honestly they've been decompressing, recharging. Sometimes you understand what you're missing when it's not there. I think that's what the players have gone through so you can really feel the excitement to do something."
Why Arsenal feel they are 'ready'
This summer, Slegers has strengthened her hand with seven new players, including full-back Ona Batlle, Caldentey's compatriot, and England dynamo Georgia Stanway to stiffen midfield.
Caldentey says Arsenal came up short last season through inconsistency and hopes the signings will help overcome that hurdle.
"We have shown amazing moments and amazing games and others where we haven't been good enough," she said. "That happened too many times last year. It was painful.
"We have added a lot of quality and that will help us."
With players such as two-time Ballon d'Or winner and fellow Spaniard Alexia Putellas arriving in the WSL, down the road at London City Lionesses, Caldentey accepts the league is getting tougher.
"It is a really attractive league," she said. "What you see and experience here, you don't get in other places. There are never any easy games.
"You want to play against the best - that's the challenge as a player and the quality here is really high."
And any observer would count Caldentey as among the very best.
In two seasons at Emirates Stadium, she has won WSL Player of the Season, come second in the 2024-25 Ballon d'Or and made the WSL Team of the Year both times.
During that period, her role has evolved from forward to midfielder and yet, despite that, only Alessia Russo has scored and assisted more for Arsenal.
"You have to adapt to what the team needs," she said. "Last year, I played a different role, closer to our defensive line. I was not used to it but these things make you grow.
"I do things better now than a year ago. Of course I enjoy playing higher up where you can be more creative and more risky but whatever my coach or team needs, I'll do it."
Her manager has stated clearly her team needs trophies. Caldentey is steeling herself to deliver.
